records.requirement: The system shall keep `NaruServe-api` free of any dependency on or bytecode reference to SLF4J (`org.slf4j`) or `android.*`, with the SLF4J adapter in `NaruServe-slf4j`, the rotating file logger in `NaruServe-filelog` and the Logcat logger in `NaruServe-logcat`.
records.rationale: Covers D-178 and D-179 (T40), in line with the wave 1 module declarations.

records.title: Every new RestApp or RouteBuilder configuration method calls the NEW-state guard first

acceptanceCriteria.text: The reflection test of FR-APP-002 AC-4 lists every non-static `RestApp` method returning `RestApp` and every `RouteBuilder` registration method, including those a later wave adds, and finds each one rejected with `IllegalStateException` in `RUNNING` with nothing recorded.

records.requirement: The system shall make every `RestApp` and `RouteBuilder` configuration method that a later wave adds (such as `ws`, `staticFiles`, `multipart` and `jsonCodec`) call the internal guard `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable` before it records anything.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 (app isolation, NEW-state guard, listen() startup and start gate), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-002.

records.title: Exceptions leave next.run() unchanged and reach the error path once

acceptanceCriteria.text: A middleware that wraps `next.run()` in `try`/`catch` catches the same exception instance the handler threw, and when it rethrows that instance a recording `onError` receives it exactly once.

records.requirement: The system shall let an exception thrown downstream leave `next.run()` unchanged and shall hand it to the error path exactly once, from the dispatcher, so a middleware can wrap `next.run()` in `try`/`catch` like a Servlet filter.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 (middleware pipeline, next contract, dispatcher order), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-004 and FR-APP-005.

records.title: Only the core writes the standard error JSON, never through JsonCodec

acceptanceCriteria.text: With an app `JsonCodec` whose `encode` and `decode` throw, a handler exception is still answered with the standard error body of FR-APP-006, byte for byte equal to the body produced with a working codec.

records.requirement: The system shall write the standard error JSON body only in the core and never through the app's `JsonCodec`, so the error body stays correct when the app codec is broken.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 (error path and standard error body), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-006.

records.title: The error outcome follows the response state after the onError chain and committed responses are aborted

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws while the response is `STREAMING` leaves the response `ABORTED` with no second status line written, and a handler that throws before commit, with no `onError` handler responding, gets the standard error response of FR-APP-006.

records.requirement: The system shall decide the outcome of the error path by the response state after the `onError` chain, and shall abort a committed response instead of giving it a second status line.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 (error path and standard error body), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-005.

records.title: Every service and owned resource lives in its app's one application context

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two apps in one JVM that register the same service key each return their own instance and close only their own owned resources, and the static-state scan of FR-APP-002 AC-2 finds no static registry or close list.

records.requirement: The system shall keep every service and owned resource in the one `DefaultApplicationContext` of its app and in no static field.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 (services, context, owned resources), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-007 and FR-APP-008.

records.title: Framework code logs only through the failure-isolating logger wrapper

acceptanceCriteria.text: With an app logger whose six methods, `flush` and `close` all throw, requests are answered, `listen` reaches `RUNNING` and `shutdown` reaches `TERMINATED`, and no logger exception reaches the adapter or the caller of `listen` or `shutdown`.

records.requirement: The system shall make framework code log only through the internal `SafeLogger` wrapper, so a logger failure is never a request or lifecycle failure.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 (logger isolation and access log), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-APP-014.

records.title: Core never names SLF4J or android types and platform loggers live in their own modules

acceptanceCriteria.text: The class-reference check of CON-APP-001 fails the build for any `org/slf4j/` or `android/` reference in the `NaruServe-api` main classes, and `LogcatLogger` reaches `android.util.Log` only by reflection.

records.requirement: The system shall keep `NaruServe-api` free of any reference to SLF4J or `android.*` types, with platform loggers in their own modules that reach the platform API by reflection or by a plain dependency.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 (logger modules and core isolation), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds CON-APP-001 and FR-APP-016.

records.title: A docs/api decision removes its marker in the same change and states its reason

acceptanceCriteria.text: The docs tests of OPS-APP-001 fail when a decided item still carries `(미확정)` on its line, and each decision of OPS-APP-001 AC-1 to AC-5 has a one-sentence reason next to it in `docs/api`.

records.requirement: The system shall remove the `(미확정)` marker of a `docs/api` item in the same change that decides it, and shall state the reason for the decision next to it.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-10 (docs/api decisions and docs compile gate), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds OPS-APP-001.

Dependencies that later waves add to the `testFixtures` configurations count as test scope under D-005.

records.title: NaruServe-api main never depends on its testFixtures source set

records.title: Dispatcher is the only RouteMatch-to-status mapping

acceptanceCriteria.text: No class outside `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal.Dispatcher` maps a `RouteMatch` kind or a pre-check result to an HTTP status, and no adapter class does.

records.requirement: The system shall map router lookup results and pre-checks to HTTP statuses only in the dispatcher, so the router stays engine-free and every adapter answers identically.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 (dispatcher, automatic responses, internal RestApp), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: Pre-checks run before any Request is built

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `OPTIONS *`, a raw path not starting with `/` and a raw path the path validator rejects, the dispatcher answers without constructing a `Request` and no handler, middleware or error handler is called.

records.requirement: The system shall run the pre-checks (`OPTIONS *`, raw path not starting with `/`, path validator) before any `Request` is built, so later middleware and `onError` may assume a non-null `Method` and a decoded path.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 (dispatcher, automatic responses, internal RestApp), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: A response commits status and headers at most once

acceptanceCriteria.text: For every response path (body writers, `end`, `stream`, automatic answers and failure answers), the exchange receives at most one call that starts the response (`commit`, `sendFile`, `upgrade` or `eventStream`).

records.requirement: The system shall commit a response's status and headers to the exchange at most once, because every adapter relies on a single commit call per exchange.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 (response writers and state machine), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: Every docs/api Java block compiles or sits on the named skip list

records.requirement: The system shall compile every ```java block of `docs/api` in the root test or list it on the named skip list, so docs examples do not drift from the API that Express users copy.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-6 (docs and docs-example compilation), moved to the SRS at SDS close.

records.title: Pre-request rejections are answered before any Request exists

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recording global middleware, a recording handler and a recording `onError` record no call for any pre-request rejection or lifecycle-gate `503`, and in every call they do receive `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path.

records.requirement: The system shall answer every pre-request rejection (unrecognised method token, raw path not starting with `/`, `PathValidator` rejection, `OPTIONS *`) and every lifecycle-gate `503` before a `Request` is built, so middleware, handlers and `onError` may assume that `req.method()` and `req.path()` are valid.
records.rationale: Durable rule of SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 (middleware pipeline, next contract, dispatcher order), moved to the SRS at SDS close; binds FR-HTTP-021.

records.title: The framework never uses runBlocking as an asynchronous adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: The build check `checkNoCoroutines`, wired into `check`, scans the main class output of every published module and fails, naming `Class -> kotlinx/coroutines/...`, when a constant-pool class name or descriptor starts with `kotlinx/coroutines/`, and passes on the wave 8 modules. [D-356]

The same check reads the resolved `compileClasspath` and `runtimeClasspath` of every published module and fails, naming the module and artifact, when a `kotlinx-coroutines` artifact is on either. [D-356]

A negative fixture proves both parts as Gradle TestKit builds that need no coroutines artifact from the network: a stub source `kotlinx/coroutines/BuildersKt.java` whose class is referenced from a fixture main class, and a fixture dependency on a `kotlinx-coroutines-core` POM served from a local file repository, each make `checkNoCoroutines` fail naming the class or the artifact, so the check cannot pass vacuously. [D-356]

records.requirement: The system shall not use `runBlocking` as an asynchronous adapter: no class of a published module references `kotlinx.coroutines`, no published module has a `kotlinx-coroutines` artifact on its `compileClasspath` or `runtimeClasspath`, and the build check `checkNoCoroutines` fails the build when either appears.
records.rationale: Covers D-356. Measured (2026-10-20): `grep -rn "runBlocking\|kotlinx.coroutines"` over `NaruServe*/src` and `src` finds no match; `docs/api/kotlin.md` documents that `suspend` handlers are unsupported in v1 and that `runBlocking` holds the request thread. Decision: the check is separate from the wave 1 `checkClassReferences` and `checkDependencyRules` tasks, because `BuildLayoutTest` pins the exact `prefixes += [...]` list of `build.gradle`; the new check scans constant pools of the main output of the nine published modules for `kotlinx/coroutines/` and reads each module's resolved `compileClasspath` and `runtimeClasspath` for group `org.jetbrains.kotlinx`, artifact `kotlinx-coroutines-*`. Pitfall: the existing prefix `kotlin/` does not match `kotlinx/` because of the slash. Rejected alternative: adding a coroutine adapter in `NaruServe-kotlin` with `runBlocking`; it would hold a request thread per suspend call and hide the cost behind a friendly signature; reopen when a separate non-blocking coroutine module is designed (post-v1).

records.title: RestApp.create() looks up the bootstrap AppFactory through ServiceLoader

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.create()` is a `public static` method of the `RestApp` interface returning `RestApp`, and `RestApp` declares no other `create` overload. [D-110; residual: class-loader overload]

Through the internal lookup helper and a dedicated class loader that exposes exactly one fake provider at `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory`, the helper returns the app the provider's `create()` returned. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: the lookup uses `ServiceLoader.load(AppFactory.class, loader)` where `RestApp.create()` passes `RestApp.class.getClassLoader()` and never the thread context class loader.

With a class loader that exposes no provider, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe` and mentions `RestApp.builder()`; `RestApp.create()` itself throws that exception in the `NaruServe-api` test run, where no provider is on the class path. [D-227]
With a class loader that exposes two providers, the helper throws `IllegalStateException` whose message names both provider class names. [wave decision: RestApp.create()]

The fake providers live in the `NaruServe-api` `test` source set, not in its `testFixtures`, so no other module's tests see a provider, and `NaruServe-api` main has no compile-time reference to TinyHttpd or Gson. The provider classes are compiled in `src/test/java`, but their `META-INF/services/com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.AppFactory` file is not on the test class path: the test writes it into a temporary directory that only the dedicated class loader sees. [D-226; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: the dedicated class loader is a `URLClassLoader` over the temporary directory whose parent loader holds the nested fake provider classes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-15]

records.title: Per-app state isolation and the NEW-state guard

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two apps built in one JVM with different routes, middleware, loggers and `onStart` registrations each answer only their own routes, run only their own middleware, log only to their own logger and expose only their own services and attributes. [D-113]

A reflection scan finds no non-`final` static field and no static field of a mutable collection type in the classes of `com.snoworca.naruserve` and `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` other than compile-time constants and `private static final` arrays that are never written after class initialisation (such as `MethodSet` `METHODS` and `DefaultResponse` `EMPTY`). [D-113]

In each of the states `STARTING` (called from an `onStart` callback), `RUNNING`, `STOPPING` (called from an `onStop` callback) and `TERMINATED`, each of `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `head`, `options`, `route(Method, ...)`, `route(MethodSet, ...)`, their route-middleware overloads, `use(mw)`, `use(prefix, mw)`, `accessLog`, `logger(l)`, `onStart`, `onStop`, `onError`, `routerPolicy` and the `get`/`use` methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained in `NEW` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the method and the current state, and the refused call changes nothing. [D-114; wave-4 carried: NEW-state rule]

Every guarded method calls one internal guard method, so a test that lists by reflection all non-static `RestApp` methods returning `RestApp` (including `logger(Logger)`) and the registration methods of a `RouteBuilder` obtained from `route(String)` finds each one rejected in `RUNNING`, while `logger()`, `state()` and `route(String)` itself are not guarded. [D-114] Decision: the one guard is the internal `AppLifecycle.requireConfigurable`, called first by every guarded method. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 SDS-AC-4]

The after-freeze rejection of verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5 still holds, because the one guard rejects when the state is not `NEW` or the route table is frozen (the harness and the FR-HTTP-008 tests freeze while the state is still `NEW`); FR-HTTP-008 AC-6 states the wave 3 situation that D-111 ends, and its wave 3 test is re-pointed to assert that `RestApp.builder()` and `RestApp.create()` are the only public static methods of `com.snoworca.naruserve` that return a `RestApp` or its builder. [D-114; D-111; wave-4 carried: NEW-state rule]

records.title: Middleware scope and pipeline order in the dispatcher

acceptanceCriteria.text: With global middleware `g1`, `g2`, prefix middleware `p1` on `/api` registered before `g2` and `p2` on `/api`, and `app.route("/api/users").use(r1).use(r2).get(h)`, a `GET /api/users` records `g1, g2, p1, p2, r1, r2, h`, and `app.get("/b", r3, h2)` makes `GET /b` record `g1, g2, r3, h2`. [D-120; D-119; T35] Decision: all global middleware run first in registration order, then all matching prefix middleware in registration order, however the two kinds of registration interleave. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-1]

Prefix `/api` runs for `/api` and `/api/users` and not for `/apix` or `/ap`; prefix `/api/` behaves as `/api`, and prefix `/` runs for every path. [D-118; T35] Decision: a trailing `/` of a prefix is ignored and `/` covers every path.

With `RouterPolicy.builder().caseInsensitive(true)` the `/api` prefix middleware runs for `/API/users`, and with `mergeSlashes(true)` it runs for `//api//users`, so every path that reaches a route under the prefix runs the prefix middleware. [D-118] Decision: the prefix comparison uses the same case and slash normalisation that the router applies under the app's `RouterPolicy`.

Inside prefix middleware and the handler, `req.path()` still returns the full decoded path (for example `/api/users`, not `/users`). [D-118; D-137] Decision: NaruServe does not strip the mount prefix from `req.path()` and has no `baseUrl`.

A request that matches no route runs global and matching prefix middleware and then receives the `404` of the fallback point; route middleware of other routes does not run. [D-121; D-117] Decision: for a lookup result other than `MATCHED` the dispatcher builds the `Request` with the parsed `Method` and empty params and runs the global and matching prefix middleware with an empty route middleware list and the fallback answer as the terminal step. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-6]

A recording global middleware runs once each for a `405` (method mismatch), a `426` (WebSocket-only route without upgrade), an automatic `OPTIONS /r` `204`, a `501` for `TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and a `501` for `CONNECT /`, before the automatic response is written. [D-117; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

A global middleware does not run for the pre-request rejections (unrecognised method token `501`, raw path not starting with `/` `400`, `PathValidator` rejection `400`, `OPTIONS *` `204`) nor for the lifecycle-gate `503`s of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate]
For a matched route all middleware and the handler run on the adapter thread that called the dispatcher, one after the other. [D-128]

records.title: next.run() contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: A middleware that calls `next.run()` twice gets `IllegalStateException` from the second call, and the downstream middleware and handler ran once. [D-122; T35]

A middleware that calls `next.run()` after `res.send("x")` completed the response gets `IllegalStateException` and no downstream middleware runs; a `Next` kept and called after the request ended (from the test thread after the in-memory exchange finished) throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-123] Decision: `next.run()` throws when the response is `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` or the request has ended, and no downstream step runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-10]

A middleware that records a marker after `next.run()` returns sees the handler's marker already recorded and `res.isCommitted()` true for a handler that called `res.send(...)`. [D-124] Decision: an exception thrown downstream propagates out of `next.run()` unchanged and the dispatcher hands it to the error path once, so a middleware may wrap `next.run()` in `try`/`catch`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-11]
A middleware that writes `res.status(401).send("no")` and returns without `next.run()` delivers `401` with body `no`, and the later middleware and the handler record no call. [D-125; T36]

Calling `next.error(e)` after `next.run()` in the same invocation, or `next.run()` after `next.error(e)`, throws `IllegalStateException`; `next.error(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-122; D-116] Decision: `next.run()` and `next.error(e)` together count as the single continuation of one invocation. Decision: `next.error(null)` throws before the continuation is consumed. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-12]
`next.run()` runs the downstream chain on the calling thread, and no middleware or handler runs after the dispatcher returned to the adapter for a non-streaming response. [D-128]

records.requirement: The system shall let each middleware invocation continue the chain at most once through `next.run()` or `next.error(e)`, return from `next.run()` only after every downstream middleware and the handler returned, deliver the response of a middleware that responds without calling `next.run()` with no later middleware or handler run, and throw `IllegalStateException` for a second continuation within one invocation and for a continuation after the response completed or the request ended.
records.rationale: Covers D-122, D-123, D-124, D-125 and D-128 (synchronous execution). The unfinished-response case of D-126 is in the wave 4 successor of FR-HTTP-006. T35, T36.

records.title: Unified error path and onError chain

acceptanceCriteria.text: With one recording `onError`, a `RuntimeException` thrown by a middleware, a checked `IOException` thrown by a handler and `next.error(e)` from a middleware each reach the handler once with the same `Throwable` instance and the request's `Request` and `Response`. [D-127; D-129; T36] Decision: a thrown `java.lang.Error` is not routed to `onError`; it aborts the response and is rethrown, as in wave 3. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-1]

An `HttpException(400)` thrown by a handler, an `HttpException(413)` and an `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` each reach `onError` with `status()` readable, and the malformed query `?x=%zz` raises an `HttpException` with status `400` that reaches `onError` after the middleware ran and before the handler. [D-129; D-130; wave-4 carried: malformed query]

With two `onError` handlers, the second runs only when the first returned with the response `NEW`, and receives the same error; when the first responded, the second records no call. [D-137] Decision: `onError` registrations form one chain in registration order that stops at the first handler that starts the response. Decision: the first `onError` handler runs whatever the response state was when the error arrived; a later one runs only while the response is still `NEW`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-2]

When every `onError` handler returned with the response `NEW`, or none is registered, the response is the standard error response of FR-APP-006 for the error. [D-132; D-137] Decision: the standard error response drops the status and headers the app set before the error. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-3]

An `onError` handler that throws makes the framework log the thrown exception at `ERROR` through the app logger and answer the standard `500` error response if the response is still `NEW`; no later `onError` handler runs. [D-129; D-133]

When a handler throws while the response is `STREAMING`, `onError` is still called once, no error body is written, and after the error path the response is `ABORTED` with the in-memory exchange closed abnormally; when the response is `COMPLETED`, it stays `COMPLETED` with the sent bytes unchanged. [D-131; T37]

A recording `onError` records no call for the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `OPTIONS` responses and for the pre-request and lifecycle-gate rejections. [residual: onError scope; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]

An error that ends in a standard `500` response is logged once at `ERROR` with its `Throwable` through the app logger; an `HttpException` with a `4xx` status is not logged at `ERROR`. [D-129; D-133] Decision: only `500`s are logged at `ERROR`, with the stack trace kept in the server log. Decision: a `500` is logged at `ERROR` whatever the response state, and no other status is logged at `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-6]

The error path decides by the response state at the time the error arrives (`NEW` gives the error response, committed but not completed gives an abort, `COMPLETED` stays unchanged), the rule that the `res.json` serialisation case of D-136 relies on; that case itself is asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists. [D-136; D-131] Decision: the error path reads the response state once, after the `onError` chain, under the response lock; because a response committed on arrival can only stay committed or end, this gives the same outcome as the arrival-state rule. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-7]

records.requirement: The system shall route an exception thrown by a middleware or handler and an error passed to `next.error(e)` to one error path that calls the registered `onError` handlers in registration order while the previous one left the response `NEW`, writes the standard error response of FR-APP-006 when the response is still `NEW` after them, and aborts instead of writing an error body when the response is already committed but not completed, while `onError` never receives the automatic `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` or `OPTIONS` responses.
records.rationale: Covers D-127, D-129, D-131, the D-137 decision on `onError` chaining, D-136 (asserted in wave 5 once `res.json` exists) and the residual on `onError` scope. Replaces the wave 3 interim failure handling (FR-HTTP-006, superseded in wave 4). T36, T37.

records.title: Standard error JSON body, status mapping and code values

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `new RuntimeException("secret com.example.Foo")` is answered `500` with exactly `{"error":{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"Internal Server Error","requestId":"<id>"}}`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a matching `Content-Length`, and the body contains neither the exception message, nor `RuntimeException`, nor `at ` stack frames. [D-132; D-133] Decision: the body has no whitespace and exactly the fields `code`, `message` and `requestId` in that order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-8]

The `code` values are `400` `BAD_REQUEST`, `404` `NOT_FOUND`, `405` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`, `413` `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `415` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `422` `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY`, `426` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`, `500` `INTERNAL_ERROR`, `501` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` and `503` `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and any other `HttpException` status uses `HTTP_<status>`. [D-134; D-137] Decision: these are the `code` values per status.

The `message` is the status reason phrase (for example `Not Found`), except for an `HttpException` created with a message, whose message is used; a `500` always uses `Internal Server Error`. [D-133; D-137] Decision: only an app-supplied `HttpException` message reaches the client.

Through the harness, a handler throwing `HttpException(400)`, `HttpException(422)`, `HttpException(413)` and `UnsupportedMediaTypeException` is answered `400`, `422`, `413` and `415` with the standard body, and any other exception `500`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]

The automatic `404`, `405` (with its `Allow` header), `426` (with `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade`), `501`, the pre-request `400`s and `501` and the lifecycle-gate `503`s carry the standard body with their `code`; the `204` answers keep no body. [D-134; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave-4 carried: standard error body]
For a `HEAD` request the standard error response carries the headers and the `Content-Length` of the body it would have had and no body. [D-132; FR-HTTP-017]
The `requestId` of a standard error body equals the request id field of the access log line of FR-APP-015 for the same request, also for the pre-request rejections. [D-135]

The body is generated by the core without the app's `JsonCodec`, escapes `"`, `\` and control characters of the `message` per RFC 8259, and is identical with any codec. [D-132] Decision: the core writes the standard error JSON itself. Decision: non-ASCII characters stay literal UTF-8 and are not escaped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-5 SDS-AC-13]
No API replaces the automatic `404`/`405` bodies in v1; an app answers custom `404` pages with a route of its own. [D-137] Decision: custom `404`/`405` bodies are not configurable in v1.

records.requirement: The system shall answer an error with no `onError` response, and the framework's own error statuses `400`, `404`, `405`, `426`, `501` and `503`, with the body `{"error":{"code":...,"message":...,"requestId":...}}`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a `Content-Length`, using the status mapping of D-134 and the `code` values decided for #5, with no stack trace or exception class name and with `requestId` equal to the id the access log records for the request.
records.rationale: Covers D-132, D-133, D-134, D-135, the D-137 decisions on `code` values per status and on custom `404`/`405` bodies, the wave decisions on `415`, on `426` and `501` (automatic responses with the standard body) and on overload `503` (a full TinyHttpd queue is a transport-level `503`, D-400, not standard JSON), and the carried line that wave 4 gives the error statuses the standard error body.

records.title: Service registration, frozen registry and the single application context

acceptanceCriteria.text: A `UserService` registered in `onStart` is returned with identity by `req.service(UserService.class)` and `req.application().get(UserService.class)` in an HTTP handler; the WebSocket and SSE cases of D-142 are asserted in wave 7. [D-142; T41; wave decision: Services for long connections]

`ctx.register` and `ctx.registerExternal` called from `onStop`, and `req.application().register(...)` called from a handler in `RUNNING`, throw `IllegalStateException`, and the registry is unchanged. [D-139; D-141; T42] Decision: `register`, `registerExternal` and `own` throw `IllegalStateException` naming the method and the state whenever the state is not `STARTING` or the registry is frozen, before the registry or the close list is touched. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-2]

A second `ctx.register(UserService.class, other)` in `onStart` throws `IllegalStateException` naming the key, so `listen()` fails with it, and `getOrNull(UserService.class)` read from a failing-start close hook still returns the first instance. [D-140; T42] Decision: the configuration error is `IllegalStateException`. Decision: the message contains the class name of the key, the first instance stays registered and the second is not tracked for closing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-3]

In `RUNNING` sixteen threads calling `req.service(UserService.class)` concurrently all receive the registered instance, and the registry seen in `RUNNING` is an unmodifiable snapshot taken before the state became `RUNNING`. [D-141]
Two `onStart` callbacks run in registration order, each exactly once for one successful `listen()`, and neither runs again on `shutdown`. [D-143; D-154; T41]

`ctx.attribute` set in `onStart` is read by handlers in `RUNNING` and by `onStop` in `STOPPING`, and eight threads writing and reading distinct keys concurrently during `RUNNING` lose no write, and `onStop` writes `ctx.attribute("k2", v)` and reads it back. [D-144] Decision: attributes live in a concurrent map that the lifecycle gate does not guard. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-7]

`ctx.logger()` in `onStart` and `onStop` returns the same instance as `app.logger()`, also after `app.logger(l)` replaced it before `listen`. [D-145] Decision: `ctx.logger()` returns `app.logger()` read at call time, the logger as set and not the framework's failure-isolating wrapper. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-6 SDS-AC-8]
The `ctx` passed to `onStart`, the `ctx` passed to `onStop` and `req.application()` in every request are the same instance. [D-146]

records.title: listen() startup sequence and the start gate

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two threads calling `listen(0)` at the same time on a `NEW` app: exactly one proceeds and the other gets `IllegalStateException`; a second `listen` after a successful one throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-153] Decision: the start is claimed by one compare-and-set from `NEW` to `STARTING`, and only its winner proceeds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 SDS-AC-6]

A recording test adapter and callbacks observe the order: state `STARTING`, `onStart` callbacks in registration order, route-table freeze, one `bind` call, state `RUNNING`, `listen` returns. [D-154; wave-4 carried: listen runs the route-table freeze]
A duplicate route of D-044 makes `listen()` throw the freeze's `RoutingConfigException` after the `onStart` callbacks ran and before any `bind` call. [D-154; D-157]
`listen()` returns only after `bind` returned, and the returned `ServerHandle` reports the bound port. [D-155]

With a test adapter whose `bind` dispatches a request from another thread before returning, the request's middleware and handler run only after `app.state()` is `RUNNING` (asserted inside the handler), and the request is answered normally. [D-156; D-428] Decision: a request arriving in `STARTING` blocks on the start gate and is dispatched only after the state is set to `RUNNING`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 SDS-AC-10]

With a test adapter whose `bind` dispatches a request from another thread and then throws `IOException`, the held request is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body, and no middleware, handler or `onError` runs for it. [D-428; wave decision: Lifecycle gate; wave decision: STARTING]

The test-fixtures harness `TestApp` builds its app with `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(inMemoryAdapter).jsonCodec(stubCodec)` (a stub `JsonCodec` in the test fixtures) and its `start()` calls `listen(0)`, which runs the route-table freeze once, so a `RoutingConfigException` of the freeze still reaches the test caller unwrapped and every wave 3 test through `TestApp` that cites a requirement wave 4 does not supersede keeps passing unchanged, while the tests citing FR-HTTP-002, FR-HTTP-003, FR-HTTP-005, FR-HTTP-006 or FR-HTTP-010 are re-pointed to FR-HTTP-021..FR-HTTP-025 and assert the standard error body (a requirement change, not a weakened test); verified FR-HTTP-001 AC-3 (the harness builds the internal implementation and runs the freeze once) still holds. [wave-4 carried: listen runs the route-table freeze; D-154] Decision: the stub codec is the test-fixtures `StubJsonCodec`, and `start()` calls `listen(0)` once. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-3 SDS-AC-12]

The start gate and the lifecycle gate belong to the exchange handler that `listen()` passes to the adapter; the wave 3 `Dispatcher(Router)` constructor and `DefaultRestApp.dispatcher()` that unit tests bind without `listen()` stay ungated, so those verified wave 3 unit tests keep dispatching. [D-428; D-156] Decision: the gates wrap the dispatcher instead of living inside it.

Resources owned and registered before an `onStart` failure are closed in reverse order before `listen()` throws, and a resource's `close()` reads `app.state()` as `FAILED`; after `listen()` threw, `app.state()` is `TERMINATED`. [D-158; D-159; T43]

records.title: Shutdown sequence, deadline and shutdown participants

acceptanceCriteria.text: A recording test adapter, participants in all three phases, an `onStop` callback, an owned resource and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger record the order: before-wait participants, `adapter.stop`, force-close participants, `onStop`, after-`onStop` participants, owned resource `close`, logger `flush` and `close`, `adapter.release`, then `app.state()` is `TERMINATED`. [D-162; D-401; T46]

The timeout passed to `adapter.stop` is the time left until the one deadline computed when `shutdown` began, so a before-wait participant that sleeps 200 ms of a 1 s timeout leaves at most 800 ms for the adapter stop. [D-162; wave-4 carried: exchange lifetime] Decision: the deadline is `System.nanoTime() + unit.toNanos(timeout)`, computed once, and `adapter.stop` receives `max(0, deadline - now)` nanoseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-8]
The internal participant registry adds participants to a phase in order and runs them in that order; a participant that throws is logged at `ERROR` and the sequence continues. [D-401]
`onStop` reads every service registered in `onStart` through `ctx.get`, before any owned resource is closed. [D-163; T45]

Two threads calling `shutdown` on a `RUNNING` app: one runs the sequence; the other and any later call return without running any step again, and `onStop` ran once. [D-161; T46] Decision: the losing caller waits for `TERMINATED` up to its own timeout and then returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-11]
A request in flight when `shutdown` begins completes normally while the adapter stop waits within the deadline. [D-162]
An app logger that is also owned is skipped at its owned position and closed once at the log-writer step; closing the console logger leaves `System.out` open. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; D-148]

An `onStop` callback that throws is logged at `ERROR`, the remaining `onStop` callbacks run and the sequence continues to `TERMINATED`. [D-162] Decision: `onStop` failures do not stop shutdown. An `Error` (not only an `Exception`) thrown by an `onStop` callback or a shutdown participant is handled the same way, so the owned-resource close, the logger flush and close and the adapter release still run; after `TERMINATED` the first such `Error` is rethrown from `shutdown`, as on the start-failure path. [wave-4 loop P issue w4-S2-001]

`shutdown(timeout, unit)` called from a route handler or middleware of a `RUNNING` app runs the sequence on a separate non-daemon thread named `naruserve-shutdown` and returns at once, and that request's response is sent in full; called from a handler while another shutdown is already `STOPPING`, it returns at once; when the shutdown thread cannot be started, the sequence runs on the calling thread and still reaches `TERMINATED`. [D-161; D-162; wave-4 loop P issue w4-P1-001] Decision: in-request shutdown does not wait for itself, because the sequence waits for in-flight requests.

Wave 6 adds temporary-file cleanup (D-255) as an after-`onStop` participant and wave 7 adds WebSocket (D-435) and SSE (D-436) closing as before-wait participants. T45, T46.

records.title: shutdown in NEW, STARTING, FAILED and TERMINATED, and listen after termination

acceptanceCriteria.text: `shutdown` on a `NEW` app sets `TERMINATED`, runs no `onStart` or `onStop` callback, never calls the adapter's `bind`, and closes a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger once. [D-164; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch inside `listen()` on thread A, `shutdown(5, SECONDS)` on thread B, then the latch released: `onStart` finishes, no `bind` happens, `listen()` throws `AppStartException`, no `onStop` runs, owned resources close in reverse order and observe `FAILED`, `app.state()` ends `TERMINATED`, and `shutdown` returns after `listen()` ended, and a `Flushable`/`AutoCloseable` app logger is flushed and closed once after the resources closed and before `TERMINATED`. [D-426; T46; residual: Logger close on every path into TERMINATED] Decision: a start ended by a pending stop throws `AppStartException` with a message saying shutdown was requested while starting. Decision: with a pending stop recorded during `onStart` callback k, the callbacks registered after k do not run; the latch test registers a second callback and asserts it never ran.

When the pending stop is recorded during `bind`, the socket bound by it is released (`stop` and `release` called) and `RUNNING` is never set, and a request that the test adapter dispatched during that `bind` is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body with no middleware, handler or `onError` run. [D-426; D-428]

With `onStart` blocked on a latch, `shutdown(100, MILLISECONDS)` returns normally without an exception before the latch is released, `app.state()` is then `STARTING` or `FAILED`, and once the latch is released `listen()` still passes through `FAILED` to `TERMINATED` and throws `AppStartException`. [D-438; T46]

A resource `close()` running during a failing `listen()` (state `FAILED`) starts thread B, which calls `shutdown(5, SECONDS)`, and then blocks 100 ms; B's `shutdown` returns after the state became `TERMINATED` and within its timeout; `shutdown` on a `TERMINATED` app returns at once with no callback or close run. [D-427]
`listen(0)` on a `TERMINATED` app throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-165; T46]

records.title: Requests reaching the dispatcher during STOPPING get 503 with Connection: close

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request sent through the in-memory adapter from a before-wait shutdown participant (after `STOPPING` began, before the adapter stop) is answered `503` with `Connection: close` and `{"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",...}}`. [D-166; D-134; wave decision: Keep-alive at shutdown]

For that request a recording global middleware, the route handler and a recording `onError` record no call, and the access log records exactly one line with status `503`. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-173]

A request that was in flight when `STOPPING` began is not answered `503` and completes with its handler's response. [D-166; D-162] Decision: the gate reads the state once, when the request enters it. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-7 SDS-AC-23]

The lifecycle gate runs before the pre-request checks, so during `STOPPING` an `OPTIONS *`, an unrecognised method token and a raw path not starting with `/` are each answered `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body, and in `STARTING` they are held on the start gate like any request. [wave decision: Lifecycle gate; D-428] Decision: the lifecycle gate is the first check of the exchange handler that `listen()` passes to the adapter, which wraps the dispatcher (FR-APP-009 AC-8).

records.title: One access log line per HTTP request

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the defaults, `GET /users/7` answered `200` with a 5-byte body produces exactly one `info` line matching `GET /users/7 200 \d+ms in=0 out=5 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`. [D-173; D-181; T38] Decision: this is the line format, and the request id is 16 lowercase hex characters generated per request. Decision: the duration is the `System.nanoTime()` difference from request start to response end divided by 1 000 000, in whole milliseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-4]

With `includeDuration(false)`, `includeBytes(false)` and `includeRequestId(false)` the line is `GET /users/7 200`, and with `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` it is written through `debug`. [D-172; D-173] Decision: a disabled part is dropped together with its leading space, and `level` selects the `Logger` method, `trace` to `error(String)` for `TRACE` to `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-5]

A response aborted after commit (handler throws while `STREAMING`) produces one line with its committed status followed by ` aborted`; a `404`, a `405`, a handler `500`, each pre-request rejection (`501` unknown token, `400` raw path, `400` validator, `204` `OPTIONS *`) and each lifecycle-gate `503` produce exactly one line. [D-173; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate]
For a streaming response the line is written once after the stream copy finished, with `out` equal to the bytes copied; for a `HEAD` response `out` is `0`. [D-173; D-177]

`in` counts the request body bytes the core read from the adapter's body stream (not the declared `Content-Length`): a dispatcher test whose handler reads 4 bytes of a 10-byte body through the internal `BodyState` stream logs `in=4`, and a handler that never reads gives `in=0`. [D-177]

After `exclude("/health")`, `GET /health` produces no line while `GET /health/x` and `GET /healthz` do; with `enabled(false)` no request produces a line. [D-174; D-172] Decision: `exclude` matches the raw path without the query exactly.
The `rid` value of the line equals the `requestId` of the standard error body of the same request. [D-135]

records.title: Logcat logger through reflection on android.util.Log

acceptanceCriteria.text: A JVM test in `NaruServe-logcat` with a test-scope fake `android.util.Log` that records calls shows `new LogcatLogger()` calling `v`, `d`, `i`, `w`, `e(tag, msg)` and `e(tag, msg, t)` with tag `NaruServe` for the six methods. [D-403] Decision: the default tag is `NaruServe`. Decision: the `android.util.Log` methods are resolved once, in the constructor, through `Class.forName("android.util.Log")`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-1]

`new LogcatLogger("MyApp")` uses tag `MyApp`, and `new LogcatLogger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. [D-403] Decision: the `null` tag check runs before the class lookup. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-2]

Without `android.util.Log` on the class path, the `LogcatLogger` constructor throws `IllegalStateException` naming `android.util.Log`; an exception thrown by a reflective call is caught and not rethrown. The case without `android.util.Log` loads `LogcatLogger` through a dedicated class loader that sees the `NaruServe-logcat` and `NaruServe-api` main classes but not the test classes. [D-403; D-171] Decision: the dedicated class loader is a `URLClassLoader` over the `NaruServe-logcat` and `NaruServe-api` main class directories whose parent is the bootstrap loader. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-4]

The `NaruServe-logcat` main classes reference no `android.*` type in their bytecode; `android.util.Log` appears only as a string for reflection, and the fake class lives only in the test source set. [D-403; D-178]

records.title: Rotating file logger with a bounded queue

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RotatingFileLogger.builder().build()` uses directory `./logs`, `maxFileBytes` `5242880`, `maxFiles` `5`, `queueCapacity` `1024` and level `INFO`; `maxFileBytes`, `maxFiles` or `queueCapacity` below `1` throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-180; I-012] Decision: the queue capacity defaults to 1024 records and no value may be unlimited. Decision: an out-of-range value throws from the builder setter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-6]

Records are written to `naruserve.log` in the console line format of IR-APP-006; when the next record would exceed `maxFileBytes` the files rotate to `naruserve.log.1` up to `naruserve.log.<maxFiles-1>`, dropping the oldest, so a test with `maxFileBytes(200)` and `maxFiles(3)` ends with at most three files. [D-180] Decision: the file names are `naruserve.log` and `naruserve.log.<n>`.
With the writer blocked on a latch inside the test output stream and `queueCapacity(2)`, the third and later records are dropped without blocking the caller and `droppedCount()` counts them. [D-180]

With a directory that cannot be created, logging calls return normally and `droppedCount()` grows; no exception reaches the caller. [wave decision: File logger directory; D-171] Decision: a failed write is handled the same way: the writer thread drops and counts the record. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-9]

`flush()` returns after every record queued before the call is written; `close()` writes the queued records, stops the writer thread so no thread of the logger remains, and later logging calls are dropped and counted. [wave decision: Logger shutdown; I-015] Decision: `flush()` and `close()` wait for a marker record queued behind the earlier records. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-9 SDS-AC-10]
The module's main classes reference no SLF4J or `android.*` type and pass the API 21 animal-sniffer check. [D-179; C-02]

The tests of this requirement and the failed-`listen()` writer-thread check of FR-APP-010 AC-6 live in the `NaruServe-filelog` test source set, which declares `testImplementation testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api'))`; tests block the writer through a package-private constructor that takes the factory of the file output stream. [D-180; I-015]

When renaming `naruserve.log` fails during rotation, the logger keeps appending to the same file without deleting any line, the public `rotationFailureCount()` counts the failure, the next rotation is attempted only after the file grows by another `maxFileBytes`, and a backup is deleted only when no free backup number is left, so a rename that keeps failing deletes no further backup. [D-180; D-171; wave-4 loop P issue w4-P1-001] Decision: a failed rotation keeps logging and backs off instead of retrying on every record.

records.title: Access log: one line per HTTP request, the WebSocket handshake and close lines, and the SSE stream-end line (wave 7)

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the defaults, `GET /users/7` answered `200` with a 5-byte body produces exactly one `info` line matching `GET /users/7 200 \d+ms in=0 out=5 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`. [D-173; D-181; T38] Decision: this is the line format, and the request id is 16 lowercase hex characters generated per request. Decision: the duration is the `System.nanoTime()` difference from request start to response end divided by 1 000 000, in whole milliseconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-4] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC1

With `includeDuration(false)`, `includeBytes(false)` and `includeRequestId(false)` the line is `GET /users/7 200`, and with `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` it is written through `debug`. [D-172; D-173] Decision: a disabled part is dropped together with its leading space, and `level` selects the `Logger` method, `trace` to `error(String)` for `TRACE` to `ERROR`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-5] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC2

A response aborted after commit (handler throws while `STREAMING`) produces one line with its committed status followed by ` aborted`; a `404`, a `405`, a handler `500`, each pre-request rejection (`501` unknown token, `400` raw path, `400` validator, `204` `OPTIONS *`) and each lifecycle-gate `503` produce exactly one line. [D-173; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; wave decision: Lifecycle gate] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC3

For a streaming response the line is written once after the stream copy finished, with `out` equal to the bytes copied; for a `HEAD` response `out` is `0`. [D-173; D-177] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC4

`in` counts the request body bytes the core read from the adapter's body stream (not the declared `Content-Length`): a dispatcher test whose handler reads 4 bytes of a 10-byte body through the internal `BodyState` stream logs `in=4`, and a handler that never reads gives `in=0`. [D-177] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC5

After `exclude("/health")`, `GET /health` produces no line while `GET /health/x` and `GET /healthz` do; with `enabled(false)` no request produces a line. [D-174; D-172] Decision: `exclude` matches the raw path without the query exactly. re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC6
The `rid` value of the line equals the `requestId` of the standard error body of the same request. [D-135] re_stated_from: FR-APP-015#AC7

An accepted upgrade to `/ws` produces exactly one handshake line matching `GET /ws 101 \d+ms in=0 out=0 rid=[0-9a-f]{16}`, written in the endpoint's `onOpen` after `101` was written and before the first frame is read, which a test asserts by reading the log before the client sends its first frame; an upgrade rejected before `onOpen` (`426` for `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 12`, `403` for a refused `Origin`, `503` beyond the limit) produces its ordinary line with the rejection status and no `101` line (T38). [D-430; D-325; T38] Decision: the handshake line is written in `onOpen` after the channel is stored and before the handler, with the duration measured from `req.startNanos()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-1] Decision: when the response ends with `upgraded101()` true no line is written from `onDone`, and a refusal before `onOpen` never calls `upgraded`, so its ordinary line is written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-2]

When a session ends, one close line `WS /ws <closeCode> \d+ms rid=<id>` is written with the same `rid` as its handshake line, the close code chosen by FR-WS-006 AC-9 (`1000` for `ws.close()`, `1001` at shutdown, `1008` on queue overflow, each also when the client never answers the server's close frame; the client's code for a client close; `1006` for a session aborted without any close frame) and the duration from `onOpen` to the close, exactly once per session (T38). Decision: the close line form is `WS <path> <closeCode>[ <n>ms][ rid=<id>]`. [D-325; T38]

An SSE stream produces no line when it starts and exactly one line when it ends, matching `GET /events 200 \d+ms in=0 out=<n> rid=[0-9a-f]{16} sse start=\d+ cause=(client|app|overflow|shutdown|error)`, where the duration covers the whole stream, `out` equals the bytes written to the stream, `start` is the epoch milliseconds of the stream start, and `cause` is the first end reason the core recorded for the stream: `app` when `close()` is called, `overflow` when the overflow policy ends the stream, and `shutdown` when the closing participant marks the stream ended or the deadline force-close begins, each recorded before any `IOException` that the ending causes; `client` only when a drain write or heartbeat to the socket failed with an `IOException`, or the drain found the connection closed, on a stream with no earlier recorded reason (how a client disconnect is detected); and `error` when a failure that is not an `IOException` in the core or app code during the drain (for example a `RuntimeException` thrown by event serialisation or by the adapter's output stream) ends a stream with no earlier recorded reason; an in-memory test asserts `cause=client` for a drain write failed with `IOException`, `cause=error` for a drain write failed with a `RuntimeException`, `cause=app` when the drain write after `close()` fails with `IOException` and `cause=overflow` when the drain write after the overflow end fails with `IOException`, and a TinyHttpd test asserts `cause=shutdown` for the stalled stream force-closed at the shutdown deadline (FR-SSE-005 AC-5); a `HEAD` to an SSE route produces its ordinary line without the `sse` part (T38). Decision: the SSE line appends ` sse start=<epochMillis> cause=<cause>` to the D-173 line, and the first recorded end reason wins over a later `IOException` or failure. [D-338; D-343; T38] Decision: for a response with a non-null `sseClient()`, `writeSse` is called with status `200`, `out` = `bytesWritten()`, the stream's start millis and the client's `cause()`; a null cause cannot occur because `sseEnded` runs only after `endBy`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-12 SDS-AC-4]

`exclude("/ws")` and `exclude("/events")` suppress the WebSocket handshake and close lines and the SSE line of those paths, `enabled(false)` suppresses all of them, and `level(LogLevel.DEBUG)` writes them through `debug`. [D-325; D-338; D-174]

records.requirement: The system shall write through the app logger at the configured level exactly one access log line per HTTP request that reaches the dispatcher, when the response completes or is aborted, in the format `<method> <path> <status>[ aborted][ <duration>ms][ in=<bytesIn> out=<bytesOut>][ rid=<requestId>]`, where `path` is the raw path without the query, the optional parts follow the options of IR-APP-007, the byte fields count body bytes actually read from and written to the connection, and requests to an excluded path produce no line, except that an accepted WebSocket upgrade gets its line with status `101` when the connection opens plus a separate close line with close code and duration, and an SSE stream gets its one line when the stream ends, with its start time and closing cause.
records.rationale: Restates FR-APP-015 AC-1 to AC-7 unchanged for plain HTTP (D-173, D-174, D-177, D-135, D-181 and the pre-request and lifecycle-gate decisions of wave 4) and adds D-430 (the `101` handshake line written in `onOpen`), D-325 (separate WebSocket close line with close code and duration) and D-338 (one SSE line at stream end with start time, duration, bytes and closing cause), which change the "one line per request when the response completes" statement; test T38 (WebSocket and SSE parts). Measured: `internal/AccessLog.java:51-86` formats the D-173 line once per request when the response completes; `DefaultAccessLogOptions`, `BodyState` and `RequestIds` keep their roles. Decision: the WebSocket close line starts with the token `WS` instead of an HTTP method so log tools can tell it from request lines; the SSE line keeps the D-173 prefix and appends ` sse start=<epochMillis> cause=<client|app|overflow|shutdown|error>`. Decision (SSE cause, AC-10): the first end reason recorded wins. The core records `app` when `close()` is called, `overflow` when the overflow policy ends the stream and `shutdown` when the closing participant marks the stream ended or the deadline force-close begins, before any `IOException` that the ending causes (TinyHttpd's `stop` aborts every remaining socket at the grace deadline, so the stalled drain write of FR-SSE-005 AC-5 then fails with an `IOException`); `client` is recorded only when an `IOException` or a detected closed connection ends a stream with no earlier recorded reason, since a client disconnect is seen only as such a failure (FR-SSE-003 AC-7, FR-SSE-004 AC-2); `error` is kept for a failure that is not an `IOException` (a `RuntimeException` in the drain, serialisation or adapter stream) with no earlier recorded reason; the core tells `client` from `error` by exception type. Pitfall: writing the SSE line at `res.sse()` time would log `out=0` and no cause; it is written when the stream ends. Pitfall: an upgrade rejected before `onOpen` must not get a `101` line; it takes the ordinary error-path line (D-444). Rejected alternative: logging every WebSocket message; it would flood the log of a chat app, reopen on demand as an option. Tests to re-point to FR-APP-019: every `FR_APP_015_*` method of `NaruServe-api/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/AccessLogTest.java`, `AccessLogAcceptanceTest.java`, `internal/DispatcherTest.java` (pre-request rejection log asserts) and the access-log asserts of `internal/StoppingGateTest.java` and `internal/AppIsolationTest.java`; the `@req FR-APP-015` comments of `AccessLog.java`, `BodyState.java`, `DefaultAccessLogOptions.java`, `DefaultResponse.java`, `DefaultRestApp.java`, `Dispatcher.java` and `RequestIds.java` move to FR-APP-019.

records.title: Long-connection shutdown coordination: closed flags before snapshots, participants with the deadline, the accepting phase, in-flight requests, force-close and the 3 s bound

acceptanceCriteria.text: `ShutdownParticipants` keeps `add(Phase, Runnable)` and gains an overload taking a participant that receives `long deadlineNanos`; participants of both kinds registered in one phase run in registration order, and a deadline participant receives the deadline that `shutdown(timeout, unit)` computed, which a test asserts by checking that `deadlineNanos - System.nanoTime()` at entry is at most the timeout and at least the timeout minus 100 ms. Decision: the deadline participant is a package-private functional interface. [residual: Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003)]

With a shutdown timeout of 500 ms and one WebSocket session whose client stopped reading, the WebSocket close wait ends within 500 ms plus 200 ms and `shutdown` returns within 500 ms plus the 3 s margin (T44 case with a timeout below 1 s). [residual: Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003)] [D-344]

Each closing participant sets its registry's closed flag under the registry lock before it takes its snapshot; afterwards `res.sse()` in a handler that was already running returns a client that is ended at once: the client receives the event-stream headers, the closing notice `event: shutdown
data: shutdown

` and the end of the body, the `onClose` listeners run once and `send` returns `false`; an upgrade that reaches the upgrade extension point after the flag receives `503` with `Connection: close` before any `101`; and every session or stream registered before the flag is in the snapshot, which an in-memory test asserts by setting the flag between two registrations. [D-445; carried: V2-002]

The before-wait participants run while the adapter still accepts connections, for at most 1 s plus 200 ms of slack: a plain request sent while the WebSocket close wait is held by a stalled session receives `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body from the stopping gate, and an upgrade sent in that phase is refused without `101`. Deviation (recorded): object.md §11.4 step 2 stops accepting new connections and upgrades before the goodbye of step 3; NaruServe accepts connections during this phase and answers them `503` under D-166, which `docs/api/lifecycle.md` records. [D-446; carried: V2-002]

A short request whose handler takes 300 ms and starts before `shutdown(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` completes with `200` and its full body, and the `onStop` callback runs only after that response completed, which a test asserts by recording both events in order (T44). [D-342]

A WebSocket session and an SSE stream whose clients stopped reading are force-closed by the deadline: both client sockets reach end of stream or reset within the shutdown timeout plus the 3 s margin. [D-343]

`shutdown(timeout, unit)` returns within the timeout plus 3 s when `onStop` callbacks and owned resources return at once, and `docs/api/lifecycle.md` records the 3 s margin with its parts (TinyHttpd stop overrun up to 1.5 s, adapter release up to 1 s, 0.5 s slack) and keeps the statement that `onStop`, resource close and logger flush run without a time limit. Decision: the D-344 margin is 3 s and is the T44 tolerance. [D-344; wave decision: Shutdown bound (W2-010)]

A T44 test opens two WebSocket sessions whose clients stop reading while the server sends to them until their writes block, one healthy WebSocket session and one SSE stream over TinyHttpd, calls `shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` and asserts that it returns within 1 s plus 3 s, that the healthy session receives close `1001`, that the SSE client receives the closing notice and that both stalled sessions' client sockets are closed. [D-439; T44]

After `shutdown` returns, no live thread of that app remains, counted by name as the threads whose names start with `naruserve-` plus `tinyhttpd-acceptor-<port>` and `tinyhttpd-watchdog`, the WebSocket session registry and the SSE stream registry are empty, and the multipart temporary directory holds no file created by that app, which a test run in an isolated test JVM fork that starts no other app asserts after a run with open sessions, streams and an upload in progress (T44). Decision: the app's threads are counted by name in an isolated fork, as in PERF-APP-001 AC-1, because TinyHttpd's `tinyhttpd-watchdog` name carries no port. [D-345]

records.requirement: The system shall coordinate the WebSocket and SSE closing participants in the before-wait phase of shutdown by setting each registry's closed flag before its snapshot, passing each participant the shutdown deadline, running them while the adapter still accepts connections for at most 1 s with every request in that phase answered `503` with `Connection: close`, letting in-flight short requests complete before `onStop`, force-closing long connections still open at the deadline, returning from `shutdown(timeout, unit)` within the timeout plus a 3 s margin, and leaving no thread, queue or temporary upload file of the app behind.
records.rationale: Covers D-342, D-343, D-344, D-345, D-439, D-445 (shared ordering and the `res.sse()`/upgrade answers after the flag), D-446, carried loop-D fix V2-002 (D-445, D-446), wave decision Shutdown bound (W2-010) and residual Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003); test T44. The per-registry participants are FR-WS-010 and FR-SSE-005; this requirement holds what they share. Measured: `internal/ShutdownParticipants.java:33` has only `add(Phase, Runnable)` with no deadline; `internal/DefaultRestApp.java:544` computes `deadline = System.nanoTime() + unit.toNanos(timeout)` and `:610-636` runs before-wait participants, `adapter.stop(left(deadline))`, force-close participants, `onStop`, after-on-stop participants (FR-APP-011); the stopping gate answers `503` + `Connection: close` (FR-APP-013, D-166). Decision: `ShutdownParticipants` gains an add-only overload taking a package-private functional interface `void run(long deadlineNanos)`; existing `Runnable` participants are unchanged (the type is package-private, so the change is allowed). Decision: the D-344 margin is 3 s = TinyHttpd `stop(grace)` overrun up to 1.5 s (acceptor join up to 1000 ms plus worker wait up to 500 ms) + adapter release wait of D-107 up to 1 s + 0.5 s scheduling slack, recorded in `docs/api/lifecycle.md` and used as the T44 tolerance; W2-010: the bound covers the core and adapter waits of D-162 while `onStop`, resource close and logger flush return promptly, and `docs/api/lifecycle.md` keeps its statement that those steps run without a time limit. Deviation (recorded): object.md §11.4 step 2 stops accepting new connections and upgrades before the WebSocket and SSE goodbye of step 3; NaruServe runs the before-wait participants while TinyHttpd still accepts connections (at most 1 s) and answers every request reaching the dispatcher with `503` + `Connection: close` (D-446), which `docs/api/lifecycle.md` records. Pitfall: snapshotting before setting the flag lets a session or stream register between the two and miss the goodbye (D-445). Rejected alternative: stopping the TinyHttpd acceptor before the participants; TinyHttpd's stop also closes its upgraded connections at once without the 1001 close frame, reopen if TinyHttpd gains a separate stop-accepting call (D-020).

records.title: res.addCookie serialises one Set-Cookie header per call

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Response` declares `Response addCookie(Cookie)` returning the receiver; `addCookie(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; two calls add two `Set-Cookie` header lines in call order and never merge them. [D-203; T33] Decision: `addCookie` returns the response for chaining like `status` and `header`.

A cookie `sid=abc` with path `/`, domain `example.com`, `maxAge` 3600, secure, httpOnly and `SameSite.LAX` produces exactly `Set-Cookie: sid=abc; Path=/; Domain=example.com; Max-Age=3600; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`; a cookie with only name and value produces `sid=abc`; `SameSite.STRICT` and `SameSite.NONE` produce `SameSite=Strict` and `SameSite=None`. [D-203; T33] Decision: attributes appear in the order `Path`, `Domain`, `Max-Age`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`.

A cookie with `maxAge` 0, path `/` and domain `example.com` produces `Set-Cookie: sid=; Path=/; Domain=example.com; Max-Age=0` when its value is empty, which deletes the cookie in browsers. [D-204; T33]

records.title: Lenient request-cookie parsing behind req.cookie and req.getCookies

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `Cookie: a=1; b=2; a=3`, `req.cookie("a").getValue()` is `1`, `req.cookie("zz")` is `null` and `req.getCookies()` holds `a=1`, `b=2`, `a=3` in that order. records.title: Loopback default bind, explicit LAN binding with warning, Host allowlist and bind outcomes

acceptanceCriteria.text: Without `server(...)`, the adapter passes `InetAddress.getByName("127.0.0.1")` to TinyHttpd's `bindAddress` explicitly, the listening socket's local address is `127.0.0.1`, `ServerHandle.address()` returns `127.0.0.1`, and no class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` calls `InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()`. [D-211; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`; residual: D-211 wording]

With `server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))` the socket binds the wildcard address and `ServerHandle.address()` returns `0.0.0.0`; with a non-loopback local address `a` found through `NetworkInterface`, a connection to `a` is refused for the default app and accepted for an app bound to `0.0.0.0` (the case is skipped through JUnit `Assume` when the host has no such address). [D-212; T49; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`] Decision: `ServerHandle.address()` returns the configured bind address after a LAN bind.

`listen()` with a bind address outside `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1` and `localhost` logs exactly one `warn` record through the app logger that names the bind address and says the app must add its own authentication, whether or not global middleware is installed, and logs no such record for the default bind; the record contains no header value, cookie or token. [D-213; wave decision: The LAN warning is unconditional; I-016; T49] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-4 SDS-AC-10]: the warning is logged after the configuration freeze and before the adapter `bind` call.

Requests with `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`, `Host: localhost:<port>` and, after `allowedHosts("myphone.local")`, `Host: myphone.local` reach the handler, and when the bind address is a host name that name is added to the allowlist; `Host: evil.example` is answered `421` with the standard error body (code `HTTP_421`) rendered by the `ErrorHandler` of FR-ENGINE-005, and neither `onError` nor the access log records it. [D-214; D-418; D-405]
`listen(0)` binds an ephemeral port: `ServerHandle.port()` returns the port TinyHttpd reports through `getPort()`, which is positive, and a client connects to it. [D-221]

A second app calling `listen(p)` on the port `p` already bound by a first app throws `AppStartException` whose cause is a `java.net.BindException`; the second app passes `FAILED` and ends `TERMINATED` as FR-APP-010 defines for a failed start, no socket and no TinyHttpd or keeper thread of the second app remains, and the first app keeps serving. [D-222; FR-APP-010] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-5 SDS-AC-7]: when TinyHttpd `start()` throws `BindException` the adapter stops the half-built server and rethrows, and the keeper thread is started only after a successful start.

records.title: TinyHttpd request limits: header size, request line, header line, slowloris guards and body framing

acceptanceCriteria.text: With default settings a request whose header section exceeds 16384 bytes is answered `431`, and a request line of 8191 bytes (method, target and version together) is answered `414` while one of 8190 bytes is served. [D-215; T48] Decision: the default request-line limit is 8190 bytes and the header-size total is 16384 bytes.

`server(o -> o.maxRequestLineLength(n))` passes `maxRequestLineBytes = n` and `inputBufferBytes = max(8192, n + 2)` to the builder, so `n` = 1, 8190, 8191 and 65534 all build and start, and `n` = 65534 gives `inputBufferBytes` 65536. [D-414; residual: Upper bounds on size settings]

A single header line of 8191 bytes is answered with TinyHttpd's transport-level `431` under default settings even when the header total stays below `maxHeaderSize`, and raising `maxHeaderSize` alone does not raise that per-line limit, while `maxRequestLineLength(10000)` raises it to 10000 bytes. [D-437; D-400]

A request with 101 header fields is answered `431`; a client that sends part of the header section and then stops is closed after the header timeout (shortened through `headerTimeout` in the test) with TinyHttpd's `408`; and with `bodyReadTimeout` set to 1 s in the test (below the 5 s grace of the body-rate guard, which otherwise ends a stalled body first) a body that stops arriving is answered `408` with `Connection: close` after the body-read timeout. [D-216; T48]

A body drip-fed at about 10 bytes per second to a route that reads it is answered `408` with `Connection: close` once TinyHttpd's 5 s body-wait grace has passed, and the connection is then closed; the adapter sets `minRequestBodyRate` from `minBodyRate` (default 240). [D-413; D-219; T48]

A request carrying both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is answered `400` by TinyHttpd's parser before dispatch, and no handler, `onError` or access-log line runs for it. [D-217; D-400; T48]

The adapter never calls `maxRequestBodyBytes` or `maxDrainBytes` on the builder, so a body larger than the JSON limit is answered `413` by the core through `onError` with the standard error body and one access-log line, and a body that no handler reads is drained by TinyHttpd up to 65536 bytes before the connection is reused or closed. [D-443; D-088; D-188]

records.title: Connection limits, derived wait queue and bounded worker pool on TinyHttpd

acceptanceCriteria.text: With default settings the adapter passes `maxWorkers` 192, `maxEventStreams` 128 (from `maxSseStreams`), `maxConnections` 512, `maxUpgradedConnections` 128 and `maxConnectionsPerAddress` 256 to the builder, which a test reads back through a package-private accessor of the built configuration, so the derived wait queue is 320 and open connections total at most 640. [D-404; D-210] Decision: TinyHttpd's own `maxEventStreams` (default 64) is set to the SSE stream limit so the effective limit is 128.

`server(o -> o.maxWorkers(4).maxSseStreams(2).maxConnections(5))` makes `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names `maxConnections`, `maxWorkers` and `maxSseStreams` with their values from the configuration freeze of FR-APP-009 (after the `onStart` callbacks, before any `bind` call), so the app ends `FAILED` and then `TERMINATED` as FR-APP-010 defines for a failed freeze, TinyHttpd's builder is never called and no socket opens; `maxConnections(6)` with the same values starts. [D-415; FR-APP-009; FR-APP-010] Decision: the check is part of the existing freeze step and its exception reaches the caller unwrapped like the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`.

With `maxWorkers(1)`, `maxSseStreams(1)` and `maxConnections(2)` (wait queue 0), two connections held open by blocking handlers occupy both workers and a third connection is answered TinyHttpd's plain-text `503` at socket level, which reaches neither `onError` nor the access log. [D-218; D-400]
With `maxConnectionsPerAddress(2)`, a third concurrent connection from `127.0.0.1` is refused by TinyHttpd while the first two are served. [D-404]

records.requirement: The system shall map the connection settings onto TinyHttpd's builder with `maxWorkers` equal to the HTTP worker budget plus the SSE stream limit (64 + 128 = 192 by default), `maxConnections` 512, `maxUpgradedConnections` 128 and `maxConnectionsPerAddress` 256, derive the wait queue as `maxConnections - maxWorkers` (320 by default) instead of configuring it, make `listen()` fail with a configuration error before TinyHttpd's builder runs when `maxConnections` is below the worker budget plus the SSE stream limit, and use TinyHttpd's bounded worker pool, whose full wait queue answers TinyHttpd's plain socket-level `503`.
records.rationale: Covers D-404, D-415 and D-218. Measured fact: TinyHttpd has no queue setter; its `WorkerPool` holds up to `maxConnections - maxWorkers` waiting connections, `build()` requires `maxConnections >= maxWorkers`, and a connection that cannot enter the full queue gets the prebuilt `503` with `Retry-After: 1` from `HttpServer.reject`. The defaults let the T26 load from one loopback address fit (256 per address). Rejected alternative: a separate queue-length setting (TinyHttpd cannot honour it independently).

records.title: TinyHttpd error mapping, ErrorHandler, transport-level rejections and log routing

acceptanceCriteria.text: The adapter's request-body stream turns TinyHttpd's `BodyTooLargeException` into `HttpException` `413`, a `SocketTimeoutException` into `HttpException` `408` and `TruncatedBodyException` and `MalformedBodyException` into `HttpException` `400`, each keeping the original as cause; the `413` branch is tested with a constructed `BodyTooLargeException`, and a truncated body (fewer bytes than `Content-Length` before the client closes its output) read by `req.body(...)` gives `400`. TinyHttpd's `ContentLengthExceededException`, raised only by the response stream when a handler writes past its declared length, is not mapped to a client status: it reaches the error path as a server error. [D-219; wave decision: The 413 branch of D-219 is a guard]

A standard error response with status `408` carries `Connection: close` and the adapter closes the connection after it, on every adapter path that produces it (the body-read timeout of D-216 and the slow-body guard of D-413). [D-219; D-413] Decision: the core error path adds `Connection: close` to every `408` it writes, and the standard messages for `408` and `421` are `Request Timeout` and `Misdirected Request`.

The adapter installs one `ErrorHandler` through the builder; for an error TinyHttpd raises after parsing and outside a NaruServe dispatch (the `Host` rejection of D-418 is the test case) it writes the status, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the body from `ServerSettings.errorRenderer()` (for `421`: code `HTTP_421`, message `Misdirected Request`), so two such responses carry two different request ids. [D-405; D-418]

The pre-dispatch rejections of D-400 tested here — an invalid request line (`400`), a request line over the limit (`414`), a header section over the limit (`431`), `HTTP/2.0` (`505`) and a header timeout (`408`) — are answered by TinyHttpd's fixed plain-text responses, and a recording `onError` and the access log record nothing for them. [D-400]

`CONNECT / HTTP/1.1` reaches the dispatcher and is answered with its unsupported-method `501` and one access-log line, while `CONNECT example.com:443 HTTP/1.1` is answered by TinyHttpd's transport-level `501` with no access-log line. [D-422; D-400]

The adapter passes TinyHttpd a `TinyLog` that writes through `ServerSettings.logger()`, mapping `SEVERE` to `error`, `WARNING` to `warn`, `INFO` to `info`, `CONFIG` and `FINE` to `debug` and `FINER` and `FINEST` to `trace`, with the throwable passed to `error(String, Throwable)`; a TinyHttpd warning appears in a recording app logger, and an app logger that throws does not stop the server from answering the next request. [D-220; wave decision: The adapter gets the safe logger] Decision: `isLoggable` returns `true` for every level and the app logger filters. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-6 SDS-AC-6]: below `SEVERE` (for example `WARNING`) a throwable is appended to the text as `message + ": " + throwable`, because `Logger` has no `warn(String, Throwable)`.
