records.title: TinyHttpd stop, release, keep-alive shutdown behaviour and the non-daemon keeper thread

acceptanceCriteria.text: `app.shutdown(t, unit)` calls the adapter's `stop` once, which calls TinyHttpd's `stop(graceMillis)` with the milliseconds left until the deadline of D-162 (at most `t` converted, never negative), so in-flight requests may complete until the deadline and are force-closed only there; because `stop` closes the listening sockets before it waits, TinyHttpd's join tail after the deadline stays small, and a test asserts that `stop` returns within the deadline plus 1500 ms; the final `release` calls `awaitTermination` with at most 1000 ms. [D-223; D-107; D-162; FR-APP-011] Decision: the adapter passes the full time left as grace, as D-223 states, and its fixed release margin is 1 second.

After shutdown returns, no thread of that app is alive: TinyHttpd's worker threads come from a `ThreadFactory` the adapter passes to the builder, which keeps TinyHttpd's default worker properties (daemon, the configured worker stack size of 256 KiB, an uncaught-exception handler that logs through `ServerSettings.logger().error(String, Throwable)`), names each thread `naruserve-<port>-worker-<n>` and reads the bound port when it creates the thread (so `listen(0)` names the real port); the acceptor is identified by TinyHttpd's own name `tinyhttpd-acceptor-<port>`, the keeper thread by `naruserve-keeper-<port>`, and a test that starts one app at a time also finds no `tinyhttpd-watchdog` thread alive after `release`; tests use handlers that end when interrupted, and a worker that TinyHttpd reports as left after stop is logged as a warning by `release`. [D-223; I-015] Decision: worker names come from the adapter's thread factory; acceptor and watchdog names are TinyHttpd's fixed names.

A request sent on an idle keep-alive connection after `STOPPING` began receives either `503` with `Connection: close` or a connection closed without a response, and a response in flight when the stop begins is committed with `Connection: close`. [D-166; T44; wave-4 carried: TinyHttpd keep-alive socket case]

After a successful bind exactly one non-daemon thread named `naruserve-keeper-<port>` is alive and TinyHttpd's acceptor and worker threads are daemon; the keeper thread ends when the adapter stop begins and no keeper thread exists after a failed bind. [D-167; wave decision: Thread wording] Decision: the keeper thread is named `naruserve-keeper-<port>`.

A child JVM started by the test runs a `main` that calls `RestApp.create()`, registers a route that calls `app.shutdown`, calls `listen(0)`, prints the port and returns; the child process is still alive and serving 1 second after `main` returned, and exits by itself after the test requests the shutdown route. [D-167; T44]

records.title: Proxy trust through app.trustProxy applied by the core on every adapter

acceptanceCriteria.text: Without `trustProxy(true)`, a request with `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=198.51.100.1;proto=https` from `127.0.0.1` has `req.remoteAddress()` `127.0.0.1` and `req.isSecure()` `false` on both the in-memory and the TinyHttpd adapter, so FR-HTTP-011 AC-2 (the default configuration) stays true. [D-080; FR-HTTP-011]

After `app.trustProxy(true)`, `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.7, 10.0.0.1` gives `req.remoteAddress()` `203.0.113.7`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` gives `req.isSecure()` `true`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: http` gives `false`, and a request without these headers keeps the adapter's values. [D-080; D-225] Decision: trusted mode uses the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry and the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value, compared case-insensitively. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-4 SDS-AC-8]: the left-most `X-Forwarded-For` entry is trimmed of surrounding whitespace.

After `app.trustProxy(true)` the `Forwarded` header alone changes neither `remoteAddress()` nor `isSecure()`, and an empty or blank `X-Forwarded-For` entry keeps the adapter's remote address. [D-080] Decision: `Forwarded` is not interpreted in v1.

The trust decision is made in `DefaultRequest` from the app setting, so the in-memory adapter and the TinyHttpd adapter give identical `remoteAddress()` and `isSecure()` results for the same headers, and no adapter class reads `X-Forwarded-*` itself. [D-080; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

records.title: TinyHttpd adapter implements HttpAdapter with confined engine types and per-feature classes (wave 6)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `TinyHttpdAdapter` is a public final class with a public no-argument constructor implementing `HttpAdapter`, and reflection finds no `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` type in any public or protected constructor, method or field signature of any public class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`. [D-209] Decision: the adapter class is `com.snoworca.naruserve.tinyhttpd.TinyHttpdAdapter`. re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC1

The adapter core class sets every TinyHttpd builder limit of FR-ENGINE-003 and FR-ENGINE-004, while the exchange bridge and the file-transfer, event-stream and upgrade paths of `HttpExchange` are separate classes of the module: the exchange delegates them to the module class `TinyHttpdFeatures`, and each keeps the exchange's commit lock, abort check and single-start rule. From wave 6, `sendFile(status, headers, file, offset, length)` writes the status, the given headers and exactly `length` bytes of `file` starting at `offset` through a plain buffered copy (no zero-copy transfer) and throws no `UnsupportedOperationException`; a socket test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range. The event-stream and upgrade paths still throw `UnsupportedOperationException` naming wave 7, which adds them. Decision: the TinyHttpd `sendFile` hook fills D-106's extension point for apps that call it directly; the framework's own static, `res.file` and `res.download` bodies do not use it. [D-210; D-404; D-106; D-291; wave decision: File bodies come from the opened stream] Decision: a negative `offset`, a negative `length` or `offset + length` beyond the file length throws `IllegalArgumentException` before the response starts. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a file that shrinks during the copy throws `IOException` (EOF before `length` bytes) and leaves the exchange to the abort path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-2] Decision: `sendFile` commits through the exchange commit, so a second start throws `IllegalStateException` like `commit`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-9 SDS-AC-3] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC2 (file-transfer hook filled by wave 6)

No class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` references TinyHttpd's `TlsConfig` or calls the builder's `tls(...)` or a `listen(..., TlsConfig)` overload, which a class-reference test checks, and on the TinyHttpd adapter `req.isSecure()` returns `false` unless proxy trust of FR-ENGINE-008 reports `https`. [D-433; D-080] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC3

Over a real socket, `GET /a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and a request without `?` has a `null` raw query, because the adapter reads `getRequestURI()` and `getQueryString()` and never `getPath()`. [D-399; I-021; wave-3 carried: TinyHttpd halves] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC4

The adapter's request headers, method token, HTTP version and remote address reach the core unchanged, and the adapter's `boundPort()` throws `IllegalStateException` before bind like the SPI requires. [D-209; D-107] re_stated_from: FR-ENGINE-001#AC5

Covers D-209, D-210, D-404, D-106, D-291, D-433, D-080, D-399 and D-107 as restated from FR-ENGINE-010, with AC-2 changed by wave 7 (the event-stream and `webSocket` paths are filled; raw `upgrade` stays unsupported) and new AC-3 and AC-4 from wave decisions TinyHttpd feature hooks (W2-003; D-210) and maxEventStreams (W2-009; D-336). Carried note (r2 W1-002 / W1-001, D-408): TinyHttpd at 46b973e keeps only `Connection: close`/`keep-alive` on a non-`101` response (`ExchangeResponse.java:172-177`, `:466-470`), so the `426` answer's `Connection: Upgrade` cannot pass through this adapter; the D-020 TinyHttpd-gap issue is opened in the wave 7 ledger and D-408 stays below `verified` (FR-WS-004); this requirement does not patch TinyHttpd. Pitfall: holding the exchange lock for the whole WebSocket read loop or SSE drain would block every other call that synchronizes on the exchange for the life of the connection. Rejected alternative: TinyHttpd's `startEventStream()` (D-335: fixed `Cache-Control: no-cache` and a separate `retry` block). Tests to re-point to FR-ENGINE-011: every `FR_ENGINE_010_*` method of `AdapterSurfaceTest`, `RawTargetSocketTest`, `AbortSocketTest` and `SendFileSocketTest` in `NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/tinyhttpd/`; `AdapterSurfaceTest#FR_ENGINE_010_AC2_sendFileIsFilledAndTheOtherHooksThrowNamingWave7` is replaced by a test that asserts the event-stream and `webSocket` paths no longer throw and that raw `upgrade` throws with a message naming no wave; the `@req FR-ENGINE-001` (discarded id) and `@req FR-ENGINE-010` comments of `TinyHttpdExchange.java` and `TinyHttpdFeatures.java` move to FR-ENGINE-011.
- [2026-10-20] Correction: the `@req FR-ENGINE-001` (discarded id) and `@req FR-ENGINE-010` comments of `TinyHttpdExchange.java` and `TinyHttpdFeatures.java` move to FR-ENGINE-011. Raw `upgrade` stays unsupported on TinyHttpd in v1 (AC-2), so the replaced AdapterSurfaceTest asserts that `eventStream` and `webSocket` no longer throw and that `upgrade` throws with a message naming no wave. The D-408 gap is a deferred D-020 issue recorded by the orchestrator in the run's issue ledger.

records.title: In-memory HttpAdapter and test harness in the test fixtures

acceptanceCriteria.text: The in-memory adapter is a class under `NaruServe-api/src/testFixtures/java` implementing `HttpAdapter`, it is packaged in the `NaruServe-api` test-fixtures jar (CON-BUILD-006 AC-8), and `NaruServe-api`'s own tests use it. [D-108]

A request sent through the in-memory adapter passes through the same dispatcher, router, `Request` and `Response` code as an adapter in production, opens no socket, and returns the status, headers and body bytes the core wrote. [D-108]

The harness builds the internal `RestApp` implementation over the in-memory adapter, runs the route-table freeze once and then sends requests, and a registration error raised by the freeze reaches the test caller as the thrown exception. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-397] Decision: the harness `start()` rethrows the freeze's `RoutingConfigException` itself, unwrapped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-8]

The in-memory adapter passes the request-target path and query string to the core undecoded, so `GET /a%20b?q=%20` reaches `req.rawPath()` = `/a%20b` and the raw query `q=%20` (`req.query("q")` = ` `). [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves]

The in-memory adapter answers an authority-form `CONNECT host:443` request itself with `501` without calling the dispatcher, mirroring TinyHttpd. [wave-3 carried: CONNECT authority-form; I-021] Decision: any `CONNECT` whose target does not start with `/` gets `501` with `Content-Length: 0`, and the `ExchangeHandler` is not called. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-9]

The in-memory adapter rewrites an absolute-form target such as `http://example.com/a?x=1` to raw path `/a` and raw query `x=1` before dispatch, mirroring TinyHttpd. [wave-3 carried: absolute-form target; I-021] Decision: of an absolute-form `scheme://authority/path?query` target only the path (or `/` when the path is empty) and the query are kept. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-10]
The in-memory adapter passes an asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` target to the core as raw path `*`, as TinyHttpd does. [D-442; I-021; loop D: V1-006/V2-004]

records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-1]

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with `Content-Length: 0` and an empty body without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no handler sees them; a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` records that it was never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422]
In every handler call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3 (until wave 4 adds the standard error body), an empty body. [D-395; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395; T02] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-3]

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]
A request with an unsupported method token is answered `501` with `Content-Length: 0` and, in wave 3, an empty body. [D-395]

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and, in wave 3, `Content-Length: 0`, asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-4]

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered in wave 3 with the same `426`, both headers and `Content-Length: 0`, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`; this is the dispatcher mapping that FR-HTTP-008 AC-7 relies on. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and `Content-Length: 0` in wave 3. [D-395] [T02]

records.title: Interim handler failure and unfinished-response handling

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with an empty body through the harness. [wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that throws a checked `IOException` after setting status `201` but before commit is answered `500` with an empty body. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: the status and headers the handler set are dropped and the `500` carries only `Content-Length: 0`; the exception is not rethrown to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-8]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a wave 3 handler can reach) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; wave decision: abort() after completion; wave decision: Interim failure handling]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()` yields `202` with `X-A: 1` and an empty body, and the response is `COMPLETED`. [wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: when the handler returns with the response `NEW` the dispatcher calls `end()`, and with it `STREAMING` it runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-10]

records.title: Internal RestApp implementation with deferred router build and freeze

acceptanceCriteria.text: The implementation is a public class in a package documented as internal and not part of the API contract, it implements `RestApp`, and it holds the router and the dispatcher. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-393] Decision: the implementation is public class `DefaultRestApp` in package `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal`, whose package javadoc states it is not API. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-14]
A registration with an invalid pattern (one that `RoutePattern.parse` rejects) throws at the registration call itself, before any freeze. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-047; D-048]

`app.get("/a/b", h)` followed by `app.routerPolicy(RouterPolicy.builder().mergeSlashes(true).build())` makes `GET /a//b` reach `h` after the harness freeze, showing the policy applies to registrations made before it. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; FR-ROUTE-006]

The `Router` is constructed only at the freeze, and a duplicate of D-044 surfaces as the freeze's `RoutingConfigException`, not at the second registration call. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-044] Decision: the freeze propagates the `RoutingConfigException` unchanged and leaves the app unfrozen, so `dispatcher()` keeps throwing `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-12]

After the harness freeze, `app.get(...)`, `app.route(Method, path, h)`, `app.route(MethodSet, path, h)` and `app.routerPolicy(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException`, and `RouteBuilder` registration methods (`get`, `put`, ...) throw `IllegalStateException` too, including on a builder obtained from `app.route(path)` before the freeze. [wave decision: Settings after the freeze] Decision: the internal WebSocket-route hook also throws `IllegalStateException` after the freeze, and a refused call records nothing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-3 SDS-AC-13]
No public static method or constructor in package `com.snoworca.naruserve` returns a `RestApp` in wave 3. [wave decision: Working app in wave 3; D-111]

The internal implementation (not the public `RestApp` interface) offers an internal WebSocket-route registration hook that records a WebSocket registration and passes it to `Router.addWebSocket` at the freeze; the test-fixtures harness uses it to register a WebSocket-only route, and wave 3 dispatches no handshake to that route (a matching upgrade request gets the same `426` as a plain `GET`) until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; wave decision: Working app in wave 3]

records.title: Request path, raw path and path parameter accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `GET /files/a%20b?x=1` matched by `/files/:name`, `req.path()` returns `/files/a b`. [D-073] Decision: `req.path()` percent-decodes the raw path once as UTF-8, keeps `+` as `+`, and applies no `mergeSlashes`, trailing-slash or case policy. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-1] Under `mergeSlashes(true)`, `GET /a//b` matched by `/a/b` gives `req.path()` = `/a//b` (the policy affects only route matching, not the decoded path). [wave 3 implementation decision]
For the same request `req.rawPath()` returns `/files/a%20b`, without `?x=1`. [D-074; wave decision: Remaining markers]
For the same request `req.param("name")` returns `a b`. [D-075]

`req.param("missing")` for a name not in the matched pattern throws an exception instead of returning `null`. [D-075] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException` and its message contains the name. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-2]

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-3]

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave decision: Interim failure handling] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse throw `IllegalArgumentException`, which the dispatcher answers `400` with `Content-Length: 0` before the handler runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Header, remote address, secure flag and Last-Event-ID accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: With headers `X-Tag: a` and `x-tag: b`, `req.header("X-TAG")` returns `a`, `req.headers("x-Tag")` returns `[a, b]`, `req.header("None")` returns `null` and `req.headers("None")` returns an empty list. [D-079; T07] Decision: the empty list returned for no match is unmodifiable. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-5]

With the in-memory adapter reporting remote address `10.0.0.5` and secure `false`, a request carrying `X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4`, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` and `Forwarded: for=1.2.3.4;proto=https` still yields `req.remoteAddress()` = `10.0.0.5` and `req.isSecure()` = `false`. [D-080]

`req.lastEventId()` returns `42` for header `Last-Event-ID: 42` and `null` when the header is absent. [D-081] Decision: when `Last-Event-ID` appears more than once the first value is returned. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: Per-request concurrent attribute store

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `req.attribute("user", u)`, `req.attribute("user", User.class)` returns `u`, and `req.attribute("none", User.class)` returns `null`. [D-082]
An attribute stored while handling one request is not visible through `attribute(key, type)` of a second request, including two requests handled concurrently. [D-082]
Eight threads writing distinct keys to the same request's attributes concurrently leave every key readable with its value and no exception. [D-083]

With a typed `null` variable `Object v = null`, `req.attribute("k", v)` removes `k`, so a later `req.attribute("k", Object.class)` returns `null`; the value parameter is annotated `@Nullable`. [wave decision: Null attribute values; D-072]
`req.attribute("k", Integer.class)` with a stored `String` throws `ClassCastException`. [wave decision: Remaining markers]

records.title: Response chaining and default status

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.status(201)` and `res.header("X-A", "1")` each return the same `Response` instance they were called on, so `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` yields `201` with `X-A: 1`. [D-089] Decision: `header` with a name already present in another case replaces that entry, keeping one header of the name, as Express `res.set` does. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-1] `res.status(code)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a code outside 100–999 (Express 5 parity), and this range check runs before the response-state check. [wave 3 implementation decision]
A handler that calls only `res.send("ok")` yields status `200`. [D-090]

records.title: Response body writers send, html, stream and end

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.send("hé")` writes the UTF-8 bytes `68 C3 A9` with `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8`, and after `res.header("Content-Type", "text/csv")` it keeps `text/csv`. [D-091] Decision: a body writer adds its default `Content-Type` only when no `Content-Type` header is set, compared case-insensitively. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-2]

`res.html("

é

")` writes UTF-8 bytes with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8`. [D-092]

`res.send(new byte[]{0, (byte) 0xFF, 10})` writes exactly those three bytes with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` when none was set, and keeps an explicitly set `Content-Type`. [D-093; wave decision: Remaining markers]

`res.stream(in, "application/pdf")` with a 1 MiB input writes all bytes in order with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, and a counting input stream shows that every `read(byte[], int, int)` call requests fewer bytes than the 1 MiB input. [D-094] Decision: the copy reads with an 8192-byte buffer and writes each chunk to the exchange output stream in order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-3]

`res.stream(...)` closes the input stream exactly once after a successful copy, after a read failure, and after `res.abort(...)` during the transfer, including when the handler already returned; the caller does not close it. [D-094; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: the single close is guarded by a compare-and-set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-4]

`res.end()` completes the response with the status and headers set so far and no body. [D-095] Decision: on a non-bodyless response `end()` commits with `Content-Length: 0`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-6]

`res.stream(InputStream, contentType)` does not block until the copy ends: it commits the response and returns, the copy to the end of the stream runs after the handler returns, and the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends; a test whose handler returns right after `res.stream(...)` observes the call return before the input is read to its end. [D-094; D-103; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: `stream` sets `Content-Type` to the argument, commits with unknown length, enters `STREAMING` and returns; the dispatcher runs the copy on the adapter thread after the handler returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Response commit flag, abort and header CR/LF rejection

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.isCommitted()` is `false` before any body write and `true` after `res.send("x")` handed the status and headers to the in-memory adapter. [D-096] Decision: `abort` before any commit leaves `isCommitted()` `false`, sets `ABORTED` and aborts the exchange without writing a status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-8]
`res.abort(new IOException("x"))` during a `stream(...)` transfer makes the in-memory adapter report the connection closed abnormally and leaves the response state `ABORTED`. [D-097]

`res.abort(...)` on a response that is already `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED` does nothing: no exception, the state is unchanged and the adapter sees no further close. [wave decision: abort() after completion]

`res.header("X\r\nY", "1")`, `res.header("X", "a\nb")` and `res.header("X", "a\rb")` each throw an exception and add no header. [D-098] Decision: the exception is `IllegalArgumentException`, the header list stays unchanged, and the response-state check runs first. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-7] Besides CR and LF, `res.header` also throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a name that is not an RFC 9110 token (empty, or a char outside tchar) and for a value holding any control character other than HTAB (such as NUL or DEL) or any char above U+00FF. [wave 3 implementation decision]

records.title: Response state machine with single commit

acceptanceCriteria.text: A response starts in `NEW`, is `COMMITTED` once status and headers are handed to the adapter, and reaches `COMPLETED` after `send`; the adapter receives the status line and headers exactly once. [D-099]

`res.status(500)` or `res.header("X", "1")` after `res.send("a")` committed the response throws an exception and the sent status and headers stay unchanged. [D-100] Decision: the exception is `IllegalStateException` naming the current state, thrown in `COMMITTED`, `STREAMING`, `COMPLETED` or `ABORTED`, and nothing changes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-10]
A second body call (`send`, `html`, `stream` or `end`) after a body was sent throws an exception and writes no further bytes. [D-101]

After `res.stream(...)` returns, the response is `STREAMING` until the copy ends, then `COMPLETED`, or `ABORTED` on abort; a read failure of the input stream during the copy, including after the handler returned, ends the response `ABORTED` with the input stream closed (FR-HTTP-014 AC-5). [D-103; D-097; wave decision: stream() closing] Decision: a read failure during the copy sets `ABORTED`, calls `exchange.abort()` and closes the input, without rethrowing to the adapter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-11]

While the response is `STREAMING` (committed but not completed), `res.status(500)` and `res.header("X", "1")` each throw an exception and the status and headers the adapter received stay unchanged. [D-100; D-099]

records.rationale: Covers D-099, D-100, D-101 and D-103 and the wave decision on `stream()` closing. D-100 applies to `addCookie` and `cache` once waves 5 and 6 add them; among the streaming responses only `stream` exists in wave 3.

records.title: Bodyless 204, 304 and HEAD responses

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that calls `res.status(204).send("x")` yields `204` with zero body bytes through the in-memory adapter. [D-102] Decision: a `204` or `304` response commits with length 0, adds no `Content-Length` header and drops the body bytes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-12]
A handler that calls `res.status(304).send(new byte[]{1, 2})` yields `304` with zero body bytes. [D-102]

An explicit `HEAD /h` route whose handler calls `res.send("body")` yields its status and headers with zero body bytes. [D-102] Decision: a `HEAD` response sends the `Content-Length` the body would have had and writes zero body bytes; a `HEAD` `stream` closes the input without copying. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-5 SDS-AC-13]
The automatic `204` answers of `OPTIONS` and `OPTIONS *` carry zero body bytes. [D-102; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

records.title: Mutation after completion throws while read accessors stay usable

acceptanceCriteria.text: After `res.send("a")` completed the response, `res.status(201)`, `res.header("X", "1")`, `res.send("b")`, `res.html("c")`, `res.send(new byte[0])`, `res.stream(in, "text/plain")` and `res.end()` each throw `IllegalStateException`. [D-084]

After completion, `res.abort(...)` returns without exception and changes nothing. [D-084; wave decision: abort() after completion]

records.title: Request body ownership with BodyState and BodyAlreadyConsumedException

acceptanceCriteria.text: `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` is a public class in `com.snoworca.naruserve` extending `RuntimeException`. [D-086; wave decision: Body ownership]

`BodyState` is an internal class whose state is `UNREAD` initially, `PARSING` while a reader holds the body, and `CONSUMED` after a completed read or `CLOSED` after the body was closed; a unit test drives each transition. [D-085] Decision: `close` moves to `CLOSED` from any state, and a later `begin` or shared parse throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-11]

A unit test acquiring the body through `BodyState` after a first read gets `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` when the second read is of a different kind (JSON, form/multipart or raw) or is a second JSON or raw read; the shared form/multipart parse of AC-4 is the only exemption. [D-086] Decision: `begin` in any state other than `UNREAD` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` naming the current state. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-9]

A unit test acquiring the shared form/multipart parse through `BodyState` repeatedly gets the same parse result each time without a second read of the stream and without `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [D-087] Decision: the shared parse after `begin`, or `begin` after the shared parse, throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`; a parser failure leaves `CONSUMED` with no cached result and later calls throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-10]
A reflection test finds no public body-reading method on `Request` at the wave 3 merge (wave 5 adds the body readers). [wave decision: Body ownership]

records.requirement: The system shall track each request body with an internal `BodyState` moving from `UNREAD` through `PARSING` to `CONSUMED` or `CLOSED`, throw the public unchecked `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` of package `com.snoworca.naruserve` for any body read after the first one, and let repeated `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` reads share one parse as the only exemption. Wave 3 exposes no public body-reading method.
records.rationale: Covers D-085, D-086, D-087 and the wave decision on body ownership (W2-004; I-012). The JSON, form, multipart and raw readers arrive in waves 5 and 6, so wave 3 tests these rules through `BodyState` directly; the raw kind is an internal consumer of the body stream.

records.title: Limit-enforcing request body input stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stream is constructed from the source stream, a limit and an optional declared `Content-Length`; constructing it with limit `0` or a negative limit throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-088; wave decision: Body ownership]
With limit `10`, reading a 10-byte source returns all 10 bytes and end of stream without error. [D-088]

With limit `10`, reading an 11-byte source without a declared `Content-Length` (a chunked-style source of unknown length) throws the internal over-limit `IOException` subclass (a type distinct from plain `IOException`, named by the implementer) on the read that would return byte 11, and no byte beyond the limit is returned. [D-088] Decision: the over-limit type is `BodyTooLargeException`, and the stream reads at most limit+1 bytes from the source. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-4 SDS-AC-12]

With limit `10` and a declared `Content-Length` of `11`, the first read throws the same internal over-limit `IOException` subclass without reading any byte from the source, so the waves that add body readers can tell it from a transport `IOException` and answer `413`. records.title: Dispatcher pipeline and pre-request checks before route lookup (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a `GET /users/7` request with `app.get("/users/:id", h)` registered reaches `h` once with a `Request` and a `Response`, and the status, headers and body `h` wrote come back through the in-memory adapter. [D-394; D-397]

With a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)`, `OPTIONS *` is answered `204` before path validation (so `*` is not rejected with `400`), and a validator rejection happens before the router lookup: `GET /%2e%2e` and `GET /a%2Fb` (both rejected by the `PathValidator`) are answered `400`, no lookup exception escapes, and `h` registered on the matching pattern `/:x` records no call. [wave decision: Order before lookup; D-442; D-052] Decision: the dispatcher checks in this order: `OPTIONS` with raw path `*` gives `204`, any raw path not starting with `/` gives `400`, a `PathValidator` rejection gives `400`, then the router lookup runs. This order applies to requests that passed the lifecycle gate; the unrecognised-method-token `501` comes after the validator check and before a `Request` is built.

A raw path that the wave 2 `PathValidator` rejects is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`, `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8`) without a router lookup, and the validator sees the raw form with a single decoding: `/%2e%2e` and `/a%2Fb` are answered `400`, while `/%252e%252e` reaches a `/:x` route with `req.param("x")` = `%2e%2e`. [wave-3 carried: path validator before lookup; D-052; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: a pre-request `400` or `501` carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and the `Content-Length` of the standard body; for a `HEAD` method token the `Content-Length` is kept and no body bytes are written. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-14]

An unrecognised method token is answered `501`, a raw path not starting with `/` `400`, a validator rejection `400` and `OPTIONS *` `204`, each before a `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them; a recording global middleware, a recording `onError` and a recording handler registered through `app.route(Method.any(), "/", h)` and `app.route(Method.any(), "/:x", h)` record that they were never called. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; D-422; wave decision: Pre-request rejections]
In every handler and middleware call `req.method()` returns a non-null `Method` and `req.path()` a non-null decoded path. [wave-3 residual: pre-request rejections; I-014]
The HTTP-level assertions of T01, T02, T03, T05 and T06 run as tests through the in-memory adapter and the harness in `./gradlew build`. [D-397]

records.requirement: The system shall provide a dispatcher that takes each exchange from an `HttpAdapter` that passed the lifecycle gate of FR-APP-009 and FR-APP-013, checks the asterisk-form `OPTIONS *` first, then rejects a raw path not starting with `/` with `400`, then rejects a raw path refused by the wave 2 path validator with `400`, and only then calls the router lookup and either runs the middleware pipeline and the matched `RouteHandler` with a `Request` and a `Response` or writes the automatic response, where the pre-request rejections are answered before any `Request` is built, so no middleware, handler or `onError` sees them, and the two `400` rejections carry the standard error body.

records.title: Automatic responses for router lookup results with the standard error body (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the harness, a request whose path matches no route is answered `404` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `NOT_FOUND`). [D-395; wave-4 carried: standard error body; D-134] Decision: the fallback answers only a response that is still `NEW`, through the request's `Response`, keeping the headers a middleware set; a response that is no longer `NEW` is left as it is. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-4 SDS-AC-15]

With only `POST /p` registered, `GET /p` is answered `405` with `Allow` listing `POST, OPTIONS`, and with `GET /r` registered `DELETE /r` is answered `405` with `Allow` including the automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, both with the standard error body (`code` `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). [D-395; T02; D-134] Decision: the `Allow` value joins the allowed methods (or `Method.any()` for `OPTIONS *`) with `, ` in `MethodSet` iteration (`Method` declaration) order.

With `GET /r` and `POST /r` registered and no `OPTIONS` route, `OPTIONS /r` is answered `204` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, OPTIONS`, no body and no `Content-Length` header. [D-395; T05; wave decision: Automatic response bodies]

`TRACE /x` with `TRACE` disabled and `CONNECT /` with `CONNECT` disabled are each answered `501` with the standard error body (`code` `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`) after the global middleware ran, while a request with an unrecognised method token (FR-ROUTE-013) is answered `501` with the standard error body before any `Request` is built, as FR-HTTP-021 AC-4 states. [D-395; wave decision: 426 and 501; wave decision: Pre-request rejections; D-422] Decision: the dispatcher tells the two cases apart by whether the method token parses to a `Method` value.

With a WebSocket-only route registered through the internal hook of FR-HTTP-008 AC-7, a plain `GET` to that path is answered `426` with headers `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` and the standard error body (`code` `UPGRADE_REQUIRED`), asserted through the in-memory adapter. [D-395; T06; wave decision: 426 over TinyHttpd; wave decision: 426 and 501] Decision: the upgrade flag passed to the lookup is `Router.isWebSocketUpgrade(token, Connection, Upgrade)` with each header's values joined by `, `.

With the same WebSocket-only hook route, a `GET` carrying `Upgrade: websocket` and `Connection: Upgrade` (for which the router returns a `MATCHED` result with route kind `WEBSOCKET`) is answered with the same `426`, both headers and the standard error body, and no handshake is attempted, until wave 7 adds `app.ws`. [D-395; T06; FR-ROUTE-015]

After `app.route(Method.any().except(Method.DELETE), "/t", h)`, `DELETE /t` through the in-memory harness is answered `405` with `Allow` = `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS` (the router's `Method` declaration order, FR-ROUTE-010 AC-1) and the standard error body. [D-395; T02]

A recording global middleware runs once before each of the `404`, `405`, `426`, automatic `OPTIONS` and disabled-`TRACE`/`CONNECT` `501` answers above and not for the unrecognised-token `501`, and a recording `onError` records no call for any of them. [wave decision: Pre-request rejections; residual: onError scope; D-117]

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler that throws `RuntimeException` before writing anything is answered `500` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) through the harness when no `onError` is registered. [D-127; D-132; wave-4 carried: interim failure handling replaced]

A handler that throws after commit while the response is `STREAMING` (the only committed-but-incomplete state a handler can reach before wave 5) leaves the response `ABORTED` and the in-memory adapter reports the exchange closed abnormally instead of a `500`; a handler that throws after the response is `COMPLETED` (for example after `res.send("x")`) leaves it `COMPLETED`, because abort is a no-op there, with the sent bytes unchanged and no `500`. [D-097; D-099; D-131; wave decision: abort() after completion]

A handler that sets `status(202)` and `header("X-A", "1")` and returns without a body write or `end()`, and a middleware that returns without responding or calling `next.run()`, each yield the status and headers set so far (`202` with `X-A: 1`, and `200` for the middleware case) with an empty body, the response is `COMPLETED`, and the app logger received one `warn` naming the method and path. [D-126] Decision: the finishing behaviour is a `warn` through the app logger followed by `end()`; with the response `STREAMING` the dispatcher runs the pending stream copy on the same adapter thread and logs no warning.

records.title: Query accessors with form-urlencoded decoding and malformed-query 400 through the error path (wave 4)

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `?a=1&a=2&b=3`, `req.query("a")` returns `1`, `req.queries("a")` returns `[1, 2]`, `req.query("c")` returns `null` and `req.queries("c")` returns an empty list. [D-076; T07]

For `?q=a+b%20c&%ED%95%9C=%EA%B8%80`, `req.query("q")` returns `a b c` and `req.query("한")` returns `글`. [D-077; T07] Decision: a pair without `=` has the empty string as its value, empty names are kept, and names and values decode `+` as space.

A query `?x=%zz`, a query `?x=%E0%A4` (truncated UTF-8) and a query `?x=%C3%28` (invalid UTF-8) are each answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (`code` `BAD_REQUEST`) and the matched handler is not called. [D-078; T07; wave-4 carried: malformed query reaches middleware and onError] Decision: a malformed `%XX` or bytes that are not valid UTF-8 (decoder `CodingErrorAction.REPORT`) make the query parse raise `HttpException` with status `400`; the dispatcher parses the query after the middleware ran and before the handler, so global and prefix middleware run, a middleware that reads `req.query(...)` receives that exception, and it reaches `onError` through the error path of FR-APP-005. The query is parsed after the route middleware ran and before the handler; a request without a matched route gets the fallback answer (`404`, `405`, ...) and its query is parsed only if a middleware reads it.

records.title: req.body media-type, syntax, size, depth, UTF-8 and polymorphism checks

acceptanceCriteria.text: Bodies with `Content-Type` `application/json`, `application/json; charset=utf-8`, `application/problem+json` and `APPLICATION/JSON` are decoded, while `text/plain`, `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `application/jsonx`, `application/json; charset=iso-8859-1` and a missing `Content-Type` make `req.body(...)` throw `UnsupportedMediaTypeException`, answered `415` with the standard error body (code `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`) without calling the codec. [D-186; T09] Decision: an allowed type is `application/json` or `application/<subtype>+json`, compared case-insensitively, with no `charset` parameter or `charset=utf-8`. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-7]: the media type is checked before the codec is called or the body stream is read.

The bodies `{"a":`, `[1,]`, an empty body and a body of only spaces and newlines are each answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`; the empty and whitespace-only bodies never reach the codec, and an `IOException` thrown by `JsonCodec.decode` is turned into `HttpException` `400` with that exception as cause unless AC-9 applies. [D-187; T09; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`] Decision: the core maps a codec `IOException` to `400` and lets an unchecked codec exception reach the error path as `500`.
With the default codec, `{"a":1} x` and `{} {}` are answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; D-187; T09]

A body of 1048577 bytes with `Content-Length` is answered `413` with code `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` before the codec reads it, and a chunked body without `Content-Length` larger than the limit, decoded through the default `GsonJsonCodec`, is answered `413` (not `400`) after at most limit + 1 bytes were taken from the exchange stream; with `app.jsonLimit(10)` an 11-byte body gives `413` and a 10-byte body is decoded. [D-188; D-088; T09]
With the default codec, an array nested 65 levels deep is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST` and one nested 64 levels deep is decoded. [D-189; T09]

A body holding the bytes `{"a":"` `0xC3 0x28` `"}` or a truncated UTF-8 sequence is answered `400` with code `BAD_REQUEST`, because the core decodes the body with a UTF-8 decoder whose malformed and unmappable actions are `REPORT`. [D-190]

Decoding `{"@class":"<canary class>","class":"<canary class>","@type":"<canary class>"}` into `Object.class` with the default codec returns a `Map` and never initialises the canary class, whose static initializer records any loading. [D-191]
The bodies `null` and ` null ` decoded with `req.body(User.class)` and with `req.body(new TypeRef<List<User>>() {})` return `null`. [D-431; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

When decoding fails and the core's size-limited stream recorded an overrun (its internal `BodyTooLargeException`, an `IOException` that a codec such as Gson may wrap), the core answers `HttpException` `413`; when the failure's cause chain holds an `HttpException` (for example the adapter `408` of FR-ENGINE-005), that exception is rethrown with its own status; each failure of this requirement reaches `onError` and the access log like any handler exception of FR-APP-005. [D-186; D-187; D-188; D-219] Decision: the overrun is detected from the limited stream's state, not only from the exception the codec rethrows. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-11]: an `HttpException` found in the cause chain is rethrown unchanged (the same instance).

records.rationale: Covers D-186, D-187, D-188, D-189, D-190, D-191 and D-431 with the wave decision "A JSON `null` decodes to `null`" (empty body is `400`, not `null`) and the residual "Trailing JSON data" (T09 cases `{"a":1} x` and `{} {}`). records.title: res.json encodes through the app codec and round-trips JSON values

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.json(value)` calls the app codec's `encode` once and sends status 200 (or the status set before) with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a `Content-Length` equal to the encoded byte count. [D-193]

A T08 echo route `res.json(req.body(type))` returns values equal to the sent ones for a POJO `User`, a `List<User>` read through `TypeRef`, the string `"x"`, the numbers `42` and `1.5`, `true` and `null`, while `{"n":42}` read with `req.body(Map.class)` comes back as JSON equal to `{"n":42.0}`, which the test compares as JSON values. [D-194; T08]
`res.json("hello")` sends exactly the 7 bytes `"hello"` and `res.json(null)` sends exactly `null`. [D-195]

A codec whose `encode` writes part of the output and then throws leaves the response uncommitted, and the request is answered `500` with exactly the standard error body of FR-APP-006 and no byte of the partial output. [D-136; D-112; wave-4 carried: res.json serialisation failure] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-12]: `res.json` encodes into a buffer that is discarded when `encode` throws, so the response stays `NEW` and the error path answers `500`.

`res.json(value)` on a response that is already committed or completed throws `IllegalStateException` before calling the codec; on a committed but not completed response (committed in the test through the internal response, as the wave 4 error-path tests do) the error path of FR-APP-005 aborts it, so the client sees an abnormally closed response and no standard error body, and on a completed response the client response stays as completed and nothing more is written. [D-136; FR-APP-005; FR-HTTP-016; wave-4 carried: a committed response is aborted]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `res.json(mapOf("success" to true))` inside a route lambda. [D-193; C-03; I-010]

records.requirement: The system shall make `res.json(value)` encode `value` through the app codec into a buffer and then send it with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8` and a matching `Content-Length`, so that POJOs, `List<User>`, strings, numbers, booleans and `null` round-trip unchanged through `req.body` and `res.json` and an encoding failure is handled before the response commits.
records.rationale: Covers D-193, D-194, D-195 and the wave 4 carried case of D-136 and D-112 (`carried-into-wave-5.md`). Encoding into a buffer first means a serialisation exception always happens while the response is uncommitted, so the standard error response of FR-APP-006 replaces it and no partial JSON reaches the client; the committed case is a `res.json` call on a response that is already committed, which the error path of FR-APP-005 handles by the response state. Measured fact recorded in `docs/api/request.md`: the default Gson decodes untyped numbers as `Double`, so an untyped `Map` round-trips to JSON-value equality only.

records.title: GsonJsonCodec with STRICT, Unsafe-free defaults, a nesting limit and end-of-document check

acceptanceCriteria.text: `GsonJsonCodec` is public, final and implements `JsonCodec` with the public constructors `GsonJsonCodec()`, `GsonJsonCodec(Gson)` and `GsonJsonCodec(Gson, int maxDepth)` and the public static method `Gson defaultGson()`; a `null` `Gson` throws `NullPointerException` and a `maxDepth` below 1 or above 255 throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-196; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec] Decision: the depth setting is the constructor argument `maxDepth`, and `GsonJsonCodec()` uses `defaultGson()`. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-1]: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names `maxDepth`, and both exceptions are thrown before the instance keeps any state.

`defaultGson()` returns a `Gson` built with `Strictness.STRICT` and `disableJdkUnsafe()`: decoding `{a:1}`, `{'a':1}` and `{"a":1 /* c */}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` throws `IOException`, and through `req.body` each is answered `400`. [D-197; D-198]

Decoding `{}` with `new GsonJsonCodec()` into a class whose only constructor takes arguments throws an unchecked exception and creates no instance, and through `req.body` the request is answered `500`. [D-199] Decision: a codec failure that is not malformed input stays unchecked and gives `500`, because it is a server-side type error. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-3]: the unchecked exception is Gson's `JsonIOException`, propagated without wrapping.

`new GsonJsonCodec()` and `new GsonJsonCodec(customGson)` both reject an array nested 65 levels deep with `IOException` and decode one nested 64 levels; `new GsonJsonCodec(gson, 10)` rejects 11 levels and decodes 10. [D-189; wave decision: The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-4]: the nesting limit is set on the `JsonReader` on every `decode`, so it also holds for an instance built from a caller-supplied `Gson`.
`decode` of `{"a":1} x` and of `{} {}` throws `IOException`, while `decode` of `null` and of ` null ` returns `null`. [residual: Trailing JSON data; wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`]

Every malformed-input failure of `decode` (syntax, lenient construct, nesting, trailing data, wrong JSON type for the target) is thrown as `java.io.IOException` with the Gson exception as cause, and no `com.google.gson` type appears in a `GsonJsonCodec` method signature other than the constructor and `defaultGson()`. [D-187; D-196] Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-2 SDS-AC-6]: Gson's `JsonSyntaxException` and `MalformedJsonException` are rethrown as `java.io.IOException` with that cause, while `JsonIOException` stays unchecked (AC-3).
`encode(null, w)` writes `null`, `encode("hello", w)` writes `"hello"` and `encode` of a `List<User>` writes a JSON array through the configured `Gson`. [D-193; D-195]

`NaruServe-gson` main classes pass the animal-sniffer API 21 check and reference no TinyHttpd type, and a Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.jsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec(GsonJsonCodec.defaultGson(), 32))`. [C-02; I-001; C-03]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-gson` the public final class `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` implementing `JsonCodec`, built with a default `Gson` configured with `Strictness.STRICT` and `disableJdkUnsafe()` or with a caller-built `Gson`, that decodes through a `JsonReader` with a nesting limit of 64 by default for every instance, requires the end of the document after the value, returns `null` for a JSON `null` document and reports malformed input as `IOException`.
records.rationale: Covers D-196, D-197, D-198, D-199, the wave decision "The JSON depth limit lives in the Gson codec" and the residual "Trailing JSON data". Pitfalls: `Gson.fromJson(JsonReader, Type)` does not check for trailing input, so the codec must check `reader.peek() == END_DOCUMENT`; a caller-built `Gson` must not silently raise the nesting limit to Gson's 255; Gson's `JsonSyntaxException` is unchecked, so the codec converts malformed-input failures to `IOException` for the core's `400` mapping. Rejected alternative: a depth parameter on `JsonCodec.decode` (changes the frozen SPI signature of D-182).

records.title: Nullability check over the public API packages of NaruServe-api

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test in `NaruServe-api` fails, naming the package, when `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` or `com.snoworca.naruserve.routing` lacks `@NullMarked` on its package, and it also asserts that `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` keeps `@NullMarked` although the method-level checks skip that package. [D-348]

The same test parses the nullable-accessor table of `docs/api/kotlin.md` and, for every row whose Kotlin type column ends in `?`, finds every public overload of that name that returns a value (for example `Request.query`, `header`, `form`, `cookie`, `file`, `lastEventId`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `body(Class)` and `body(TypeRef)`; the void overload `attribute(String, Object)` is skipped) and fails when `getAnnotatedReturnType()` lacks `@Nullable`; for every row without `?` it fails when such an overload's return type is `@Nullable`. [D-348; D-351]

Reflection over every public class and interface of the three public API packages in the main jar named by `naruserve.apiJar` (not the test class path) finds no `org.jspecify.annotations.NonNull` on a type, member, parameter or type use, because under `@NullMarked` an unannotated reference type is non-null. [D-348]

The check is a reusable function that a negative fixture proves: a fixture package without `@NullMarked`, a fixture method that the table names without `@Nullable`, and a fixture member with `@NonNull` each make it fail with a message that names the package or member, so the check cannot pass vacuously. [D-348]

The check runs in `./gradlew build` (a unit test of `NaruServe-api`, not a manual step) and passes on the wave 8 API, and a public method added later by any wave is covered because the check enumerates the packages by reflection instead of listing methods. [D-348; I-010]

traceLinks.notes: the compileOnly JSpecify annotations that Kotlin reads

records.requirement: The system shall run, as part of `./gradlew build`, an automated check over the public API packages of `NaruServe-api` (`com.snoworca.naruserve`, `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi`, `com.snoworca.naruserve.routing`) that fails when a package lacks `@NullMarked`, when a method named in the nullable-accessor table of `docs/api/kotlin.md` lacks `@Nullable` on its return value, or when the public API carries `@NonNull`, so that every reference-typed return value and parameter of a public method has a nullability annotation by contract: non-null through the package default, nullable through `@Nullable`.
records.rationale: Covers D-348, wave decisions Nullability check (r1 W2-005) and its second reading (r2 W2-004), and the Kotlin-visible part of I-007 and I-010; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `package-info.java` of `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `.spi`, `.routing` and `.internal` each carries `@org.jspecify.annotations.NullMarked`; `grep -rn NonNull NaruServe-*/src/main` finds no `@NonNull` (only `Objects.requireNonNull`); the nullable `Request` accessors are `query`, `header`, `lastEventId`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `body(Class)`, `body(TypeRef)`, `cookie`, `form` and `file` (`Request.java:29-127`). Decision: "has a nullability annotation" is satisfied by the package default plus `@Nullable`, because under `@NullMarked` an unannotated reference type is non-null by contract and Kotlin reads it as `T`; no `@NonNull` exists. The round-1 test "a null-capable type without `@Nullable`" is dropped because it cannot be derived from signatures. Pitfall: the test class path of `NaruServe-api` also holds classes of package `com.snoworca.naruserve` (for example `NullabilityFixture`, which carries `@NonNull` on purpose, CON-BUILD-011 AC-2); every enumeration of this requirement and of FR-KT-002 and FR-KT-003 therefore reads the classes of the main jar given by the existing system property `naruserve.apiJar` (`build.gradle:179-183`), never the test class path. Pitfall: JSpecify `@Nullable` is a type-use annotation, so on `<T> @Nullable T attribute(...)` it sits on the return type, not the method; reflection must read `getAnnotatedReturnType()`. Rejected alternative: adding `@NonNull` to every signature; it is redundant under `@NullMarked` and the wave 1 convention (CON-BUILD-011) already drops it; reopen only if Kotlin stops reading the package default.

records.title: Public method names of NaruServe-api avoid the Kotlin hard keywords

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test in `NaruServe-api` enumerates by reflection, from the main jar named by `naruserve.apiJar`, every public and protected method of every public class, interface and enum of `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` and `com.snoworca.naruserve.routing`, including nested types, and fails with the message `Type.method` when a name is one of `as`, `fun`, `in`, `is`, `object`, `typealias`, `typeof`, `val`, `var` or `when`. [D-352]

The check is a reusable function proved by a negative fixture: a fixture type with a method named each of the ten words makes it fail once per word, and a fixture type with methods `get`, `set`, `use`, `value` and `isSecure` passes, so soft keywords and `is`-prefixed names are not flagged. [D-352]

The check passes on the wave 8 API and runs in `./gradlew build`; a Kotlin test calls one method of each of `RestApp`, `Request`, `Response`, `RouteBuilder` and `WebSocketSession` without a backtick. [D-352; I-010]

records.requirement: The system shall run, as part of `./gradlew build`, an automated check that fails, naming `Type.method`, when a public or protected method of a public type in the public API packages of `NaruServe-api` is named with a Kotlin hard keyword that is a legal Java identifier — `as`, `fun`, `in`, `is`, `object`, `typealias`, `typeof`, `val`, `var` or `when` — so that no Kotlin call needs backticks.
records.rationale: Covers D-352 and wave decision Kotlin keywords (r1 W2-006); supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): a source scan of the method declarations of `NaruServe-api/src/main/java` and the other published modules finds no method named with one of the ten words. Decision: the check list is the ten words that are Kotlin hard keywords and legal Java identifiers; the other Kotlin hard keywords (`break`, `class`, `do`, `else`, `for`, `if`, `interface`, `package`, `return`, `super`, `this`, `throw`, `try`, `while`, `continue`, `null`, `true`, `false`) are Java keywords or literals and cannot be method names. Pitfall: Kotlin soft and modifier keywords (`get`, `set`, `by`, `value`, `where`, `open`, `field`) are legal names and `app.get(...)` depends on it; adding them to the list would forbid the Express-style `get`. Pitfall: the rule is on method names only, because Java parameter names are invisible to Kotlin. Rejected alternative: also scanning every other published module; their public classes (`TinyHttpdAdapter`, `GsonJsonCodec`, loggers, servlet classes) are implementation classes that app code rarely calls; reopen if one of them gains a keyword-named public method.

records.title: Kotlin lambdas are accepted by every callback parameter without a DSL

acceptanceCriteria.text: A reflection test over the main jar named by `naruserve.apiJar` finds every interface declared in `com.snoworca.naruserve`, `.spi` or `.routing` that is the parameter type of a public method of those packages and has exactly one abstract method (ignoring `Object` methods and `default` methods) and fails, naming it, when it lacks `@FunctionalInterface`. [D-350; I-007]
The same test fails, naming the interface, when an interface that is a callback parameter type has no abstract method or more than one, which would stop Kotlin SAM conversion. [D-350]

A Kotlin test passes a lambda to each callback parameter of the matrix: `app.get`/`post`/`route` with `RouteHandler`, `app.use(path) { req, res, next -> }` with `Middleware`, `app.onError`, `app.onStart`, `app.onStop`, `app.server`, `app.multipart`, `app.webSocket`, `app.sse`, `app.ws`, `ws.onText`, `ws.onClose { code, reason -> }` and `res.sse().onClose { }`, each without a receiver DSL, and runs a request or session through the in-memory harness that reaches the lambda; the matrix covers every interface of the AC-1 inventory (16 on 2026-10-20, including the `WebSocketSession` listener types and the SPI types `ExchangeHandler`, `ErrorRenderer`, `StreamDrain` and `UpgradeHandler`, which the test implements as Kotlin lambdas). [D-350; T11]

A second Kotlin test fails the build when the Java reflection inventory of AC-1 names an interface that the Kotlin matrix of AC-3 does not list, by reading the Kotlin matrix from a `CALLBACK_TYPES` list in one shared test class that the Java inventory test compares with its reflection result, so the matrix cannot fall behind the API. [D-350; I-010]

records.requirement: The system shall accept a Kotlin lambda, without a DSL builder, for every callback parameter of the public API: each interface used as a callback parameter type of a public method is a Java functional interface annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with exactly one abstract method, and a Kotlin test passes a trailing lambda to each such parameter, for example `app.get("/x") { req, res -> }`.
records.rationale: Covers D-350 and the callback part of I-007 and I-010; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `@FunctionalInterface` appears 18 times in 14 files of `NaruServe-api/src/main/java`, on `RouteHandler`, `Middleware`, `ErrorHandler`, `LifecycleCallback`, `Configurer`, `WebSocketHandler`, the `SseClient` and `WebSocketSession` listener types, the SPI types `ExchangeHandler`, `ErrorRenderer`, `StreamDrain`, `UpgradeHandler` and the internal `ShutdownParticipants` and `MultipartParser` callbacks; earlier waves already compile lambdas for subsets in `HttpApiKotlinTest`, `AppEntryKotlinTest`, `WebSocketKotlinTest`, `SseKotlinTest` and `WaveSixKotlinTest`. Decision: the inventory test lists every interface that is a parameter type of a public method and has exactly one abstract method, and the Kotlin matrix names each of them, so a new callback type fails the build until it has a Kotlin lambda test. Pitfall: SAM conversion needs exactly one abstract method; a callback interface that gains a second abstract method silently loses lambda syntax in Kotlin (a `default` method does not). Rejected alternative: a Kotlin DSL builder (`routes { get("/x") { } }`); it is forbidden by C-03 and would put `kotlin.*` in Core.

records.title: Every Kotlin example of docs/api exists as a Kotlin test that compiles and runs

acceptanceCriteria.text: A docs test in `NaruServe-api` enumerates every ```kotlin block of every `docs/api/*.md` and fails, naming `<file>#<n>`, when the Kotlin test sources of `NaruServe-api` and `NaruServe-kotlin` hold no `// docs-example: <file>#<n>` marker for it (the test also reads `NaruServe-servlet/src/test/kotlin`, where the Kotlin example of `servlet.md` lives), and when a marker names a block that does not exist. [D-349]

Each marked test function (its extent runs from its marker line to the next marker line or the end of the file) contains every non-blank whitespace-normalised line of its block or the comment `// adapted: <reason>`, declares the app-defined types the block uses (`User`, `UserService`, `Todo` and so on) and runs in `./gradlew build` through the in-memory harness, asserting the outcome that the surrounding docs text states. [D-349; T11]

The `kotlin.md` early-exit blocks run and are asserted: `return@get` yields `404` for an unknown user, `return@use` yields `401` without `Authorization`, and the `if/else` expression form yields the same two outcomes without `return@`. [D-349]

The docs test is a reusable function proved by negative fixtures, so an inserted block without its marker and a stale marker each make it fail, and adding a kotlin block to any `docs/api` file in a later wave fails the build until its test exists. [D-349; I-008; I-010]

Each block runs in exactly one module with exactly one marker: blocks that use the `NaruServe-kotlin` extension (`req.body<User>()`) run in `NaruServe-kotlin`'s tests against the module extension of IR-KT-002, the other blocks run where the wave 5 and 7 docs Kotlin tests already hold them (`JsonDocsKotlinTest`, `SseDocsKotlinTest`, `WebSocketDocsKotlinTest` gain the markers), and only the test-local copy of `body()` in `JsonDocsKotlinTest` (wave 5, OPS-JSON-001 AC-5) stays untouched. records.rationale: Covers D-349, the Kotlin part of I-009 and I-010; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `docs/api/*.md` holds 45 ```kotlin blocks (`kotlin.md` 10, `websocket.md` 7, `sse.md` 5, `app.md`, `middleware.md`, `response.md` and `routing.md` 3 each, `json.md` and `request.md` 2 each, `cookie.md`, `express-migration.md`, `logging.md`, `multipart.md`, `static.md`, `README.md` and `lifecycle.md` 1 each); waves 5 and 7 already compile subsets in `JsonDocsKotlinTest`, `SseDocsKotlinTest` and `WebSocketDocsKotlinTest`. records.title: Kotlin test of every nullable accessor with safe-call syntax and every non-null accessor without it

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` calls `req.query("page")?.toIntOrNull() ?: 1`, `req.cookie("session")?.value`, `req.header("Authorization")`, `req.form("name")`, `req.file("file")?.save(...)`, `req.lastEventId()` and `req.attribute("k", String::class.java)` with declared nullable types, and asserts each returns `null` when the request lacks the value and the value when present. [D-351; T11]

The same test calls `req.param("id")` as `String` and asserts `IllegalArgumentException` for a name the pattern lacks, calls `req.queries("tag")` and `req.files("f")` as non-null lists and asserts an empty list when absent, and calls `req.service(UserService::class.java)` as `UserService` and asserts an exception when the service is not registered. [D-351]
The test calls `req.body(User::class.java)` as `User?` and asserts `null` for a JSON `null` body, and `req.body(object : TypeRef<List<User>>() {})` as `List<User>?`. [D-351; D-349]

Each table row of `docs/api/kotlin.md` maps to a test function named after the accessor, and a docs test fails, naming the row, when a row has no function, so a row added to the table is tested. [D-351]

traceLinks.notes: the annotation check that the table rows are compared with

records.requirement: The system shall test with Kotlin, for every row of the nullable-accessor table of `docs/api/kotlin.md`, that the accessor assigns to the Kotlin type the table states: a nullable accessor is used with safe-call or elvis syntax and returns `null` when the value is absent, and a non-null accessor is used without them and returns the stated empty value or throws the stated exception.
records.rationale: Covers D-351; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): the table has 12 rows: `req.param` `String` (throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a name the pattern lacks, `Request.java:25`), `req.query`, `req.form`, `req.header`, `req.cookie`, `req.file`, `req.lastEventId`, `req.attribute(key, type)` and `req.body(type)` nullable, `req.queries` and `req.files` empty lists, `req.service` throwing. Decision: the test routes real requests through the in-memory harness and asserts each row in both the present and the absent case; the declared Kotlin type is written in the test (`val page: String? = req.query("page")`, `val id: String = req.param("id")`) so a platform-type regression fails compilation. Pitfall: `val x = req.query("a")` would infer a platform type if the annotation were lost; the explicit declared type is what makes the test fail. Rejected alternative: deriving the test from the table text; Kotlin types cannot be generated from text, and AC-2 of FR-KT-001 already compares the table with the annotations.

records.title: Kotlin test of the default Gson codec limit for classes without a no-argument constructor

acceptanceCriteria.text: A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-gson` decodes `{"name":"a"}` into `data class User(val name: String)` through the default `GsonJsonCodec` and asserts that `com.google.gson.JsonIOException` is thrown. [D-355; T11]

A Kotlin test routes `POST` with `{"name":"a"}` and `req.body(User::class.java)` through the in-memory harness with the default `GsonJsonCodec` and asserts status `500` with the standard error body of code `INTERNAL_ERROR`, matching the `json.md` statement. [D-355; T11]
A class `CreateUserRequest { var name: String? = null }` decodes `{"name":"a"}` with `name == "a"` and `{}` with `name == null` through the same codec. [D-355; D-349]

A docs test asserts that `json.md` contains `JsonIOException` and the default-constructor sentence and that `kotlin.md` contains the sentence that Gson does not understand Kotlin default arguments and non-null types, so the test and the text name the same limit. [D-355]

records.requirement: The system shall show with a Kotlin test over the default `GsonJsonCodec` that a Kotlin data class without a no-argument constructor cannot be decoded — the codec fails with Gson's `JsonIOException` and the request path answers `500` — while a class with a no-argument constructor (nullable properties initialised to `null`) decodes, matching `docs/api/json.md` and `docs/api/kotlin.md`.
records.rationale: Covers D-355; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `docs/api/json.md:31` states that the default Gson configuration turns off constructor-bypassing instance creation (`Unsafe`) and `:69` that a type problem such as a class without a default constructor (`JsonIOException`) is `500`; `docs/api/kotlin.md` recommends nullable `var` fields; `NaruServe-gson/src/test/kotlin/com/snoworca/naruserve/gson/GsonCodecKotlinTest.kt` exists. Pitfall: a Kotlin class whose constructor parameters all have default values gets a synthetic public no-argument constructor on the JVM, so only a data class with at least one parameter without a default demonstrates the limit. Decision: the failing fixture is `data class User(val name: String)`; the passing fixture is the `CreateUserRequest { var name: String? = null }` shape of `kotlin.md`. Rejected alternative: enabling Unsafe creation so data classes decode; it is off on purpose (FR-JSON-003) because it bypasses constructors and defaults.

records.title: Engine-free multipart parser shared by every adapter: boundary 400, nested parts, part-header limits 413

acceptanceCriteria.text: The multipart parser is a class of `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` that references no adapter, TinyHttpd, Servlet or `java.nio.file` type, no class of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` references TinyHttpd's `MultipartReader` (class-reference test), and the T13 to T16 tests and the T17 cases other than the mid-upload disconnect run both over a TinyHttpd socket and over the in-memory test adapter with the same results; the T17 mid-upload disconnect case of FR-MULTIPART-006 AC-1 runs over a TinyHttpd socket only. [D-247]

A `multipart/form-data` request without a `boundary` parameter, or whose boundary is empty, longer than 70 characters or contains a character outside the RFC 2046 `bchars` set, or whose body lacks the first delimiter or the close delimiter, is answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006 through `onError` when an accessor reads it, and the handler's accessor call throws `HttpException(400)`. Decision: a body truncated before the close delimiter is malformed and gets `400`. [D-236] Decision: the `boundary` parameter name is matched case-insensitively, a quoted-string value is unquoted, and the value must consist of RFC 2046 `bchars` with no trailing space. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a part without a `Content-Disposition: form-data` carrying a `name` parameter is also malformed and answered `400`, and every temporary file of that parse is deleted before the `HttpException(400)` is thrown. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-2] Decision: bytes before the first delimiter and after the close delimiter are ignored as preamble and epilogue. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-3]

A part whose `Content-Type` is `multipart/mixed` inside a `multipart/form-data` body appears in `parts()` as one entry whose `contentType()` is `multipart/mixed` and whose content is the raw nested body bytes, and the parser does not split it into further parts. [D-237]

A part header line of 8192 bytes is accepted, a part header line of 8193 bytes is answered `413`, and a part whose header lines total more than 16384 bytes is answered `413`, both with the standard error body, like the other multipart limits. [D-235; D-233; wave decision: Oversized part headers] Decision: a header line is counted in bytes without its CRLF for the 8192 line limit, and the 16384 total is the sum of those line lengths. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-4]

Over TinyHttpd with default settings, a multipart body of 67108864 bytes in total holding a file part of 33554432 bytes is parsed and both reach the handler, while a body one byte above 67108864 is answered `413` by the core, because TinyHttpd's default body limit stays `-1` (no cap) and the adapter never sets `maxRequestBodyBytes` (FR-ENGINE-003 AC-7). [D-232; D-247; wave-5: FR-ENGINE-003]
