records.requirement: The system shall parse `multipart/form-data` bodies with one engine-free parser in `NaruServe-api` that serves every adapter, including the TinyHttpd adapter, answer a missing or malformed boundary with `400`, expose a nested `multipart/*` part as an ordinary part without recursive parsing, and answer a part header line above 8192 bytes or a part header section above 16384 bytes with `413`.
records.rationale: Covers D-235, D-236, D-237, D-247 and the wave decision "Oversized part headers" (D-235, D-233). Builds on CON-HTTP-001 and CON-BUILD-013 (engine-free core; no TinyHttpd `MultipartReader` in api), FR-HTTP-020 (limit stream) and FR-ENGINE-003 AC-7 (the adapter never sets `maxRequestBodyBytes`, TinyHttpd's default `-1` means no cap). Pitfall: using TinyHttpd's `MultipartReader` would give two parsers whose limits differ between adapters (T13-T17 would test only one); rejected. Risk answered from code_context.json: a 64 MiB upload over TinyHttpd needs no adapter change.

records.title: Multipart and urlencoded size limits on accumulated received bytes answered 413

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `maxFileSize(1024)`, a file part of 1024 bytes is accepted and one of 1025 bytes is answered `413`; with `maxRequestSize(4096)`, a body of more than 4096 bytes is answered `413`; and with the default `maxParts` 20, a body of 20 parts is accepted and one of 21 parts is answered `413`; each `413` carries the standard error body of FR-APP-006 and passes through `onError`. [D-233; T15] Decision: under `maxParts` 20 the `413` is thrown when the 21st part delimiter is reached, before that part's headers are read. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-5] Decision: a file part fails with `413` on the first byte above `maxFileSize`, and text parts never count against `maxFileSize`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-6]

A chunked multipart body and a multipart body without `Content-Length` that exceed `maxRequestSize` are answered `413` once the accumulated received bytes pass the limit, the parser reads no more than the limit plus one internal read buffer of 8192 bytes of the body, and a body whose `Content-Length` already exceeds `maxRequestSize` is answered `413` before any part reaches the handler. Decision: the parser's internal read buffer is 8192 bytes. [D-234; T15] Decision: the body stream is wrapped in a limit counter bound to both `maxRequestSize` and `Content-Length`, so a `Content-Length` above the limit fails on the first read and a chunked body fails after the limit plus one read buffer. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-2 SDS-AC-7]
With the default `formLimit`, an urlencoded body of 1048576 bytes is parsed and one of 1048577 bytes is answered `413`, also when it is sent chunked without `Content-Length`. [D-238; D-234]

records.requirement: The system shall answer `413` when a multipart file part exceeds `maxFileSize`, a multipart body exceeds `maxRequestSize`, a multipart body holds more than `maxParts` parts, or an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body exceeds `formLimit`, counting accumulated received bytes so that chunked bodies and bodies without `Content-Length` are bounded the same way.
records.rationale: Covers D-233, D-234 and D-238 (T15). Builds on FR-HTTP-020 (limit-enforcing stream and `BodyTooLargeException`), FR-APP-005 and FR-APP-006 (one error path, standard body) and IR-JSON-002 (bounded-limit pattern). Pitfall: trusting `Content-Length` alone lets a chunked body bypass the limit; the count is taken on bytes read.

records.title: form, file, files and parts behaviour over urlencoded and multipart bodies with one shared parse

acceptanceCriteria.text: For the urlencoded body `name=Kim+Lee&name=x&city=%EC%84%9C%EC%9A%B8`, `req.form("name")` returns `Kim Lee`, `req.form("city")` returns `서울` and `req.form("zip")` returns `null`, decoded by the form rules of FR-HTTP-025 (`+` as space, percent-decoded UTF-8); an urlencoded body with malformed percent-encoding (`a=%G1`, `a=%4`) or invalid UTF-8 (`a=%FF`) makes the accessor throw `HttpException(400)`, answered `400` with the standard error body of FR-APP-006, like the malformed query of FR-HTTP-025; for a multipart body, `form(name)` returns the first part of that name that has no `filename` parameter, and never a file part. [D-240] Decision: an urlencoded pair without `=` (such as `a`) yields the value `""` and an empty pair (as in `a&&b=1`) is skipped; a multipart text part is decoded as strict UTF-8 and malformed bytes make the accessor throw `HttpException(400)`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-2] Decision: for an urlencoded body `parts()` is empty and `file(name)` returns `null`, while `form(name)` returns the first decoded value. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-3]

Decision: on a request whose `Content-Type` is neither `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` nor `multipart/form-data` and whose body is still unread, `req.form(name)` returns `null`, `file(name)` returns `null`, `files(name)` and `parts()` return empty lists, none of them reads the body, and a later `req.body(...)` on a JSON body still reads it; once `req.body(...)` has read the body, a call of `form`, `file`, `files` or `parts` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` (FR-HTTP-019 AC-3), as `docs/api/request.md` states. [D-240; D-241] Decision: the media type is the `Content-Type` text before `;`, trimmed and compared case-insensitively; for any other media type the accessors leave the body state untouched while it is unread and throw `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` once it is not. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-1]

Decision: a file part is a part whose `Content-Disposition` carries a `filename` parameter. `req.file("doc")` returns the first file part named `doc` or `null`, and `req.files("doc")` returns every file part named `doc` in body order, or an empty list when there is none. [D-241; T13]

A multipart request holding the text fields `title` and `tag`, two files named `photos` and one file named `doc` exposes `form("title")`, `form("tag")`, `file("doc")`, `files("photos")` with both files in body order, and `parts()` with all five parts in body order, all inside one handler. [D-242; T13]

Repeated calls of `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` in one request parse the body once and return the same `UploadFile` instances, and after any of them a call of `req.body(...)` throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` because the body was read as the `FORM` kind (exclusive kinds of FR-HTTP-019 AC-3); the body-state check of `req.body` runs before the JSON media-type check of FR-JSON-001, so this case never yields `UnsupportedMediaTypeException`. Decision: the four accessors share one cached parse result. [D-242; D-240; D-241] Decision: when the shared parse failed with `400` or `413`, a later accessor call throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-5]

records.requirement: The system shall make `req.form(name)` return the first text field of that name from an urlencoded or multipart body or `null`, `req.file(name)` the first file part of that name or `null`, `req.files(name)` every file part of that name in body order or an empty list, and `req.parts()` every part, all four reading one shared parse of the body under the `FORM` body kind.
records.rationale: Covers D-240, D-241 and D-242 (T13). Builds on FR-HTTP-019 (exclusive body kinds, cached shared form/multipart parse), FR-HTTP-025 (form-urlencoded decoding rules) and FR-JSON-001 (urlencoded and multipart are not JSON). records.title: Memory and disk spooling with bounded heap, server-generated temp names and unchanged client filenames

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `memoryThreshold(1024)`, a file part of 1024 bytes creates no file in the temp directory (the test lists the directory before and after), and a file part of 1025 bytes creates exactly one temporary file in the configured `tempDirectory` while its request runs. [D-243; T14] Decision: when byte `memoryThreshold`+1 of a file part arrives the temp file is created, the buffered bytes are flushed to it and the memory buffer is dropped. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-1]

Uploading a 32 MiB file with the default 64 KiB `memoryThreshold` keeps the used heap, measured after `System.gc()` before the upload and while the handler holds the `UploadFile`, from growing by 8 MiB or more. Decision: the asserted heap bound is 8 MiB for a 32 MiB upload. [D-244; T14]

Every temporary file is created through `File.createTempFile` in `tempDirectory` with the prefix `naru-upload-` and the suffix `.tmp`; for a part whose filename is `../../evil.sh`, `a/b\c.txt` (one backslash) or a 300-character name, the temporary file name contains no part of the filename or the field name, and no file appears outside `tempDirectory`. Decision: the temp-name prefix is `naru-upload-` and the suffix `.tmp`. [D-245; T16]

`UploadFile.filename()` returns the client's `filename` parameter unchanged, including `../../evil.sh` and a non-ASCII name, and `save(File)` writes only to the destination the app passes, so no framework code builds a path from the filename (a test checks that no file named after the client value appears anywhere under the temp directory or the working directory). [D-246; T16]

Decision: a multipart text part (one without a `filename` parameter) is never spooled and is held in memory, and the total of the content bytes of all text parts of one multipart request is capped by the `formLimit` of IR-MULTIPART-001 (default 1 MiB, like multer's `fieldSize` but per request), so the heap held by text parts never exceeds the same bound as an urlencoded body; with the default `formLimit`, one text part of 1048576 bytes reaches `form(name)` and `parts()`, one text part of 1048577 bytes is answered `413`, and two text parts of 600000 bytes each are answered `413`, each `413` with the standard error body; text parts also count against `maxRequestSize` and `maxParts` but not against `maxFileSize`. [D-243; D-244; D-238]

records.title: UploadFile content methods: save, transferTo, bytes limit and use after the request ended

acceptanceCriteria.text: `save(dest)` writes content byte-equal to the uploaded part for an in-memory part and for a spooled part, replacing an existing `dest`, and after it returns the spooled part's temporary file no longer exists. Decision: `save` replaces an existing destination file. [D-249; T18] Decision: `save` copies through a truncating `FileOutputStream` and then deletes the temp file, never `File.renameTo`, so the result is the same across file systems. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-3]
`transferTo(out)` writes the full content of an in-memory part and of a spooled part into `out`, and a test stream that records `close()` shows that `transferTo` never closed it. [D-250; T18]

`bytes()` returns the full content for a part of 8388608 bytes and throws `IllegalStateException` naming the part size and the 8388608-byte limit for a part of 8388609 bytes; `inputStream()` reads the full content and `size()` equals the number of content bytes. [D-251; D-248; D-239]

After the request of an upload has ended, `inputStream()`, `save(File)`, `transferTo(OutputStream)` and `bytes()` throw `IllegalStateException`, while `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()` and `size()` keep returning their values. Decision: only the content methods throw after the request ended. [D-252] Decision: when the request ends every `InputStream` handed out by `inputStream()` is closed, so a later read on it throws `IOException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-4]

Decision: after a successful `save(dest)`, a later `inputStream()`, `bytes()`, `transferTo(OutputStream)` or second `save(File)` on the same part throws `IllegalStateException` for in-memory and spooled parts alike, because the content now lives only at `dest`, while `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()` and `size()` keep returning their values; a test calls `bytes()` after `save` on a spooled part and on an in-memory part. [D-249; D-252] Decision: `close()` called before the request ended releases the content like `save`, after which the content methods throw `IllegalStateException` and the metadata methods keep their values. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-5]

records.title: Temporary upload file cleanup at request end, after save, after 413, on disconnect and through an after-onStop shutdown participant

acceptanceCriteria.text: A test that lists `tempDirectory` finds it empty after each of: a request whose handler ignores its spooled upload and returns; a request whose handler calls `save`; a request answered `413` because a spooled part passed `maxFileSize`; and a request whose client closes the socket after sending half of a spooled part over TinyHttpd. [D-254; T15; T17] Decision: the uploads are released once when the response's done callback fires (complete or abort) or the error path returned, and a parse failure, including an `IOException` in the middle of an upload, deletes its temp files before rethrowing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-6]

The app registers one internal participant in the `AFTER_ON_STOP` phase of the shutdown participant registry of FR-APP-011; with a handler holding an open spooled upload when `shutdown` is called, the participant runs after `onStop` and after the in-flight request finished or was force-closed by the adapter stop, and the temporary file no longer exists when `shutdown` returns. [D-255; carried: V1-003] Decision: the participant is added once, when the app is constructed. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-4 SDS-AC-8]

After the cleanup participant has deleted the open temporary files it closes the app's spool registry: a handler thread still running after the adapter's force-close that then parses a multipart body with a part above `memoryThreshold` gets `HttpException(500)` from the accessor (no `UncheckedIOException`), answered `500` if its connection is still open, and leaves no file in `tempDirectory`; a parse during the graceful drain (`STOPPING`, before the participant ran) still spools normally. [wave decision: Spool cleanup closes the spool registry; D-255; D-254]

Each upload deletes its own temporary file when its request ends while other requests still hold open uploads, whose files stay until their own requests end. [D-254; wave decision: Spool cleanup closes the spool registry]

records.requirement: The system shall delete temporary upload files when their request ends, after a successful `save`, after a `413` and when the client disconnects mid-upload, and shall delete the temporary files still open at shutdown before `shutdown` returns through an after-`onStop` participant of the shutdown participant registry that then closes the app's spool registry, so a later parse fails with `HttpException(500)` and leaves no file.
records.rationale: Covers D-254 and D-255 (T15, T17), the carried line V1-003 (D-401, D-162, D-255: temp cleanup is an after-onStop participant that runs only after in-flight requests finished or were force-closed) and the wave decision "Spool cleanup closes the spool registry" (D-255, D-254; r4 W2-001). records.title: CycloneDX SBOM for every published module, generated only for a -Prelease run

acceptanceCriteria.text: `./gradlew -Prelease releaseSbom` writes one CycloneDX JSON file per published module — nine files named `<module>.cdx.json` under `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/`, one for each entry of `naruModules` — each with `bomFormat` `CycloneDX` and a component for every `runtimeClasspath` dependency of that module (Gson 2.14.0 for `NaruServe-gson`, `kotlin-stdlib` for `NaruServe-kotlin`, `slf4j-api` for `NaruServe-slf4j`, the TinyHttpd components for `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`), and none for `compileOnly` or test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API and Jetty). [D-375; T50]
The run is recorded with its command, date, file list and component counts in `docs/release/test-results.md` under T50, because the plugin cannot be resolved by the default build. [D-375; D-381]

A default-build test asserts that `build.gradle` contains the conditional `apply from: 'gradle/release.gradle'` guarded by `project.hasProperty('release')`, that the strings `cyclonedx` and `dependencycheck` occur in none of `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle` and `gradle.properties` (the files it scans) but only in `gradle/release.gradle`, that `gradle/release.gradle` pins each plugin version as an exact literal, and that no release task is a dependency of `check`, `build` or `test`. [r4 W2-004; I-019]

`./gradlew build --offline` with a Gradle user home that holds every default-build dependency (Jetty 9.4 included) but neither release plugin succeeds, which a recorded run (command, date, exit code) shows for the release machine. [r4 W2-004; I-019]

The default `./gradlew build` still passes `BuildLayoutTest` with its assertions unchanged — `con_BUILD_003_AC1_rootBuildFileHoldsPluginsCompileDependenciesAndChecks` and `con_BUILD_003_AC2_noModuleBuildFile` keep their expectations and are re-pointed to CON-BUILD-017 — and one check is added to it for the conditional apply of AC-3. [CON-BUILD-017]

traceLinks.notes: single root build file with the release-only script exception

records.requirement: The release build shall generate a CycloneDX SBOM for each of the nine published modules when run with `./gradlew -Prelease releaseSbom`, through the CycloneDX Gradle plugin that the root `build.gradle` applies only inside `if (project.hasProperty('release'))` by `apply from: 'gradle/release.gradle'`, so that a default `./gradlew build`, online or offline, never resolves the plugin and no release task is wired into `check` or `build`.
records.rationale: Covers D-375, wave decision Release plugins (r4 W2-004), I-019 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the nine published modules are the entries of `naruModules` in `build.gradle:11-12`; the Gradle plugin portal metadata lists `org.cyclonedx:cyclonedx-gradle-plugin` up to 3.5.1 and the network was reachable; `build.gradle` has a `plugins {}` block with `ru.vyarus.animalsniffer` and the Kotlin plugin `apply false`. Decision: the plugin is applied from `gradle/release.gradle`, a script plugin with its own `buildscript {}` block, because a `plugins {}` block cannot be conditional and resolves its plugin even with `apply false`; `gradle/release.gradle` is not a module build file, so CON-BUILD-017 AC-2 (no `build.gradle` in a module directory) holds; CON-BUILD-003 AC-1 (the root `build.gradle` holds every module's configuration) would read false once release tasks live in the applied script, so wave 8 supersedes CON-BUILD-003 with CON-BUILD-017, whose AC-1 states the one exception, and the line of `CLAUDE.md` that says the root `build.gradle` configures all modules gets the same exception sentence. The plugin version is an exact literal pinned when the file is written (not a dynamic range); the SBOM files go to `build/reports/naruserve/sbom/<module>.cdx.json`; the lifecycle task names are `releaseSbom`, `releaseScan`, `releaseLicenses` and `releaseCheck`. Pitfall: `BuildLayoutTest` reads `build.gradle` for pinned strings (`'java-library'`, `options.release = 8`, the class-reference prefixes), so the conditional apply is added without touching them. Measured by prototype (2026-10-20, feasibility run): applying the CycloneDX plugin by id from a subproject failed while applying it by class (`org.cyclonedx.gradle.CyclonedxPlugin`) from the script plugin wrote nine SBOMs including the TinyHttpd components. Rejected alternative: a `buildscript { classpath }` in the root file; it resolves the plugin on every build, including offline.

records.title: Dependency vulnerability scan with a pending record that keeps the full dependency list

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the scanner stubbed to fail for each of four causes — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit and a tool error — the report writer in `gradle/release-tools` produces a report whose status line is `pending`, whose reason line names the cause, and whose dependency list equals the sorted union of the `group:name:version` of the `runtimeClasspath` entries of the nine published modules in `dependency-graphs.txt` without the project's own `com.snoworca.naruserve:*` components and with the `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` components kept, which a default-build test over the writer asserts without network. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

A finished scan produces the status `completed` with a findings table (dependency, identifier, CVSS score, severity), or the sentence `no findings`, and the report names the scanner version and the data timestamp. [D-376]

`docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md` exists and holds the report of the release run (`pending` with the reason, or `completed`), and the T50 vulnerability line of `docs/release/test-results.md` is `manual-pending` when the report is `pending` and `verified` when it is `completed` on the release machine, which a docs test compares. [D-376; D-381]
The report's dependency list excludes `compileOnly` and test-scope artifacts (the Servlet API, JSpecify, JUnit, Jetty) and includes the TinyHttpd components. [D-376]

`releaseScan` runs the scanner in a child Gradle invocation with `ignoreExitValue` and writes the `pending` report when that invocation exits non-zero or leaves no report file, which the report writer's test covers with a stub exit code. [D-376; r3 W2-005]

changeNotes.reason: Feasibility=medium (score 70) at assessment; its stated conditions were addressed by SRS text fixes before promotion (blocker: no mechanism to convert a scanner failure into pending: dependencyCheckAggregate 13.0.0 fails despite failOnError=false). Run: 2026-10-20.NaruServe.wave-8.v01

records.requirement: The release build shall run `./gradlew -Prelease releaseScan`, an OWASP Dependency-Check scan, run in a child Gradle invocation whose exit value is ignored, of the runtime dependencies of the published modules, and write `build/reports/naruserve/vulnerability-scan.md` with the status `completed` and the findings, or, whenever the scanner cannot finish — no network, a missing NVD API key, a rate limit or a tool error — with the status `pending`, the failure reason and the full dependency list (`group:name:version`, one line each, sorted, without duplicates), without failing the build for that reason.
records.rationale: Covers D-376, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: pending for any reason the scanner cannot finish) and T50; the block on findings is FR-REL-003. Measured (2026-10-20): the Gradle plugin portal lists `org.owasp:dependency-check-gradle` up to 13.0.0; the network was reachable but a scan without an NVD API key is rate-limited and can fail partway; the shipped runtime dependencies are Gson 2.14.0 with `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0`, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0 with `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0`, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components, as `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` lists them per module and configuration. Decision: the pure parts — the report writer, the pending decision and the dependency-list derivation — are plain Java 8 sources in `gradle/release-tools` (package `com.snoworca.naruserve.release`), which the root `test` source set adds as a source directory (so the unit tests compile in the default build) and which `gradle/release.gradle` compiles with its own `JavaCompile` task and runs with `JavaExec` tasks, so the script never needs compiled classes at configuration time, so the default build can test them without any plugin or network. Decision: the committed record of the release run is `docs/release/vulnerability-scan.md`, copied from the build report; the scan covers the `runtimeClasspath` of the nine published modules and excludes test scope (Jetty 9.4 of the Servlet tests); the scanner's own failure is caught by a wrapper task that writes the pending report. Measured by prototype (2026-10-20, feasibility run): Dependency-Check 13.0.0 aborts with "Analysis failed" even with `failOnError=false`, so a failure inside the same build cannot be turned into a record; `releaseScan` therefore runs the scan in a child Gradle invocation with `ignoreExitValue` and writes `pending` on a non-zero exit or a missing report. Pitfall: Dependency-Check fails the build on an update error by default; the wrapper converts that into `pending`, otherwise an offline release machine could not record anything. Rejected alternative: treating a pending scan as a pass; the record says `pending`, T50 stays `manual-pending` for this part and I-020 forbids promoting a requirement on a pending check.

records.title: Release is blocked by an unexcepted High or Critical dependency vulnerability

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the decision function of `gradle/release-tools` exercised by a default-build test, a fixture report with one High finding and no exception makes the check fail with a message naming the vulnerability id and the dependency; the same report with a complete exception row passes; a Medium finding passes; a Critical finding fails; an exception row without a reason or approver is ignored and the check still fails. [D-377]

A fixture report with the status `pending` makes the check pass and prints `scan pending: release not cleared for T50 vulnerability part`, and the release notes list the scan as pending. [D-377; r3 W2-005]
`docs/release/vulnerability-exceptions.md` exists with the table header (id, dependency, reason, approver, date) and either the recorded exceptions or `no exceptions`. [D-377]
The check reads only the runtime dependencies of the published modules, so a High finding in a test-scope artifact does not block, which a fixture asserts. [D-377]

`releaseCheck` depends on `releaseScan` and `releaseLicenses` in the task graph (a text test of `gradle/release.gradle` asserts it), reads `build/reports/naruserve/vulnerability-scan.md` of the same run, and is not a dependency of `check`, `build` or `test`. [D-377; r4 W2-004]

records.requirement: The release build shall define `releaseCheck` as a task that depends on `releaseScan` and `releaseLicenses` and reads the report that run wrote (`releaseSbom` runs separately), and shall fail `./gradlew -Prelease releaseCheck` while the vulnerability report shows a High or Critical finding (CVSS 7.0 or higher) for a runtime dependency of a published module that has no recorded exception in `docs/release/vulnerability-exceptions.md`, where an exception names the vulnerability id, the dependency, the reason, the approver and the date; a `pending` scan does not block the build but is shown as pending, never as passed.
records.rationale: Covers D-377, I-019 and I-020, wave decision Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005: a finished scan with a High or Critical finding still blocks) and T50. Measured: `object.md:1170` (the first general release gate) requires "no unresolved High/Critical dependency vulnerability (exception approval procedure separate)". Decision: severity follows the CVSS v3 base score (High 7.0 to 8.9, Critical 9.0 and above), an exception row with a missing field counts as no exception, the exceptions file starts with a header and the line `no exceptions`, and a `pending` report is shown in the release notes as an open item. Pitfall: a `pending` status must not read as green; the release documentation and `docs/release/test-results.md` print the literal. Rejected alternative: blocking while the scan is pending; D-376 makes pending an allowed recorded state for an offline run, and blocking it would make an offline release impossible, so the open item is explicit instead.

records.title: License report: every shipped dependency is non-GPL and listed in THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md

acceptanceCriteria.text: `releaseLicenses` writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` with one row per shipped dependency taken from the `runtimeClasspath` entries of `dependency-graphs.txt` — Gson 2.14.0, `error_prone_annotations` 2.48.0, `kotlin-stdlib` 2.2.0, `org.jetbrains:annotations` 13.0, `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 and the TinyHttpd components — giving license name and URL, and a section of provided artifacts that names `javax.servlet-api` as container-provided and not shipped. changeNotes.reason: Feasibility=medium (score 76) at assessment; its stated conditions were addressed by SRS text fixes before promotion (blocker: slf4j-api 1.7.36 POM has no <licenses> (MIT is in the parent slf4j-parent), so a POM-only license query fails). Run: 2026-10-20.NaruServe.wave-8.v01

records.requirement: The release build shall run `./gradlew -Prelease releaseLicenses`, which resolves the license of every dependency on the `runtimeClasspath` of the published modules, fails when any has a GPL-family license (GPL, LGPL or AGPL) or none that can be determined, and writes `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` at the repository root listing each shipped dependency as `group:name:version` with its license name and URL, and a default-build test shall fail when that file does not list exactly those dependencies.
records.rationale: Covers D-378 and T50. Measured (2026-10-20): the root `LICENSE` and `/Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/LICENSE` both open "BSD 3-Clause License"; Gson, `com.google.errorprone:error_prone_annotations:2.48.0` (Gson's transitive dependency), `kotlin-stdlib` and `org.jetbrains:annotations:13.0` are Apache-2.0 and `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 is MIT by their POMs; `javax.servlet-api` 3.1.0 (CDDL with GPLv2 classpath exception) is `compileOnly` and therefore provided by the container, not shipped; `build.gradle` already writes the resolved graphs to `build/reports/naruserve/dependency-graphs.txt` (`checkDependencyRules`). Decision: licenses come from the POMs through an artifact resolution query; the TinyHttpd components come from an override table in `gradle/release.gradle` with the source `TinyHttpd/LICENSE` (the included build has no POM); a component with no license information and no override fails the task; the file also lists the compile-only artifacts under "provided by the container or the build, not shipped" with their licenses so the CDDL/GPL entry is explicit. Pitfall: the `slf4j-api` 1.7.36 POM has no `<licenses>` element; its MIT license is declared in the parent POM, so the resolution walks the parent POM chain before it reports a missing license. Pitfall: a dependency whose POM states two licenses (dual license) passes when at least one is non-GPL and the file lists both. Rejected alternative: a name-based allowlist of group ids; a new transitive dependency would pass unseen.

records.requirement: The root build shall publish each of the nine modules to `mavenLocal` with `maven-publish` configured in the root `build.gradle` — coordinates `com.snoworca.naruserve:<module>:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, no remote repository — with a POM whose dependencies carry the versions the resolved graph selects, including the TinyHttpd components of `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`.
records.rationale: Covers wave decision Publishing (r1 W2-004: v1 publishes to `mavenLocal` only, README coordinates `com.snoworca.naruserve:<module>:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, the POM mechanism is settled at SRS authoring) and D-383 (POM part), D-375, D-379. Pitfall: without the version mapping the generated POM has a dependency without a `<version>`, which Maven consumers reject. Rejected alternative: publishing sources and javadoc jars; v1 publishes to the local repository only, reopen with a remote repository.

[D-326] Decision: `res.sse()` replaces any app-set `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control`, removes `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, and sets status `200` whatever status was set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-6] Decision: when `ex.eventStream` throws a `RuntimeException`, the client is removed from the registry, the state stays `NEW` and the exception is rethrown so that the error path commits a `503`; an `IOException` aborts the response and returns an ended client. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-8]

`res.sse()` on a response that is already committed throws `IllegalStateException` and writes nothing, and a second `res.sse()` on the same response throws `IllegalStateException`. Decision: `res.sse()` follows the single-commit rule of FR-HTTP-016. [D-326]

`client.send("connected", "ready")` writes exactly the bytes `event: connected
data: ready

` to the client (T24). [D-328]

`client.send("m", "a
b
cd")` writes exactly `event: m
data: a
data: b
data: c
data: d

`, and `client.send("m", "a
")` writes exactly `event: m
data: a
data: 

` (T24). Decision: every data line, including an empty one, is written as `data: ` followed by the line. [D-329]

`client.send(SseEvent.event("progress").id("100").data("{"progress":50}").retry(3000))` writes exactly `event: progress
id: 100
retry: 3000
data: {"progress":50}

`, the same bytes result when `retry` and `id` are set before `data`, an unset `id` or `retry` writes no line, and an event whose data is `null` or never set writes the single line `data: ` (T24). Decision: the field order is `event`, `id`, `retry`, `data`, as `docs/api/sse.md` shows. [D-330]

traceLinks.notes: single commit and STREAMING state for res.sse()
CR/LF rejection rule reused for event names and ids

records.requirement: The system shall, on `res.sse()`, commit status `200` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=UTF-8` and `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform`, put the response in `STREAMING` and return an `SseClient`, serialise each event as its `event`, `id`, `retry` and `data` lines in that order followed by a blank line with the data split at CR, LF and CRLF into one `data:` line per line, reject event names and ids that contain CR, LF or NUL, and expose a reconnecting client's `Last-Event-ID` through `req.lastEventId()`.
records.rationale: Covers D-326, D-328, D-329, D-330, D-331, D-337 and the data-only send of D-339; test T24. Measured: `Request.java:47` declares `lastEventId()` (verified under FR-HTTP-011 AC-3), so D-337 needs only an end-to-end check inside an SSE handler; `Response` has no `sse` method (`Response.java:9`). The event-stream format follows the WHATWG HTML "Server-sent events" parsing rules: a line `data: x` and `data:x` parse the same, an empty data line contributes an empty line, and EventSource dispatches an event without `event:` as `message`. Decision: each data line, including an empty one, is written as `data: ` followed by the line, so the data `a` followed by LF becomes the lines `data: a` and `data: `, and EventSource rebuilds the same string; lines end with LF; the fields are written in the fixed order `event`, `id`, `retry`, `data` whatever the setter order. Pitfall: a name or id with LF would inject a forged field; D-331 rejects it before anything is queued. Pitfall: `res.sse()` after `res.send(...)` must not write a second status line; it throws `IllegalStateException` like the other writers on a committed response (FR-HTTP-016). Rejected alternative: escaping CR/LF in names instead of rejecting them; silent rewriting hides app bugs, reopen never in v1.

records.title: SSE outbound queue, drain loop and heartbeat: any-thread sends in call order, handler-thread writes before the drain starts and the overflow policy

acceptanceCriteria.text: After the handler returned, 8 threads each send 500 distinct events concurrently to one stream with a reading client; the client receives all 4000 events, every event's lines arrive contiguous with no line of another event between them, and the events of each thread arrive in that thread's call order (T25). [D-333; D-406]

A send made from a thread other than the handler's thread is queued and written to the socket by the drain loop on the thread the adapter chose, which a test asserts by recording the writing thread in the in-memory adapter and finding it different from the sending thread. [D-406]

With `heartbeatInterval` 1 s and nothing sent, the client receives `: ping

` within 1 s plus 500 ms after the last write and again after the next interval, and with an event sent every 300 ms no `: ping` arrives during 3 s (T25). Decision: the heartbeat is the comment line `: ping` written after one heartbeat interval with no write, default interval 15 s. [D-332] Decision: the drain waits on the client lock for the time left until `lastWrite + heartbeat` and then writes `: ping

` itself, flushing after each event and each ping; no timer thread exists. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-2]

With `sendQueueSize(1024)`, a drain write held blocked by the in-memory adapter and sends of 100-byte events from a non-handler thread, the send that would make the queued bytes exceed 1024 returns `false` without throwing; once the write is released the client receives no event queued after the blocked one, the body ends, the `onClose` listeners run once, `isOpen()` is `false` and every later `send` returns `false`. Decision: overflow ends the stream (dropped event, discarded queue, ended body) and the overflowing `send` returns `false`. [D-406; D-339]

A handler that sends 600 events of 1 KiB each (more than 256 KiB in total) to a reading client before it returns, under the default `sendQueueSize` over TinyHttpd, delivers every event in order and leaves `isOpen()` `true` after the handler returned; the handler waits on a latch after its first send, and the test reads that first event from the client socket before releasing the latch, so handler-thread sends reach the socket while the handler is still running. Decision: a send on the handler's own thread before the drain starts is written, under the exchange lock, to the stream the adapter handed over through `StreamDrain.attach(out)` and flushed after the event. Deviation (recorded): D-406 says every `send` fills the outbound queue; until the drain loop starts, a send on the handler's own thread writes straight to the attached stream under the exchange lock, so the queue limit applies only to other threads' sends. [D-406; wave decision: Sends inside the SSE handler (r4 W2-001)] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)] Decision: that send takes `writeLock`, writes every queued entry in order and then its own event to the attached stream, flushes, and returns `true`; an `IOException` there ends the stream with cause `client` and returns `false`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-4]

While the handler is still running, another thread queues events `A` and `B`, and then the handler thread sends `C`; the client receives `A`, `B`, `C` in that order, which a test asserts with a latch that holds the handler until `B` is queued. Deviation (recorded): until the drain starts, the handler thread writes the queued events and then its own event to the stream attached through `StreamDrain.attach(out)` under the exchange lock, instead of the drain loop writing every event. [residual: SSE send order before the drain starts (r5 W2-001)] [D-333] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)] Decision: when the drain starts it sets `draining` under the client lock and then takes `writeLock`, so a handler-thread write in progress finishes before the first drain write. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-5]

After the stream ended by client disconnect, `close()`, overflow or shutdown, `send` returns `false`, adds nothing to the queue and throws nothing, and the stream's queue holds zero bytes, which a test reads through the internal stream state. [D-406]

The test-fixture `InMemoryHttpAdapter` exchange's `eventStream` calls `drain.attach(out)` before it returns, with the same exchange-synchronized stream it later passes to `drain(out)`, which a test asserts by recording both instances; with a stub exchange whose `eventStream` never calls `attach`, a handler-thread send before the drain starts is queued under the `sendQueueSize` bound like another thread's send and the drain writes it in call order, which a test asserts. Decision: without an attached stream the core falls back to the bounded queue. [wave decision: Sends inside the SSE handler (r4 W2-001)] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)]

records.requirement: The system shall give each SSE stream a bounded outbound queue of `sendQueueSize` bytes that `SseClient.send` from any thread fills with whole serialised events, which the core drain loop of the event-stream extension point writes to the socket in call order, write a `: ping` comment after each heartbeat interval in which nothing was written, write a send made on the handler's own thread before the drain loop starts, after every event already queued, straight to the stream the adapter handed over through `StreamDrain.attach(out)` (falling back to the bounded queue when the adapter attached no stream), and end the stream when a queued send would make the queued bytes exceed `sendQueueSize`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-332, D-333, D-406 and D-339 (overflow policy), wave decision Sends inside the SSE handler (r4 W2-001) and residual SSE send order before the drain starts (r5 W2-001); test T25. Measured: `spi/StreamDrain.java` is the core-owned drain loop type of the D-106 event-stream point (IR-HTTP-007 AC-3), and `HttpExchange.eventStream(int, List, StreamDrain)` (`spi/HttpExchange.java:89`) lets the adapter choose the thread (FR-SSE-003: the TinyHttpd request worker). Deviation (recorded): D-406 says `SseClient.send` from any thread fills the outbound queue; until the drain loop starts, a send on the handler's own thread first writes every event already queued, in queue order, and then its own event straight to the committed stream under the exchange lock, so a replay loop inside the handler is paced by the socket and never trips the overflow policy, and the queue limit applies only to other threads' sends until then (r4 W2-001, r5 W2-001); `docs/api/sse.md` records it. Decision: overflow drops the event, discards the queued events, ends the stream and makes that `send` return `false` (no exception), so a broadcaster loop needs no `try`. Decision: queued bytes count the serialised UTF-8 bytes of each event. Decision: the heartbeat is the comment `: ping` followed by a blank line, written after one heartbeat interval with no write. Pitfall: a heartbeat timer that fires on a separate thread would need its own lock; the drain loop waits on the queue with the heartbeat interval as timeout and writes the comment itself. Rejected alternative: blocking the sender when the queue is full; it stalls app threads that broadcast to many clients, reopen on demand for a blocking `send` variant. Rejected alternative: queueing handler-thread sends before the drain starts; a handler replaying more than 256 KiB of missed events would overflow its own stream before the drain could run.
- [2026-10-20] Deviation (recorded), committee decision StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1): handler-thread sends before the drain (r4 W2-001, r5 W2-001) go to the stream each adapter hands over via the add-only `default` `StreamDrain.attach(OutputStream)` (IR-HTTP-007 AC-4), a second default method beyond W2-001's "one default method" wording. AC-5 now latches the handler so the test proves the write reaches the socket while it runs; AC-8 covers the in-memory attach and the queue fallback.

records.title: TinyHttpd event-stream class: chunked body on the request worker, NaruServe SSE counter with 503 before start, drain writes synchronized on the exchange

acceptanceCriteria.text: A class-reference test finds no call to TinyHttpd's `startEventStream` in `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`, and over a real socket an SSE response arrives with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, exactly one `Cache-Control` header with the value `no-cache, no-transform`, and an event with `retry` arrives as one block in the field order of FR-SSE-001. [D-335] Decision: the headers are written with `setStatus` and `setHeader` per pair, no `Content-Length`, and flushed once through `Body` before `attach`, so TinyHttpd frames the body chunked and the client sees the headers at once. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-11 SDS-AC-3]

The drain loop runs on the TinyHttpd request worker that ran the handler, after the handler returned: a test records the handler's thread and the thread of a drain write and finds them equal, and finds the drain write starting only after the handler returned. Decision: `eventStream` commits the headers and registers the drain, and `TinyHttpdExchange.run` runs it on the same worker until the core reports the stream ended. [D-335; wave decision: TinyHttpd feature hooks (W2-003)] Decision: a `RuntimeException` from the drain aborts the exchange. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-11 SDS-AC-5]

With `maxWorkers(2)` and `maxSseStreams(3)`, three open SSE streams and two concurrent plain `GET` requests whose handlers each wait 200 ms are all answered while the three streams stay open, so open streams hold one worker each and never take the HTTP worker share. [D-336]

With `maxSseStreams(2)` over TinyHttpd and two open streams, a third request whose handler calls `res.sse()` receives `503` with the standard error body and its request id, because the NaruServe counter throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started and the dispatcher's error path commits it; after one stream ends, a new `res.sse()` is accepted. Decision: `res.sse()` propagates that `HttpException` to the handler. [D-336; wave decision: SSE limit answer (r3 W2-001)]

`TinyHttpdAdapter` still sets TinyHttpd's `maxEventStreams` to `maxSseStreams`, which the existing limit-mapping test asserts, and no NaruServe code opens a TinyHttpd event stream, so the NaruServe counter is the only bound that answers `503` for SSE. [wave decision: maxEventStreams (W2-009)] [D-336]

`eventStream` holds the exchange lock only to check abort and mark the response started: on an aborted exchange it throws without writing a status line, and after it a `commit` or a second `eventStream` throws `IllegalStateException`; every drain write and every handler-thread write before the drain starts runs inside `synchronized (exchange)`, so a test that calls `abort()` while another thread sends sees the client stream end after a whole event and never receives bytes written after the abort. `eventStream` calls `drain.attach(out)` before it returns, with the same exchange-synchronized stream it later passes to `drain(out)`, and a test asserts both calls receive the same instance. [wave decision: TinyHttpd feature hooks (W2-003)] [carried: wave 5 drain synchronization (w5-P2-002)] [wave decision: Sends inside the SSE handler (r4 W2-001)] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)] Decision: inside one `synchronized (ex)` block `start` calls `requireStartable`, then `tryAcquire`, then marks the response started; the header set, the flush, `attach` and `register` run after the lock is released. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-11 SDS-AC-1]

When the client closes its socket, a later write or heartbeat of the drain loop fails with an `IOException`, the stream, which had no earlier recorded end reason, ends with the FR-APP-019 line `cause=client`, and the worker returns to the pool within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s (with `heartbeatInterval` 1 s: 3 s), because the first write after the peer closed may still succeed and only the next one fails, which a test with `heartbeatInterval` 1 s asserts by opening `maxSseStreams` new streams afterwards and reading the access log line. [D-336; D-335; D-338]

Because TinyHttpd buffers the response body output, the stream handed to `attach` and `drain` is flushed after each event and each `: ping` heartbeat the drain loop writes and after each handler-thread write before the drain starts: over a real socket with `heartbeatInterval` 1 s, a single small event sent from another thread after the handler returned reaches the client within 500 ms of the `send`, and with nothing sent a `: ping` reaches it within 1 s plus 500 ms, each without further writes behind it. Decision: the core drain loop calls `flush()` after each event and heartbeat, and the TinyHttpd stream passes the flush to the socket. [D-335; D-332] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)]

records.title: SSE stream lifetime: open after the handler returns, onClose exactly once, explicit close, HEAD on an SSE route, req.service in SSE handlers and shutdown from onClose

acceptanceCriteria.text: After the SSE handler returned, an event sent 2 s later from another thread reaches the client and `isOpen()` is `true`, over TinyHttpd (T25). [D-327]

When the client closes its socket, the `onClose` listeners run exactly once within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s (with `heartbeatInterval` 1 s: 3 s), `isOpen()` becomes `false`, a later `send` returns `false`, and the FR-APP-019 line of the stream carries `cause=client` (T25). [D-334; D-327; D-338]

`client.close()` called from another thread writes every event queued before it, ends the chunked body so the client reads end of stream after the last event, and runs the `onClose` listeners once; a second `close()` changes nothing and runs no listener again. Decision: `close()` ends the stream normally. [D-334; D-339] Decision: when the queue is empty and the client is ended, the drain returns from its loop, calls `res.sseEnded(null)`, removes the client from the registry and only then runs the listeners, so the body ends before `onClose` runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-8]

Two `onClose` listeners run once each in registration order; a listener that throws is logged at ERROR with the request id and the next listener still runs; a listener registered after the stream ended runs at once, once, on the registering thread before `onClose` returns. Decision: `onClose` on an ended client runs at once. [D-334]

A drain write that fails with `IOException` on a stream with no earlier recorded end reason ends the stream, runs the `onClose` listeners once, logs the FR-APP-019 line with `cause=client` and lets the worker return, with no exception reaching the adapter's caller, which an in-memory test asserts by failing the third write; a drain write that fails with a `RuntimeException` ends the stream the same way with `cause=error`; a drain write that fails with `IOException` after `close()` was called keeps `cause=app`, the first recorded end reason of FR-APP-019 AC-10. [D-334; D-338] Decision: when the response aborts before any drain started, `abort` ends the client with cause `error` and runs the listeners, and a later drain call returns at once. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-13]

A `HEAD` request to an SSE route receives `200` with the event-stream headers of FR-SSE-001 and no body, and the response completes; inside the handler `send` returns `false`, `isOpen()` is `false` and an `onClose` listener runs once at registration; with `maxSseStreams(1)` over TinyHttpd, three `HEAD` requests followed by a `GET` that opens a stream all succeed, so `HEAD` takes no SSE slot and holds no worker after the handler returns. [wave decision: HEAD on an SSE route (r3 W2-002)] [D-327; D-334] Decision: for `HEAD` the headers are committed bodyless through the `end()` path, `ex.eventStream` is never called and nothing is registered, and `sse()` returns an ended client while `sseClient()` stays `null`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-10 SDS-AC-11]
`req.service(Clock.class)` inside an SSE handler returns the same instance that `onStart` registered, which a test asserts by identity (T41). [carried: D-142 SSE case]

Over the in-memory adapter and over TinyHttpd, an `onClose` listener that calls `app.shutdown(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)` returns from that call within 500 ms, and the app reaches `TERMINATED` afterwards, because the thread that runs the drain loop enters the request mark (`AppLifecycle.enterRequest`) before the loop and leaves it after the `onClose` listeners it runs, also when that thread is the in-memory adapter's own worker. [residual: shutdown from an SSE onClose listener (r5 W2-004)] [D-334]

records.rationale: Covers D-327, D-334, wave decision HEAD on an SSE route (r3 W2-002), carried D-142 SSE case (T41, from wave 4) and residual shutdown from an SSE onClose listener (r5 W2-004); test T25. Measured: `internal/AppLifecycle.java:110-115` provides `enterRequest()`/`exitRequest()`, which `internal/GatedExchangeHandler.java:46` calls around a dispatch; `docs/api/lifecycle.md` ("요청 핸들러 안에서 shutdown") promises that `shutdown` called during a request returns at once, so the mark must span the drain loop and its `onClose` listeners for that promise to hold when a listener calls `shutdown` (r5 W2-004). The mark is thread-local, and the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread (IR-HTTP-007 AC-3), so the drain thread enters the mark itself (AC-8). FR-HTTP-017 keeps `HEAD` bodyless; for `HEAD` `res.sse()` takes no SSE slot and runs no drain, so no worker is held after the handler returns (r3 W2-002). Decision: an `onClose` registered on an ended client runs at once, once, on the calling thread (removes the `docs/api/sse.md` marker); listener exceptions are logged at ERROR with the request id and the other listeners still run. Decision: `close()` ends the stream normally: the drain writes queued events, ends the chunked body and runs `onClose`. Pitfall: a client disconnect is seen only on a write, and the first write after the peer closed may still succeed, so the heartbeat bounds detection to two intervals plus 1 s. Rejected alternative: a background reader thread per stream to detect disconnects at once; it doubles SSE threads against D-416, reopen never in v1.

records.title: Shutdown of SSE streams: before-wait participant appends the closing notice, marks streams ended and does not wait

data: shutdown

traceLinks.notes: adapter stop aborts stalled streams at the deadline
outbound queue and drain loop receive the notice

records.requirement: The system shall register a before-wait shutdown participant that sets the SSE stream registry's closed flag under its lock, then snapshots every open stream and, without waiting, appends to each stream's outbound queue the closing notice `event: shutdown` with `data: shutdown`, exempt from the queue limit, and marks the stream ended, so that its drain loop writes the queued events and the notice, ends the chunked body, runs the `onClose` listeners once and returns its worker.
records.rationale:
Covers D-341, D-436, D-343 (SSE part) and the SSE part of D-445 (flag before snapshot; the behaviour of `res.sse()` after the flag is FR-APP-020); tests T44 (SSE parts). Measured: `internal/ShutdownParticipants.java:19-26` defines the `BEFORE_WAIT` phase "After STOPPING began, before the adapter stop waits", and `internal/DefaultRestApp.java:617-619` runs it before `adapter.stop(left(deadline))` (FR-APP-011). TinyHttpd's stop closes only its own event streams and upgraded connections and otherwise waits for a D-335 stream until the deadline, so without this participant every open stream would hold `shutdown` to the timeout. Decision: the closing notice is `event: shutdown
data: shutdown

`, dispatched to EventSource listeners of `shutdown`, with non-empty data because EventSource drops events whose data is empty; it is exempt from `sendQueueSize`. Pitfall: waiting for the drains inside the participant would spend the D-344 budget twice; the participant returns at once and the adapter stop waits for the workers. Pitfall: a stream stalled on a full socket never finishes its drain; TinyHttpd aborts it at the deadline (D-343). Rejected alternative: closing sockets without a notice; the client could not tell shutdown from a network failure and would reconnect at once to a stopping server.

records.title: Static mount mapping, directory index, several mounts, routes first, global middleware and the trailing-slash redirect

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `app.staticFiles("/", root)`, `GET /` returns the bytes of `root/index.html` and `GET /assets/app.js` returns the bytes of `root/assets/app.js`, both `200`. [D-256; T27]
`GET /docs/` returns `root/docs/index.html`, and with `index("main.html")` it returns `root/docs/main.html` instead. [D-257; D-261; T27]

With the mounts `/` on `rootA` and `/static` on `rootB`, `GET /static/x.css` returns `rootB/x.css` and `GET /a.txt` returns `rootA/a.txt`; with `spaFallback(true)` on the `/` mount, `GET /static/x.css` with `Accept: text/html` still returns `rootB/x.css`, and `GET /static/missing.css` with `Accept: text/html` receives the SPA index of the `/` mount. Decision: mounts are consulted in registration order and a miss in one mount falls through to the next, as with several Express `static` middlewares; SPA fallback runs only after every mount missed the file lookup, and then the first registered mount with `spaFallback(true)` whose prefix matches the path serves its index. [D-258; D-265]
With an explicit `GET /index.html` route and a `/` mount whose root holds `index.html`, `GET /index.html` returns the route's body. [D-259; T27]

A global middleware registered through `app.use` that sets `X-Mw: 1` runs on `GET /assets/app.js` served from a mount, the response carries `X-Mw: 1`, a global middleware that ends the response itself prevents the file from being sent, and one access-log line is written for the static request. [D-407; T35]

`GET /docs?x=1` for the directory `root/docs` is answered `301` with `Location: /docs/?x=1`; `GET /my%20docs` is answered `301` with `Location: /my%20docs/` built from the raw encoded path; and `GET //assets` is answered `404`, so no `Location` starts with `//` (a T29 case). [wave decision: SPA fallback exclusions; D-267; T29] Decision: the `301` applies to `GET` and `HEAD` of a directory without a trailing `/`, with `Location` equal to the raw path plus `/` plus `?` and the raw query when a query is present. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-6 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Method handling on static paths: 405 Allow GET, HEAD, fall-through after a route's method mismatch, OPTIONS and 501 order

acceptanceCriteria.text: Under `app.staticFiles("/", root)` with no route for the path, `POST /assets/app.js`, `PUT /assets/app.js` and `DELETE /docs/` (a directory with an index file) are answered `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD`, and the file is not sent. [D-260] Decision: a method other than `GET` or `HEAD` gets the static `405` only when a `GET` would be served; otherwise the router's answer (`404` or the route's `405`) stands. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-6 SDS-AC-8]

`OPTIONS /assets/app.js` on a static-only path is answered `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD`, the automatic `204` of D-395 applies to explicit routes only, and an unknown method token or a disabled `TRACE`/`CONNECT` on that path is answered with the router's `501` before any static mount lookup. Decision: the order is the FR-HTTP-021 AC-2 pre-check order (`OPTIONS *` `204`, raw path not starting with `/` `400`, `PathValidator` `400`, unknown-token `501`), then the router lookup with the disabled `TRACE`/`CONNECT` `501` of FR-HTTP-022 AC-4, then the static mounts, so a `PathValidator` `400` still comes before either `501`. [wave decision: OPTIONS on a static-only path; D-260; D-395]

With only `POST /login` registered and `root/login` a file, `GET /login` and `HEAD /login` are served from the mount; with `spaFallback(true)` and no file `GET /login` (with `Accept: text/html`) receives the SPA index; with no mount serving it `GET /login` receives the route's `405` with the route's own `Allow`; and `PUT /login` receives the route's `405` with the route's own `Allow`, with no `Allow` values merged. [wave decision: Static files after a route's method mismatch; D-259; D-260]

A path that a WebSocket route of the router owns is never served from a static mount or by SPA fallback, even when a file of that name exists. Decision: in wave 6, where `app.ws` does not exist yet, the test registers the WebSocket route through the internal router. [wave decision: Static files after a route's method mismatch; D-265]

The `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD` applies only when a `GET` for the same path would be answered from the file system (a file, a directory index, a directory listing or the trailing-slash `301`); SPA fallback content does not count, so under a `/` mount with `spaFallback(true)` `POST /missing`, `POST /api/typo` and `POST /.env` receive `404` (a T27 case). A path that D-052 or D-268 rejects receives `400` for every recognised, enabled method because path validation runs before method handling: `POST /a/..%2Fb` and paths with an encoded `/` or `NUL` get the `PathValidator` `400` of FR-HTTP-021; for a path that no explicit route matches and that lies under a static mount prefix, the static D-268 check runs before the static `405`/`404` method decision, so `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` and `OPTIONS` of `/%252e%252e/secret.txt` and `/a%252Fb` under a `/` mount all receive `400` (test cases). Explicit routes still take precedence: with `app.post("/:x", h)` registered, `POST /a%252Fb` reaches `h`. [residual: served only by a static mount; D-260; D-262; D-265; D-268; D-271; T27]

records.title: Directory without index, escaped directory listing, nosniff header and bounded-chunk streaming

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the default `directoryListing(false)`, `GET /empty/` for a directory without `index.html` is answered `404` with the standard error body. [D-262]

With `directoryListing(true)`, `GET /files/` for a directory holding `b.txt`, `a b.txt`, `<x>&.txt`, `.hidden` and a symbolic link is answered `200` with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8` whose links list `<x>&.txt`, `a b.txt` and `b.txt` in that order, the text showing `<x>&.txt` and the link `href` using `%3Cx%3E%26.txt` and `a%20b.txt`, with no entry for `.hidden` or the symbolic link; `GET /files/..%2F` is answered `400`, and a listing request for a directory reached through a symbolic link below the root is answered `404`. Decision: entries are sorted by `String.compareTo` on the raw, unescaped entry name before any HTML escaping or percent-encoding, so `<` (U+003C) sorts before `a` (U+0061). [D-420; D-268; D-269; D-270; D-271] Decision: a directory entry is listed with a trailing `/` in its text and `href`, and links are relative names with HTML-escaped text and a percent-encoded UTF-8 `href`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-1]

Every static `200`, `206`, `304` and listing response and every `HEAD` response from a mount carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. [D-263] Decision: `416` responses from a mount or from `res.file`/`res.download` also carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-2]

Serving a 64 MiB file from a mount keeps the used heap, measured after `System.gc()` before and during the transfer, from growing by 8 MiB or more, and the file is read through a fixed-size buffer. Decision: the copy buffer is 8192 bytes. [D-264]

records.title: SPA fallback conditions and the always-excluded /api/ and /ws/ prefixes

acceptanceCriteria.text: Under `app.staticFiles("/", root, o -> o.spaFallback(true))`, `GET /app/users/7` with `Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml` and no such file is answered `200` with the bytes of `root/index.html`. [D-265; T27] Decision: SPA fallback requires `GET` or `HEAD` and an `Accept` header containing `text/html` case-insensitively; `*/*` alone does not qualify. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-6 SDS-AC-6]

No SPA fallback is served for `GET /app/users/7` with `Accept: application/json` (answered `404`), for a path whose file exists (the file is served), for a path an explicit `GET` route matches (the route answers) or for a path a WebSocket route owns. [D-265]

`GET /api/x`, `GET /api`, `GET /ws/chat` and `GET /ws` with `Accept: text/html` and no file are answered `404`, while `GET /apix` with `Accept: text/html` receives the SPA index, because exclusions match on segment boundaries of the full request path. [D-266; D-267; wave decision: SPA fallback exclusions] Decision: the full raw request path is compared with each exclusion prefix stripped of a trailing `/`, matching when equal or followed by `/`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-6 SDS-AC-7]

After `spaExclude("/admin")`, `GET /admin/x` and `GET /api/x` with `Accept: text/html` are both answered `404`, so configured prefixes are added to `/api/` and `/ws/` and never replace them. Decision: `spaExclude` adds prefixes; `/api/` and `/ws/` are always excluded. [wave decision: SPA fallback exclusions; D-267]

records.title: Static path traversal rejected with 400 and hidden dot segments answered 404

acceptanceCriteria.text: Under `app.staticFiles("/", root)` with a file `secret.txt` beside `root`, the requests `/../secret.txt`, `/%2e%2e/secret.txt`, `/a/%2E%2E/%2E%2E/secret.txt`, `/a%2Fb`, `/a%2fb`, `/a%00.txt`, `/%252e%252e/secret.txt` and `/a%252Fb` are each answered `400`, and none of them returns the bytes of `secret.txt`. [D-268; T29] Decision: each raw segment is decoded once and answered `400` when it is `.` or `..`, holds `/` or NUL, or still holds `%2e`, `%2f` or `%00` in any case, so a second decode would produce one of those. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-6 SDS-AC-1]

D-052's `400` for `.` and `..` segments is checked first, so `/./index.html` and `/a/../index.html` are answered `400`, while `/.git/config`, `/.env` and `/assets/.hidden/x.js` (existing files) are answered `404`. records.title: Canonical-root containment, symbolic-link refusal with java.io only, allowSymlinks and the post-open re-check

acceptanceCriteria.text: Each mount computes `dir.getCanonicalFile()` once when the app starts listening, and an opened file whose canonical path is not under that canonical root is refused with `404`; a mount whose root directory is reached through a symbolic link (a test creates `link -> realRoot` and mounts `link`) serves the regular files of `realRoot`, while a symbolic link inside it is refused. [D-269; D-411] Decision: containment compares canonical paths with the root path plus the separator, so `/root2` is not under `/root`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-5]

By default a file reached through a symbolic link below the canonical root is answered `404`, also when the link points to a file inside the root; detection uses `java.io` only, comparing each path component's canonical path with its parent's canonical path plus its name, and no class of the resolver references `java.nio.file`. Decision: a refused file is answered `404`, the same as a missing file. [D-270; T29]

With `allowSymlinks(true)`, a symbolic link below the root whose target lies inside the canonical root is served `200`, and a symbolic link whose target lies outside the canonical root is still answered `404`. [D-272; D-269]

After opening a file for a static mount, `res.file` or `res.download`, the resolver recomputes the opened file's canonical path and the symbolic-link component check and, when either fails, closes the stream and refuses the file; a T29 test swaps a path component for a symbolic link to a directory outside the root through a test hook between the first check and the open, and the response does not contain the outside file's bytes. [D-447; carried: V1-008; T29] Decision: when the re-check after open finds a change the stream is closed and `FileNotFoundException` is thrown, answered `404`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-3]

For `res.file(file)` and `res.download(file, name)`, which have no mount, the root of the component check is the canonical form of `file.getAbsoluteFile().getParentFile()`: a named file that is itself a symbolic link is refused, a directory or missing file is refused, ancestors above that parent (such as Android's `/sdcard` link) are not checked, and the post-open re-check compares the canonical path before and after opening. Decision: a refused `res.file`/`res.download` target is answered `404` through the error path with the standard error body. [wave decision: The root of res.file and res.download; D-447; D-270; D-409] Decision: the refusal is a `FileNotFoundException` from the resolver, mapped to `HttpException(404)` by the response. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-4]

The T29 swap test runs in a JVM started with `-Dsun.io.useCanonCaches=false`, set in the Gradle test task, because a Java 8 JVM caches canonical paths for up to 30 seconds otherwise. [wave decision: Java 8 canonical-path cache; D-447; D-411] Decision: the swap test asserts that the property is set. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: MIME lookup order, built-in table, case-insensitive extensions, text charset and the per-app registry

acceptanceCriteria.text: For an extension `foo` registered as `application/x-mount` through `options.mime`, as `application/x-app` through `app.mimeTypes()` and absent from the built-in table, the mount serves `a.foo` as `application/x-mount`; without the mount entry it serves `application/x-app`; an extension found only in the built-in table (`js`) gets the built-in type; and `a.unknownext` gets `application/octet-stream`. [D-273; T28] Decision: the extension is the text after the last `.` of the file name, and a name without `.` or ending in `.` gets `application/octet-stream`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-7]
A test parses the MIME table of `docs/api/static.md` and asserts that the built-in table holds exactly those extension-to-type entries, no more and no fewer. [D-274]

`APP.JS`, `app.Js` and `app.js` all resolve to the same type, `mime("SVG", ...)` and `register("Svg", ...)` match `x.svg`, and `mime(".data", ...)`, `mime("data", ...)`, `register(".webp", ...)` and `register("webp", ...)` each match a file with that extension. [D-275; D-277]

A `.css` file is sent as `text/css; charset=UTF-8`, a `.html` file as `text/html; charset=UTF-8`, an extension registered as `text/x-custom` as `text/x-custom; charset=UTF-8`, and a `.png` file as `image/png` without a charset parameter. [D-276] Decision: a registered type that already has parameters or a charset is sent unchanged; only a bare `text/*` type gains `; charset=UTF-8`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-7 SDS-AC-8]

`app.mimeTypes().register("webp", "image/webp").register("avif", "image/avif")` chains on the same registry; in a process with two apps, a type registered on one app does not change the type the other app sends for that extension, and the built-in table is an unmodifiable map that registration does not change. [D-277; T28]

records.title: CachePolicy values, res.cache, static cache patterns and the server-wide default Cache-Control

acceptanceCriteria.text: `noStore()`, `noCache()`, `privateFor(10, MINUTES)` and `publicFor(1, HOURS)` give the header values `no-store`, `no-cache`, `private, max-age=600` and `public, max-age=3600`, `publicFor(365, DAYS).immutable()` gives `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and the policy on which `immutable()` was called still gives its old value. [D-278; D-279; T32]

A handler calling `res.cache(CachePolicy.noStore())` sends `Cache-Control: no-store`, and a second `res.cache(...)` call before commit replaces the value. Decision: the last `res.cache` call before commit wins. [D-280]

With `options.cache("**/*.html", noCache())` and `options.cache("/assets/**", publicFor(365, DAYS).immutable())` on a `/` mount, `/index.html` and `/docs/a.html` carry `Cache-Control: no-cache` and `/assets/app.js` carries `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. [D-281; T32]

Decision: a pattern is matched against the path relative to the mount prefix, beginning with `/`; a pattern not starting with `/` is matched as if prefixed by `**/`; `*` matches within one segment; `**` matches zero or more segments, so `**/*.html` matches `/index.html`; and when several patterns match, the first registered wins. Under a `/static` mount, `/assets/**` matches the request `/static/assets/x.js`, `*.css` matches `/static/a/b.css`, and with `/assets/**` registered before `**/*.js` the request `/static/assets/x.js` gets the first policy. [D-282] Decision: `*` matches `[^/]*`, `**/` matches zero or more segments, and the pattern must match the whole mount-relative path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-3]

With the default `defaultCache(null)`, a JSON route and a static file without a matching pattern send no `Cache-Control`; with `defaultCache(CachePolicy.noCache())`, both send `Cache-Control: no-cache`, while a route calling `res.cache(noStore())`, a route calling `res.header("Cache-Control", "max-age=5")`, a static file matching an `options.cache` pattern and a static file served after a global middleware called `res.header("Cache-Control", "private")` keep their own value. Decision: `defaultCache` is applied at commit only when the response holds no `Cache-Control` at that moment, whatever set it, so a header set by the framework itself (such as the SSE header of D-326, verified with SSE in wave 7) is kept by the same rule. [D-410; T32] Decision: `defaultCache` applies to every response without `Cache-Control` at commit, error and `304` responses included. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: ETag, Last-Modified and Accept-Ranges on file responses, conditional 304 precedence and HEAD

acceptanceCriteria.text: A static `GET`, a `res.file` and a `res.download` response for a 1234-byte file whose modification time is `1700000000123` ms carry `ETag: "4d2-18bcfe5687b"`, `Last-Modified: Tue, 14 Nov 2023 22:13:20 GMT` (truncated to whole seconds) and `Accept-Ranges: bytes`. Decision: the ETag is strong and has the form `"<hex length>-<hex lastModified millis>"`. [D-283; T30]

`If-None-Match` carrying the current ETag, a list containing it, its weak form `W/"..."` or `*` gives `304` with no body, the same `ETag` and the same `Cache-Control` that the `200` for that file carries (from `options.cache` or `defaultCache`, as RFC 9110 §15.4.5 requires), also when an `If-Modified-Since` older than the file is present; a non-matching `If-None-Match` gives `200` even when `If-Modified-Since` would match. Decision: `If-None-Match` uses the weak comparison of RFC 9110. [D-284; T30] Decision: for a method other than `GET` or `HEAD` (such as `res.file` in a `POST` handler), `If-None-Match`, `If-Modified-Since`, `Range` and `If-Range` are ignored and the full `200` is sent. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-5]

Without `If-None-Match`, an `If-Modified-Since` equal to or later than the truncated `Last-Modified` gives `304` with no body, an earlier one gives `200` with the full body, and an unparsable date is ignored (`200`). [D-285; T30] Decision: `If-Modified-Since` is parsed as IMF-fixdate (RFC 850 and asctime also accepted) and compared in whole seconds with the file's modified time divided by 1000. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-6]

`HEAD` for a static file carries the same status, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, `Accept-Ranges`, `Cache-Control` and `X-Content-Type-Options` as `GET` for that file and no body bytes. [D-286; T30]

records.title: Single byte ranges 206 and 416, multi or malformed ranges 200, If-Range and the combined Range and cache test

acceptanceCriteria.text: For a 1000-byte file, `Range: bytes=0-99` gives `206` with `Content-Range: bytes 0-99/1000`, `Content-Length: 100` and those 100 bytes; `bytes=900-` gives bytes 900 to 999; `bytes=-50` gives the last 50 bytes; and `bytes=990-5000` is clipped to `Content-Range: bytes 990-999/1000` with 10 bytes. [D-287; T31] Decision: `Range` applies to `GET` only; a `HEAD` with `Range` gets the `200` headers. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-7]

For a 1000-byte file, `Range: bytes=1000-` and `bytes=2000-2100` give `416` with `Content-Range: bytes */1000` and the standard error body. [D-288; T31] Decision: the `416` carries the same `ETag` and `Last-Modified` as the `200`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-8]
`Range: bytes=0-9,20-29`, `Range: bytes=abc`, `Range: items=0-9` and `Range: bytes=50-10` each give the full `200` response with all 1000 bytes. [D-289; T31]

With `Range: bytes=0-99`, an `If-Range` equal to the current strong ETag or to the current `Last-Modified` date gives `206`, while an `If-Range` holding another ETag, an older date or a weak ETag `W/"..."` gives the full `200`. Decision: an HTTP-date `If-Range` matches only when it equals `Last-Modified` exactly. [D-290; T31] Decision: a date `If-Range` holds only when its seconds equal the `Last-Modified` seconds. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-9]

A combined test asserts that a `206` response carries the same `ETag`, `Last-Modified` and `Cache-Control` as the full `200` for that file, that a `Range` request whose `If-None-Match` matches the current ETag receives `304` without a body, and that a `Range` request with a matching strong `If-Range` receives `206`. [D-432; T30; T31]

records.requirement: The system shall answer a single satisfiable byte range of a static, `res.file` or `res.download` response with `206` and `Content-Range`, clipping an end beyond the file length, answer a single range starting at or beyond the length with `416` and `Content-Range: bytes */<length>`, answer several ranges or a malformed `Range` header with the full `200`, and answer an `If-Range` that differs from the current validator or is a weak ETag with the full `200`.
