records.title: res.file and res.download bodies, Content-Disposition, engine-free evaluation and bodies from the opened stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: `res.file(new File(dir, "report.pdf"))` answers `200` with `Content-Type: application/pdf`, the file bytes and no `Content-Disposition` header, and honours `Range` and conditional headers like a static file. [D-293; D-283; D-287] Decision: the type comes only from the app `MimeTypes` and the built-in table, and conditionals and `Range` are evaluated like a static file. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-11]

`res.download(file, "report.pdf")` sends `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="report.pdf"`; for the filename `a\r\nSet-Cookie: x=1".pdf` the header value contains no CR, LF, double quote, backslash or other control character and no `Set-Cookie` header appears in the response. Decision: a non-ASCII filename is also sent as `filename*=UTF-8''` with percent-encoded bytes next to an ASCII `filename` fallback whose non-ASCII characters are replaced by `_`. [D-292] Decision: the sanitiser drops CR, LF, `"`, `\` and other control characters, replaces non-ASCII characters by `_` in `filename`, and adds `filename*` only when the name has non-ASCII characters. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-10]

The Range, ETag and conditional evaluation classes live in `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal`, reference no adapter, TinyHttpd or Servlet type (core isolation check of CON-BUILD-013), and the T30 and T31 tests pass over the in-memory test adapter and over TinyHttpd. [D-291]

Static, `res.file` and `res.download` bodies are written from the `InputStream` the resolver opened and re-checked, skipped to the range start and limited to the range length, through `HttpExchange.commit`; a recording test adapter shows that `HttpExchange.sendFile(...)` is never called for them, and the `HttpExchange` SPI signatures are unchanged. [wave decision: File bodies come from the opened stream; D-291; D-264; D-106] Decision: the range start is reached by a loop over `InputStream.skip` and then `read`, failing with `IOException` if the file holds fewer bytes. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-8 SDS-AC-12]

Static mounts, `res.file` and `res.download` all read through the built-in `java.io.File` `ResourceResolver`, which a test checks by observing its `open`, `length`, `etag` and `modified` calls for each of the three. [D-409]

records.title: Servlet adapter lifecycle: the container initialises the app with onStart and destroys it with shutdown, binds no socket and reports port 0

acceptanceCriteria.text: On the embedded container, context startup builds the app through the configurer and calls `app.listen(0)` before the first request: `onStart` callbacks have run once, `app.state()` is `RUNNING` and a request is served. [D-359]

Context destruction runs `app.shutdown(10, SECONDS)` (or the `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` value): `onStop` callbacks run, the state is `TERMINATED`, `ServletAdapter.stop` and `release` have been called, `shutdown` returns within that timeout plus the margin of `docs/api/lifecycle.md`, and a second destruction is harmless. [D-359]

`ServletAdapter.boundPort()` throws `IllegalStateException` before any `bind` (the SPI contract of `HttpAdapter.boundPort`) and returns `0` after `bind`; `bind("127.0.0.1", 8080, handler)` and `bind(settings, handler)` return without starting a thread or opening a socket and ignore host and port, which a test asserts for the adapter alone; `ServerHandle.port()` of the app is `0`. [D-359; D-107; r3 W2-001]
A user call of `app.listen(8080)` on an app built with a `ServletAdapter` binds nothing, runs `onStart` and reaches `RUNNING` through the same path as the initializer. [D-359; r2 W2-001]

When `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` is on the web application's class path the initializer finds it by reflection and presets it as the codec; the configurer may replace it with `Builder.jsonCodec`; when neither exists startup fails with a `ServletException` whose message contains `com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec` and `jsonCodec`. The module `runtimeClasspath` stays `NaruServe-api` only. [r5 W2-002; I-005]

The app logger is the `ConsoleLogger` that `RestApp.Builder` defaults to when the configurer does not call `Builder.logger`, and a logger that the configurer sets is the one the app keeps. [r4 W2-003; FR-ENGINE-009]
A failing `onStart` callback (an `AppStartException` from `listen`) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` that carries it as cause, and no thread of the app remains. [D-359; I-015]

Deviation (recorded): the frozen D-416 thread total of 451 (452 with the keeper thread, PERF-APP-001 AC-2) bounds the embedded TinyHttpd app; on the Servlet adapter the threads are the container's plus at most `maxSseStreams` SSE threads (FR-SVL-005), and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-416]

records.requirement: The system shall start the app on the Servlet adapter when the container initialises the web application — the initializer installs the `ServletAdapter`, finds the Gson codec by reflection, calls the configurer and then `app.listen(0)`, so `onStart` runs and the state becomes `RUNNING` exactly as on the embedded engine — and shall run `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` with the timeout of `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` (default 10) when the container destroys the web application; `ServletAdapter.bind` stores the handler and opens no socket, and `boundPort()` and `ServerHandle.port()` are `0`.
records.rationale: Covers D-359, wave decisions Servlet start path (r2 W2-001), Port on the Servlet adapter (r3 W2-001, which supersedes the first-request port of round 2), Servlet bind (r4 W2-006), Gson on the Servlet adapter (r5 W2-002) and the D-107 bind contract. Measured (2026-10-20): `HttpAdapter.bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` defaults to `bind(host, port, handler)` (`spi/HttpAdapter.java:20-29`); `DefaultRestApp.start` reads `a.boundPort()` once right after bind (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:506-507`) and `ServerHandle.port()` returns that captured value; `RestApp.Builder.build()` throws `IllegalStateException` without `httpAdapter` or `jsonCodec`; the module `runtimeClasspath` is `NaruServe-api` only (CON-BUILD-006 AC-5). Decision: the destroy callback is a `ServletContextListener` that the initializer adds with `addListener`; a user call of `listen(int)` on an app holding the Servlet adapter takes the same path and binds nothing; `docs/api/servlet.md` tells the reader to take the port from the container. The logger is the one the configurer sets, otherwise the Builder default `ConsoleLogger`, which is also what `RestApp.create()` picks on a JVM without `android.util.Log` (FR-ENGINE-009). Pitfall: because `boundPort()` is read once, a port learned from the first request would never reach `ServerHandle`; round 3 therefore fixed `0`. Pitfall: `Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.gson.GsonJsonCodec")` must use the web application's class loader, not the module's, when the container isolates them. Rejected alternative: a `compileOnly` or `runtimeOnly` dependency on `NaruServe-gson` so the codec is a normal import; it would break the `runtimeClasspath` pin of CON-BUILD-006 AC-5 and I-005.

records.title: Servlet request mapping: raw path minus context path and servlet mapping, raw query, headers, and the same application types as on the embedded engine

acceptanceCriteria.text: With context path `/app` and pattern `/api/*`, a request to `/app/api/users/%41;v=1?x=%20` reaches a route `/users/:id` with `req.rawPath()` equal to `/users/%41;v=1`, `req.param("id")` equal to `A;v=1` and `req.query("x")` equal to a space; with pattern `/*` or `/` the same request without `/api` reaches the same route, and a request to the bare servlet root reaches the route `/` (empty remainder is `/`). [D-363; D-399]

A request whose raw URI does not start with the context path plus the registered prefix at a segment boundary (a test sends `/app/%61pi/users` to pattern `/api/*`) is answered `404` with the standard error body and a request id, and `getServletPath()`, `getPathInfo()` and `getParameter*` are never read, which a recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy asserts. [D-363; r3 W2-004]

Headers reach `req.header(name)` and `req.headers(name)` with repeated names kept in their per-name order (the Servlet API gives no cross-name order), `Cookie` request headers reach the core cookie parser unchanged (`req.cookie("s")` returns a NaruServe `Cookie`, never `javax.servlet.http.Cookie`), `req.remoteAddress()` is `getRemoteAddr()` and `req.isSecure()` is `isSecure()`; `app.trustProxy(true)` takes effect in the core (FR-ENGINE-008). [D-360]

A shared case suite — route parameters, query decoding, JSON body and `res.json`, cookies read and written, `404`, `405` with `Allow`, automatic `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`, middleware order, `onError` and the standard error body, `res.file` — runs on the Servlet adapter and on the in-memory adapter with identical statuses and bodies, using the same app definition code, so application code needs no change between engines. [D-360; I-021]

The path-rejection cases of D-052 (malformed percent-encoding, invalid UTF-8, an encoded `/`, an encoded or raw `NUL`, `.` and `..` segments raw and encoded) sent as raw request lines to the embedded container are answered `400`, or `404` when the container normalises the path and never reaches the servlet, and never `2xx`; the `OPTIONS *` request is sent too, and the observed status of every case is recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`. [D-052; I-021]
Header values the framework writes never contain CR or LF on this adapter, and security-related log lines of the adapter carry no token, session id or file content. [I-016; I-017]

records.requirement: The system shall map each servlet request to the `HttpExchange` values the core expects — `methodToken`, the raw `getRequestURI()` with the context path and the url-pattern prefix the initializer registered stripped at a segment boundary and kept percent-encoded, the raw `getQueryString()`, `getProtocol()`, every header value with duplicates kept and per-name order preserved, `getRemoteAddr()`, `isSecure()` and `getInputStream()` — so that routes, middleware, `Request`, `Response` and `Cookie` behave as on the embedded engine.
records.rationale: Covers D-360, D-363 (path handling), D-399, D-052, wave decisions Servlet path edge cases (r2 W2-003) and Servlet path and WebSocket answer (r3 W2-004: the remainder is the request URI minus the context path minus the url-pattern prefix, not `getServletPath()`), and I-021. Measured: `HttpExchange.rawPath()` is "the raw request-target path, undecoded" and `httpVersion()` is the request-line version such as `HTTP/1.1` (`spi/HttpExchange.java:27-37`). Decision: context path `/app`, pattern `/api/*` and URI `/app/api/users/%41;v=1` give the path `/users/%41;v=1`; patterns `/*` and `/` strip nothing after the context path; an empty remainder is the path `/`; path parameters (`;name=value`) stay in the path as in Express; when the raw URI does not start with the context path plus the prefix at a segment boundary (the remainder must be empty or start with `/`) the adapter answers `404` with the standard error body through the `ErrorRenderer` of the settings. Pitfall: containers match servlet mappings on the decoded path, so `/app/%61pi/x` can reach the servlet while the raw prefix `/api` does not match; `getServletPath()` and `getPathInfo()` are decoded and normalised and must not be used (D-399). Pitfall: `getParameter*` would consume a form body (FR-SVL-004). Rejected alternative: matching the prefix on the decoded path; it would let an encoded segment change which handler runs.

records.title: Servlet response writing: commit, finish, abort, sendFile and a single start per exchange

acceptanceCriteria.text: A handler's `res.status(201).header("X-A", "1").send("ok")` reaches the client as status `201`, header `X-A: 1` and body `ok` with the `Content-Length` the core set; a `res.stream` response of unknown length arrives with an intact body and without a `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` conflict (chunked framing is asserted only for a body larger than the container's output buffer or after a flush, because a container may buffer a small body and frame it with a length); and no error page of the container appears for a `404` or `500` the core produced, because `sendError` is never called. [D-360]
A HEAD request to a GET route returns the `Content-Length` of the GET body and no body bytes, and a `204` and a `304` carry no body, on the embedded container. [D-360; FR-HTTP-017]

After `abort()` the next body write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException` (a write already blocked inside the container ends only by the container's write timeout, FR-SVL-006 AC-3), `abort()` called twice is harmless and `abort()` may run on another thread than the writer; a second `commit`, `sendFile` or `eventStream` on one exchange throws `IllegalStateException`. [r2 W2-006]

`res.file` and `res.download` on a file serve the whole file, a single `Range` (`206` with `Content-Range`) and a `416`, byte for byte equal to the in-memory adapter, with `sendFile` copying in chunks of at most 64 KiB, which a spy output stream records, and never reading the file into memory; the class references no `java.nio.file` type. [D-360; FR-STATIC-010]
Response header order on the wire is the container's, `docs/api/servlet.md` says so, and no test of the shared case suite depends on header order. [r2 W2-006]

traceLinks.notes: file bodies from the opened file

changeNotes.reason: Feasibility=medium (score 79) at assessment; its stated conditions were addressed by SRS text fixes before promotion (blocker: adapter 'never adds' Content-Length but AC-1 admits Jetty may add a length for small buffered bodies). Run: 2026-10-20.NaruServe.wave-8.v01

records.requirement: The system shall write each response through the container's `HttpServletResponse` — `commit` sets the status with `setStatus` and writes each header with `addHeader` in the given order, and `Content-Length` with `setHeader` exactly as the core gave it, without `sendError`, never itself adds, removes or changes `Content-Length` (its own code never calls `setContentLength`; a container may still frame a small buffered body with a length), and returns the container's output stream; `finish` completes the response; `abort` marks the exchange aborted so that every later write, `commit` or `finish` throws `IOException`; `sendFile` writes exactly `length` bytes of the file from `offset` in bounded chunks; and a second start of the same exchange throws `IllegalStateException`.
records.rationale: Covers D-360 (the `Response` behaviour is the core's; the adapter must not alter it), wave decision Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006: `abort()` marks the exchange aborted and later writes throw `IOException` because the container owns the socket; response header order is the container's) and the SPI contract of `HttpExchange.commit`, `abort` (idempotent, thread-safe) and `sendFile`. Measured: `spi/HttpExchange.java:55-75` states that the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`, that header chars are at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, and that `abort()` may run on any thread while another thread is writing. Decision: header values are written with `addHeader` as given and the `Content-Length` header the core provides with `setHeader` (one rule, no `setContentLength`); the status is set with `setStatus` so the container renders no error page; `abort` does not close the container's socket (the container owns it) and does not call `sendError`; `sendFile` uses `java.io` only (no `java.nio.file`, CON-HTTP-002) and a buffer of at most 64 KiB. Pitfall: `HttpServletResponse.setContentLength` and containers that compute a length for small bodies can change `Content-Length`; the core's header is passed through `setHeader`, and a HEAD response keeps the length the GET body would have had (FR-HTTP-017). Rejected alternative: closing the connection from `abort` through container-specific APIs; it is not portable across containers.

records.title: Servlet multipart and form bodies go through the core parser over the request input stream

acceptanceCriteria.text: On the embedded container, a multipart request with two files and a text field returns the same `req.file`, `req.files`, `req.form` and `req.parts` values as on the in-memory adapter, and a urlencoded form returns its fields, using the shared case suite of FR-SVL-002. [D-363; FR-MULTIPART-003]

A recording `HttpServletRequest` proxy shows that during these requests the adapter reads `getInputStream()` and never calls `getParts`, `getPart`, `getParameter`, `getParameterMap`, `getParameterNames` or `getParameterValues`, and the registered servlet has no multipart configuration. [r1 W2-007; r4 W2-005]

A multipart body above the `app.multipart` file size, part count or total limit is answered `413`, a urlencoded form above `app.formLimit` is answered `413` and a JSON body above `app.jsonLimit` is answered `413`, each with the standard error body, and after the response no upload temporary file of the app remains in `tempDirectory`. [D-363; FR-MULTIPART-002; I-015]

A client that closes the connection in the middle of a multipart upload leaves no upload temporary file after the request ends (T17 on this adapter), which a test asserts by listing `tempDirectory` after the container's request thread returned. [FR-MULTIPART-006; I-015]

records.requirement: The system shall serve multipart and urlencoded request bodies on the Servlet adapter through the core parser reading `requestBody()`, the container's input stream, and shall never call `getParts()`, `getPart(...)`, `getParameter*`, or register the servlet with a `MultipartConfig`, so the `app.multipart`, `formLimit` and `jsonLimit` limits of the core apply as on the embedded engine.
records.rationale: Covers D-363 (multipart support) and wave decision Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007: multipart uses the core parser over the request input stream, not the Servlet `Part` API; `jsonLimit`, `formLimit` and the multipart limits still apply in the core (the wave decision's "body limit"; `RestApp` has no other body limit setting)), r4 W2-005 (no multipart configuration) and I-015. Measured: `internal/MultipartParser.java` is the engine-free parser shared by every adapter (FR-MULTIPART-001). Pitfall: on a POST with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `getParameter*` makes the container read and consume the body, leaving the core an empty stream; the adapter must not touch it. Pitfall: a servlet registered with a `MultipartConfig` makes some containers parse multipart before the servlet and write temp files the core cannot clean. Rejected alternative: `getParts()` with `MultipartConfig` limits; it would duplicate the limits (container versus `app.multipart`) and break the one-parser rule of FR-MULTIPART-001.

records.title: Servlet SSE under AsyncContext: bounded stream counter, dedicated executor and no async timeout

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `maxSseStreams(2)` and two open streams, a third request whose handler calls `res.sse()` receives `503` with the standard error body and its request id, because the adapter's counter throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started; after one stream ends a new `res.sse()` is accepted, and the counter is released also when the drain fails with `IOException` and when the exchange is aborted. [D-361; r3 W2-002]

The drain runs on a thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>` that is a daemon and not a container pool thread, the container request thread has returned from `service()` while the stream is open (a test records both thread ids and the return), and the executor never holds more than `maxSseStreams` threads. [D-361; D-106]

The servlet is registered with `asyncSupported=true`; a test filter in front of the servlet records, after the handler called `res.sse()`, that `request.getAsyncContext().getTimeout()` is `0` for every stream; and a stream kept open longer than the container's default async timeout (the test lowers it to 1 s) still receives a heartbeat after 2.5 s and is not ended by the container. [r4 W2-005]

An event sent from another thread after the handler returned reaches the client within 500 ms of the `send`, a `: ping` heartbeat reaches an idle client within `heartbeatInterval` plus 500 ms, and an event sent by the handler thread before the drain starts reaches the client while the handler still runs, each flushed without further writes behind it. [D-361; D-406; FR-SSE-002]

When the drain ends (client close, `close()` or the core's end report) `AsyncContext.complete()` is called, the stream's `onClose` listeners run once, and `abort()` on an SSE exchange also calls `AsyncContext.complete()`. [D-361; r5 W2-001]

A stream whose client closed its socket is detected by the next write or heartbeat failing with `IOException`, ends with the access-log cause `client` and returns its executor thread within two heartbeat intervals plus 1 s. [D-361; FR-SSE-004]

changeNotes.reason: Feasibility=medium (score 72) at assessment; its stated conditions were addressed by SRS text fixes before promotion (blocker: AC-3 is not discriminating on Jetty 9.4.58: a committed stream survives the 1 s default timeout without setTimeout). Run: 2026-10-20.NaruServe.wave-8.v01

records.requirement: The system shall implement `HttpExchange.eventStream` on the Servlet adapter so that the exchange counts open streams against `maxSseStreams` (default 128) and answers `503` before the exchange is marked started when the bound is reached, otherwise calls `startAsync()` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)`, commits status and headers, hands the container's output stream to `StreamDrain.attach`, runs the core drain loop on a dedicated bounded executor owned by the adapter — daemon threads named `naruserve-servlet-sse-<n>`, at most `maxSseStreams`, never the container's pool threads — returns at once so the container's request thread is released after the handler returned, and completes the `AsyncContext` when the drain ends.
records.rationale: Covers D-361, D-106 (the event-stream point), wave decisions SSE bound and thread owner on the Servlet adapter (r3 W2-002) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005: `asyncSupported=true` and `AsyncContext.setTimeout(0)` per stream), and I-012 and I-015. Measured: `spi/StreamDrain.java` is the core-owned drain loop type with `attach(OutputStream)`; FR-SSE-003 fixes the TinyHttpd mirror (counter that throws a `503` `HttpException` before the exchange is marked started, drain on the request worker). Decision: the Servlet counter is the adapter's own, with the same `maxSseStreams` of the frozen `ServerSettings`; the executor is created at `bind(ServerSettings, handler)`; heartbeat and event writes are flushed after each write so the container does not buffer them. Frozen: D-106 says the adapter chooses the thread that runs the loop ("an `AsyncContext` on the Servlet adapter"). Deviation (recorded): the loop runs on an adapter-owned executor thread, not on the container's request thread; a container pool thread blocked for the life of a stream would exhaust the pool, and the 128-thread bound keeps I-012 (no unbounded default). Deviation (recorded, inherited from FR-SSE-002 for D-406): sends made inside the handler before the drain starts are written directly on the handler thread, synchronised on the exchange, as on TinyHttpd. Pitfall: the default async timeout of a container (30 s on Jetty 9.4) would end a long stream with a `500`, hence `setTimeout(0)`. Pitfall: checking the counter after the exchange is marked started leaves the dispatcher unable to commit the `503` (r3 W2-001 of wave 7). Rejected alternative: running the drain on the container thread with a blocking loop; it holds one container thread per stream.

records.title: Servlet stop and release: refuse new requests, wait for in-flight exchanges to the deadline, then cut the rest

acceptanceCriteria.text: With one slow plain request in flight, `stop(2, SECONDS)` makes a new request answer `503` with `Connection: close` and the standard error body at once, returns as soon as the slow request finishes (before the deadline), and a request that outlasts the deadline does not make `stop` return later than the deadline plus 1 s. [D-359; r3 W2-003]

With open SSE streams, `shutdown` delivers the closing notice of FR-SSE-005 through the core, each stream's client sees the end of the chunked body within the shutdown timeout plus the D-344 margin, the `AsyncContext` of each stream is completed, and the executor is shut down. [D-359; FR-SSE-005]

A stream whose client stopped reading is cut at the deadline: `stop` returns within the deadline plus 1 s and the stream's `AsyncContext` is completed, so the container closes the output (Jetty frees a blocked writer at once, another container at its own write timeout, which the test does not wait for); the deviation sentence is present in `docs/api/servlet.md` and `docs/api/sse.md` gains a pointer to it. [r5 W2-001]

`release()` detaches the handler (later requests are answered `503`), `stop` and `release` are idempotent, `stop` before `bind` is harmless, and after `shutdown` returns a test finds no thread named `naruserve-servlet-sse-*` alive within 2 s and no upload temporary file of the app. [D-107; I-015]
Every test of the module that starts the container asserts after shutdown that no server thread and no temporary upload file of that app remains (a shared test rule). [I-015]

changeNotes.reason: Feasibility=medium (score 75) at assessment; its stated conditions were addressed by SRS text fixes before promotion (blocker: AC-3 needs a non-reading client filling TCP buffers (flaky); its premise is pessimistic, complete() frees the writer). Run: 2026-10-20.NaruServe.wave-8.v01

records.requirement: The system shall implement `HttpAdapter.stop(timeout, unit)` on the Servlet adapter so that it first refuses new requests with `503` and `Connection: close`, then waits for the in-flight exchanges until the deadline, and at the deadline calls `shutdownNow()` on the SSE executor and `AsyncContext.complete()` on every stream still open; and `release()` detaches the handler, so that after shutdown no `naruserve-servlet-sse-*` thread and no upload temporary file of the app remains.
records.rationale: Covers D-359 (shutdown on container destroy), D-107 (two-call stop), wave decisions Servlet stop (r3 W2-003) and Blocked writes of a Servlet SSE stream (r5 W2-001), and I-012, I-015. Measured: the core shutdown sequence runs the before-wait participants (the SSE and WebSocket closing participants, FR-SSE-005) and then `adapter.stop(left(deadline))` (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:682` `a.stop`, `:705` `a.release`, FR-APP-011). Deviation (recorded under I-012): a drain thread stuck in a socket write to a client that stopped reading is bounded only by the container's own write timeout, which the adapter does not control; the "cut at timeout" promise of `docs/api/sse.md` therefore holds on the Servlet adapter up to that container bound, and the release documentation lists the deviation (OPS-REL-007). Decision: the adapter counts in-flight `service()` calls and open streams under one lock and waits on its condition; refusing by `503` happens before the core handler runs, using the `ErrorRenderer` of the settings. Pitfall: `stop` called from the container's destroy callback may run on a container thread, so it must not wait for container-owned work beyond the deadline. Rejected alternative: interrupting container request threads at the deadline; interrupting a thread the container owns is unsafe.

records.title: WebSocket is not supported on the Servlet adapter: an upgrade request answers 501, other requests keep 426

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request with `Upgrade: websocket`, `Connection: Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` and a valid key to a path with an `app.ws` route, on the embedded container, receives `501` with the standard error body (a `code`, a `message` and the request id), never `101` and never `500`, and no WebSocket session or upgraded connection is registered. [D-363; r3 W2-004]

A request without `Upgrade` to the same path receives `426` with `Upgrade: websocket`, a request with a rejected `Origin` receives the core's `403` before any `501`, and a request to the same path with a method other than GET keeps its core answer. [FR-WS-003; FR-WS-004]

`ServletExchange.upgrade(headers, handler)` also throws `HttpException(501)`; a unit test calls both methods on an exchange and asserts the status of the exception and that the exchange stays unstarted, so a later `commit` still works. [D-363]

`docs/api/servlet.md` states that WebSocket is not supported on the Servlet adapter in v1, that `app.ws` routes answer `501` there and that the embedded engine serves them, which a docs test asserts. [D-363]

records.requirement: The system shall answer a real WebSocket upgrade request to a route registered with `app.ws` on the Servlet adapter with status `501` and the standard JSON error body, because `ServletExchange.webSocket` (and `upgrade`) throw `HttpException(501)` instead of the SPI default that leads to `500`, while a request without an upgrade to a path that has only an `app.ws` route keeps the core's `426`.
records.rationale: Covers D-363 (WebSocket support) and wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007: Servlet 3.1 has no WebSocket API, so a route registered with `app.ws` answers `501` with the standard JSON error body and `docs/api/servlet.md` says it is not supported in v1) and Servlet path and WebSocket answer (r3 W2-004: `HttpException(501)` because the SPI default would lead to `500`; this applies only to real upgrade requests). Measured: `HttpExchange.webSocket` defaults to throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` (`spi/HttpExchange.java:99-101`), which the core maps to `500`; the core checks Origin before the upgrade extension point (FR-WS-003) and answers `426` for a non-upgrade request before any adapter call (FR-WS-004). Deviation (recorded, for D-408 over TinyHttpd): TinyHttpd replaces `Connection: Upgrade` on a non-`101` response (FR-WS-004 AC-2); on the Servlet adapter the headers pass through `addHeader` to the container, so the test records whether `Connection: Upgrade` reaches the client and asserts `426` and `Upgrade: websocket` only. Rejected alternative: bridging to `javax.websocket` (it is `compileOnly` in the module); the Servlet adapter would then depend on a container-specific endpoint registration and WebSocket stays a v1 non-goal here.

records.title: Servlet adapter keeps maxSseStreams and the error renderer from the settings and ignores the embedded-engine server options

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds that `ServletAdapter` declares its own `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)`, and a test shows that the adapter used `maxSseStreams(3)` (a fourth stream is refused, FR-SVL-005) and the settings' `ErrorRenderer` (a custom renderer's body appears in the adapter's own `503` and `404` answers). [r4 W2-006; D-363]

A test sets `allowedHosts("example.test")`, `bindAddress("10.255.255.1")`, `maxWorkers(1)` and `maxHeaderSize(1024)` on the app and shows the Servlet adapter serves a request with another `Host` header and a normal header block unchanged, so these settings have no effect there. [r2 W2-006]

The core limits still apply: a JSON body above `app.jsonLimit` answers `413`, a urlencoded form above `app.formLimit` answers `413` and a multipart request above the `app.multipart` limits answers `413`, each with the standard error body, on the embedded container. [D-363; r1 W2-007]

`docs/api/servlet.md` lists the 13 ignored `ServerOptions` settings by exactly the names above and the applied settings (`jsonLimit`, `formLimit`, `app.multipart`, `maxSseStreams`, the SSE options, `trustProxy`), and a docs test checks that every listed name exists on `ServerOptions` or `RestApp`, so the list cannot drift. [D-363]

`docs/api/servlet.md` states that the core's LAN warning for a non-loopback `bindAddress` and `ServerHandle.address()` describe the configured setting, not the container's connector, and a test shows that a default app logs no such warning on the Servlet adapter. [r2 W2-006]

traceLinks.notes: allowedHosts and bind outcomes in TinyHttpd

records.requirement: The system shall override `HttpAdapter.bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` on the Servlet adapter to keep the frozen settings it uses — `maxSseStreams` and the `ErrorRenderer` (and logger) — while `bind(host, port, handler)` only stores the handler, and shall ignore every `ServerOptions` setting that configures the embedded engine (`bindAddress`, `allowedHosts`, `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxRequestLineLength`, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `minBodyRate`, `maxWorkers`, `maxConnections`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and `maxConnectionsPerAddress`), listed as ignored in `docs/api/servlet.md`, while `jsonLimit`, `formLimit` and the `app.multipart` limits still apply in the core.
records.rationale: Covers D-359, D-363, wave decisions Servlet adapter semantics left open (r2 W2-006) and Servlet bind (r4 W2-006). Measured (2026-10-20): `allowedHosts` is enforced only by the TinyHttpd adapter (`NaruServe-tinyhttpd/.../TinyHttpdAdapter.java:118-120`) and nowhere in `NaruServe-api/src/main` outside `ServerOptions` itself; `bindAddress` and `port` are applied only by the TinyHttpd adapter's bind (`:100`), but the core still logs a LAN warning for a non-loopback `bindAddress` (`internal/DefaultRestApp.java:499`) and `ServerHandle.address()` reports the configured address, so on the Servlet adapter both describe the setting, not the container; `ServerSettings` carries `maxSseStreams` (default 128), `logger` and `errorRenderer` (`spi/ServerSettings.java:32-56`). Decision: the ignored list in `servlet.md` names exactly the `ServerOptions` settings `bindAddress`, `allowedHosts`, `maxHeaderSize`, `maxHeaderCount`, `maxRequestLineLength`, `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `minBodyRate`, `maxWorkers`, `maxConnections`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and `maxConnectionsPerAddress`, plus the port argument of `listen`; the applied list names `jsonLimit`, `formLimit`, `app.multipart`, `maxSseStreams`, the SSE options and `trustProxy`. Pitfall: because `allowedHosts` is an adapter setting, a Host allowlist the application relies on is not enforced behind a container; `servlet.md` tells the reader to configure virtual hosts in the container. Rejected alternative: enforcing `allowedHosts` in the Servlet adapter; the container owns the connector and virtual host, and a second enforcement would diverge from it.

records.title: Upgrade dispatch: middleware chain to completion, then the upgrade extension point, handler once after 101

acceptanceCriteria.text: A global middleware and a prefix middleware `app.use("/ws", mw)` each record their call and run `next.run()`; an upgrade request to `app.ws("/ws/chat", h)` records both calls, in registration order, and both `next.run()` calls have returned before `HttpExchange.webSocket` is called, which an in-memory adapter test observes through a call log. [D-296; D-429] Decision: the terminal step only records that it was reached, and `WebSocketUpgrade.run` is called after `pipeline.run` returned, only when the terminal was reached and the response is still `NEW`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-1]

A middleware that answers `res.status(401).end()` without calling `next.run()` on an upgrade request makes the client receive `401`, `HttpExchange.webSocket` is never called and the `ws` handler never runs (T22). [D-296]

The `ws` handler is invoked exactly once per accepted upgrade, on the endpoint's `onOpen` after the adapter wrote `101`, which a test asserts by recording that the in-memory channel was open and the `101` recorded when the handler ran; a handshake refused before `101` (for example a `503` from the adapter) never invokes the handler. Decision: the handler runs after `101`, from `onOpen`. [D-295; wave decision: Handler timing (W2-004)] Decision: the handler runs on the adapter's calling thread after the channel is stored; a refusal before `onOpen` never runs it. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-2]
After the `ws` handler returns, the session stays open and a text message sent 500 ms later reaches its `onText` listener; the connection ends only by a close, an error or shutdown. [D-295]
A global middleware that counts its calls is called once for the upgrade request and not again for any of 3 text and 2 binary messages that the session receives afterwards (T21). [D-297]
`req.service(Clock.class)` inside the `ws` handler returns the same instance that `onStart` registered, compared with `assertSame` (T21, T41). [D-316] [carried: D-142 WebSocket case]

An upgrade request (`Upgrade: websocket`, `Connection: Upgrade`) matching an `app.ws` route no longer receives the wave 3 `426` fallback of FR-HTTP-022 AC-6: it reaches `HttpExchange.webSocket`, and a non-upgrade `GET` to a path with both `app.get` and `app.ws` routes reaches the `app.get` handler. The upgrade cases of `HttpAcceptanceTest#sdsAc18_T06_FR_HTTP_022_AC5_AC6_webSocketOnlyHookRouteGives426` and `DispatcherTest#sdsAc18_FR_HTTP_022_AC5_AC6_webSocketOnlyRouteGives426ForPlainAndUpgradeGet` are re-pointed to this AC and changed to assert the handshake (a requirement change by wave 7, not a weakened test), while their non-upgrade `426` cases stay and are re-pointed to FR-WS-004 AC-1; `app.ws` registers through the internal `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute(String, RouteHandler)` hook, which keeps its signature and stays the internal registration that `app.ws` delegates to, and the `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` fixture keeps its signature and keeps registering through that hook, so verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5 and AC-7 stay true and the direct hook calls of `DefaultRestAppTest` compile unchanged; only the assertions of the re-pointed upgrade cases change to the handshake behaviour, and every test that uses the fixture (StaticMethodTest, MiddlewarePipelineTest, ErrorPathTest) still passes under `./gradlew build`. [D-429; D-294] Decision: when the matched route's handler is not a `WebSocketRoute` (the `TestApp.webSocketRoute` hook), the upgrade completes with a null handler and that `RouteHandler` is never called. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-3]

When `HttpExchange.webSocket` returns after the connection closed, the dispatcher finishes the exchange without writing an HTTP response and without calling `finish()` before it returned. [D-429; D-295] Decision: `res.upgraded()` finishes the exchange exactly once and writes no HTTP response, and `Dispatcher.finish` leaves the COMPLETED response alone. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-4] Decision: when `webSocket` throws and the session was not opened, the exception is rethrown to the error path; when the session was opened, the core logs ERROR `websocket <rid> failed` and still calls `res.upgraded()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-5]

records.requirement: The system shall, for an upgrade request matching an `app.ws` route, run the global and prefix middleware chain to completion and, only when no middleware responded, hand the request to `HttpExchange.webSocket`, run the `WebSocketHandler` once from the endpoint's `onOpen` after `101` was written, keep the connection open after the handler returns, and run no HTTP middleware per WebSocket message.
records.rationale:
Covers D-295, D-296, D-297, D-316, D-429 (dispatcher part), wave decision Handler timing (W2-004; D-303, D-295) and carried line D-142 WebSocket case (from wave 4; T41); tests T21 and T22. Measured: `internal/Dispatcher.java:357-360` answers a MATCHED WEBSOCKET route that reaches the fallback with `426` + `Upgrade`/`Connection`, so before wave 7 an upgrade request to a hook WebSocket route gets `426` (FR-HTTP-022 AC-6, true as history "until wave 7 adds app.ws"); tests asserting that 426 are re-pointed here. Decision (W2-004): the handler runs from `onOpen`, after `101`, matching the `ws` library's `connection` event; a `413` or `503` from the adapter therefore never runs user code. Pitfall: running the handler before `101` would let user code write an HTTP response on an upgraded exchange; rejected. Rejected alternative: per-message middleware (Socket.IO style); D-297 forbids it, reopen never in v1. The `Origin` check of FR-WS-003 runs between the middleware chain and the extension point; the access-log lines are owned by FR-APP-019 in the APP scope.
- [2026-10-20] Test re-point (AC-7): verified FR-HTTP-022 AC-6 stays as history for waves 3-6; from wave 7 its upgrade-to-WebSocket-route case is owned here. The upgrade cases of HttpAcceptanceTest#sdsAc18_T06_FR_HTTP_022_AC5_AC6_* and DispatcherTest#sdsAc18_FR_HTTP_022_AC5_AC6_* and the TestApp.webSocketRoute fixture move to FR-WS-001 and assert the handshake; this is a requirement change, not a weakened test.
- [2026-10-20] Fixture and hook (AC-7, corrects the note above): `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute(String, RouteHandler)` and `TestApp.webSocketRoute(path)` keep their signatures and stay the internal registration that `app.ws` delegates to, so verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5/AC-7 stay true and DefaultRestAppTest's direct hook calls compile unchanged; only the re-pointed upgrade assertions change to the handshake.
records.implementationNotes:
- -
- [2026-10-20] Decision for AC-7 (A4-02): app.ws passes the hook a RouteHandler adapter holding its WebSocketHandler; for a hook route whose RouteHandler is no such adapter the core completes the upgrade, runs no ws handler and never calls that RouteHandler, so re-pointed fixture cases assert HttpExchange.webSocket was called. The later rationale note (hook and fixture keep their signatures) replaces the earlier "fixture moves" note.

records.title: TinyHttpd upgrade class: RFC 6455 handshake through WebSocketHandler and pre-101 rejections through the dispatcher's error path

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over a TinyHttpd loopback socket, a handshake with `Upgrade: websocket`, `Connection: Upgrade`, `Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==` and `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` receives `101` with `Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=`, and a text frame sent afterwards reaches the session's `onText` (T19). [D-298]

Over TinyHttpd, a handshake missing `Sec-WebSocket-Key` receives `400` with the D-132 standard JSON error body whose `requestId` equals the request's id, and the connection is not upgraded: no `101` is read and the socket accepts no WebSocket frame (T19). [D-299; D-444]

Over TinyHttpd, a handshake with `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 12` receives `426` with the header `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` and the standard error body carrying the request id, and the access log records status `426` for that request (T19). [D-444] [carried: V2-001]

The TinyHttpd upgrade class catches every `HttpException` that `WebSocketHandler.handle` or the `res.upgrade` call inside it throws before `101` and rethrows it to the core as a NaruServe `HttpException` with the same status and headers, which a test asserts for each status it can raise: `400` and `426` + `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` from requests built without `Sec-WebSocket-Key` and with `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 12`, and `413` (upgrade request body above `maxDrainBytes`) and `503` + `Retry-After` (`maxUpgradedConnections` reached) from a fake TinyHttpd response whose `upgrade` throws them. TinyHttpd's `403` for a `null` listener cannot occur because the factory always returns NaruServe's listener (AC-6); the `403` of a refused `Origin` comes from the core check of FR-WS-003, which a TinyHttpd test asserts with the standard error body and its request id. [D-444] Decision: the TinyHttpd `HttpException` becomes a NaruServe `HttpException(getStatus(), getMessage())` with each `getHeaders()` pair added by `withHeader` in order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-2]

An error response for a pre-`101` rejection carries no `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` and no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header, which TinyHttpd tests assert on the two rejections raised after TinyHttpd set `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`: the `503` of a third upgrade with `maxUpgradedConnections(2)` (FR-WS-009 AC-1) and the `413` of an upgrade whose request body exceeds `maxDrainBytes`. [wave decision: Handshake headers on rejections (W2-008)] Decision: when the response is not committed, the mapping first calls `setHeader("Sec-WebSocket-Accept", null)` and `setHeader("Sec-WebSocket-Protocol", null)` on the wrapped response, which removes both, before throwing. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-3]

The upgrade class builds the TinyHttpd `WebSocketHandler` with `allowAnyOrigin()`, passes the configured `maxMessageSize` to both `maxFramePayloadBytes` and `maxMessageBytes` and the ping interval in milliseconds to `pingInterval`, calls `handle` on the request worker thread, and its factory always returns NaruServe's listener without running user code, which a test asserts by recording the handler configuration and the calling thread. [D-429; wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: `webSocket` holds the exchange lock only for `requireStartable` and `markUpgraded`, never while the read loop runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-7]

`handle` is called with a `ResponseWrapper` whose `upgrade` keeps the returned `UpgradedConnection`, and `WebSocketChannel.abort()` calls that connection's `close()`, which a test asserts by aborting an open session and observing the client socket reach end of stream within 1 s. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)]

The TinyHttpd exchange stays unstarted until `101` has been written: after a pre-`101` rejection the dispatcher's error path commits the error answer on the same exchange without an `IllegalStateException`. [wave decision: Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002)] Decision: the wrapped upgrade runs `onCommitted` only if the response is committed when it returns or throws, so `413` and `503` leave the exchange unstarted for the error path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-4]

An `IOException` or `RuntimeException` that `webSocket` throws after `101` is logged at ERROR with the request id and ends the exchange without any HTTP error answer written to the upgraded connection, and no exception reaches TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener` callbacks. [wave decision: User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005)] Decision: a `RuntimeException` from an endpoint call inside a TinyHttpd listener callback is caught, the channel is aborted and the callback returns normally. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-6]

WebSocket framing on the TinyHttpd adapter comes only from the `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-websocket` artifact that the root `build.gradle` already declares for `NaruServe-tinyhttpd`; the build's dependency check still allows no other module to depend on a `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` artifact. [D-302]

records.requirement: The system shall implement `HttpExchange.webSocket` on the TinyHttpd adapter with a TinyHttpd `WebSocketHandler` built with `allowAnyOrigin()`, the configured message limit and ping interval, called on the request worker through a `ResponseWrapper` that keeps the returned `UpgradedConnection`, answering a valid RFC 6455 handshake with `101` and the correct `Sec-WebSocket-Accept`, and turning every rejection raised before `101` into a NaruServe `HttpException` that carries its status and headers and leaves the exchange unstarted for the dispatcher's error path.
records.rationale: Covers D-298, D-299, D-302, D-444, D-429 (TinyHttpd part), wave decisions WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001, TinyHttpd part), Handshake headers on rejections (W2-008), Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002) and User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005, adapter part); carried loop-D fix V2-001; tests T19 and the upgrade part of T35. Measured: `tinyhttpd/TinyHttpdFeatures.java:56` `upgrade(Response, ...)` and `:51` `eventStream(...)` throw `UnsupportedOperationException` naming wave 7; the feature hooks are package-private and may change to receive the exchange (W2-003, D-210 protects only the adapter core limit mapping). TinyHttpd's `WebSocketHandler` (read-only checkout at 46b973e) offers `allowAnyOrigin()`, `maxFramePayloadBytes(int)`, `maxMessageBytes(int)`, `pingInterval(int millis)` and `handle(Request, Response)`; its listener has `onOpen/onText/onBinary/onClose` and no `onError`. `allowAnyOrigin()` is used because the core checks `Origin` itself (FR-WS-003, W2-005). Pitfall: TinyHttpd's handshake may set `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` before it throws; W2-008 requires dropping it before the error path renders, through whatever mechanism the TinyHttpd `Response` API allows (SDS decides). Pitfall: marking the exchange started before `101` would make the error path's commit throw (r2 W2-002). Rejected alternative: answering rejections inside the TinyHttpd class with TinyHttpd's own error page; it would bypass the D-132 standard body and the request id, reopen never. The access log records the rejection status on the request's ordinary line (FR-APP-019, APP scope). Header carriage uses `HttpException.withHeader` (IR-HTTP-008, HTTP scope).

records.title: Origin check in the core before the upgrade extension point, same-origin default and allowlist

acceptanceCriteria.text: With no allowlist configured, an upgrade request without an `Origin` header and one with `Origin: http://example.test:8080` and `Host: example.test:8080` both reach `HttpExchange.webSocket`. Decision: the default admits no-`Origin` and same-origin requests. [D-303; wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)]

With no allowlist configured, an upgrade request with `Origin: http://evil.test` and `Host: example.test` receives `403` with the standard JSON error body carrying the request id, `HttpExchange.webSocket` is never called and the `ws` handler never runs (T22). [D-300; wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)]

Same-origin comparison uses scheme `https` when `req.isSecure()` is true and `http` otherwise, normalises default port 80 for `http` and 443 for `https`, and compares hosts case-insensitively: `Origin: HTTP://Example.Test` with `Host: example.test:80` is admitted, `Origin: https://example.test` on a non-secure request is rejected with `403`, and `Origin: http://example.test:8081` with `Host: example.test:8080` is rejected with `403`. Decision: scheme from `isSecure()`, host and port from `Host`. [wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)] Decision: scheme and host of the `Origin` are lowercased, port 80 or 443 is taken by scheme when absent, `Host` is read as `host[:port]` with a bracketed IPv6 form, and an unparseable `Origin`, or a present `Origin` with no `Host`, is not same-origin. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-7]
`Origin: null` is rejected with `403` when no allowlist is configured and when the allowlist holds only named origins. [D-300; wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)]

With `allowedOrigins("https://app.example.com")` configured, an upgrade with `Origin: https://APP.example.com:443` is admitted, an upgrade with `Origin: https://other.example.com` receives `403`, and the no-`Origin` and same-origin cases are still admitted (T22). [D-300; wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)] Decision: each allowlist entry is normalised the same way once at freeze and compared as normalised tuples, with `*` anywhere in the list admitting every `Origin`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-3 SDS-AC-9]
With `allowedOrigins("*")` configured, an upgrade with any `Origin`, including `Origin: null`, is admitted. [wave decision: Origin check (W2-005)]

The `Origin` check runs after every global and prefix middleware returned and before `HttpExchange.webSocket`: a middleware that records its call is called for a request that is then rejected with `403`, and a middleware that answers `401` prevents the `Origin` check result from being written. [D-300; D-429]

records.requirement: The system shall check the `Origin` header of every upgrade request in the core after the middleware chain and before `HttpExchange.webSocket`, admitting a request with no `Origin`, a same-origin `Origin` and, when an allowlist is configured, each listed origin or any origin for the entry `*`, and answering every other `Origin` with `403` without upgrading.
records.rationale: Covers D-300, wave decision Origin check (W2-005; D-300, D-303) and the default part of D-303; test T22. Reason the check sits in the core: TinyHttpd's own check always admits a missing or same-origin `Origin`, so its allowlist cannot express the NaruServe default; the adapter therefore uses `allowAnyOrigin()` (FR-WS-002). Decision (C-07): same-origin means scheme, host and port equal to the request's own, with scheme `https` when `req.isSecure()` and `http` otherwise, host and port from `Host`, default ports 80/443 normalised and host compared case-insensitively; the literal `Origin: null` (sandboxed iframes, file URLs) is rejected unless `*` is listed. Pitfall: browsers do not apply CORS to WebSocket, so a cross-site page can open an authenticated socket with cookies (cross-site WebSocket hijacking); the same-origin default blocks it. Rejected alternative: admit-all when unset (the `ws` library default); reopen if non-browser-only deployments find the default too strict, since `*` exists. Rejected alternative: reject-all when unset; it breaks the same-origin browser case that works in Express with `express-ws`. The 403 body is the standard error body of FR-APP-006 (HTTP_403 via its fallback rule).

records.title: RFC 6455 protocol enforcement from TinyHttpd: masking, UTF-8, message limit, reassembly, control frames, ping and close handshake

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over TinyHttpd, a raw-socket client that sends an unmasked text frame after `101` receives a close frame with code `1002` and the session's `onClose` listener receives `1002` (T20). [D-304]
A text frame whose payload is the invalid UTF-8 byte sequence `0xC3 0x28` makes the server send close `1007`, and `onText` is not called (T20). [D-305]
With the default limit, a 1048577-byte text message sent as one frame makes the server send close `1009`, while a 1048576-byte message reaches `onText` whole (T20). [D-306]

With `maxMessageSize(4096)`, a 4097-byte binary message sent once as a single frame and once as three continuation fragments of 2048, 2048 and 1 bytes makes the server send close `1009` both times, and a 4096-byte message sent in four fragments reaches `onBinary` once with all 4096 bytes in order (T20). [D-419; D-307] [carried: V1-004] [carried: V2-003]

A text message sent as fragments `"Hel"`, `"lo"` reaches `onText` once as `"Hello"`, and a Ping frame interleaved between the two fragments is answered with a Pong without breaking the reassembly (T20). [D-307; D-309]
A Ping control frame with a 126-byte payload, and a Ping frame with FIN clear, each make the server send close `1002`. [D-308]

A client Ping with payload `"abc"` is answered with a Pong carrying `"abc"`, and `ws.ping()` called from the handler makes the client receive a Ping frame, written through the session's sender slot by `WebSocketChannel.ping` (T21). [D-309; wave decision: Ping (r2 W2-001)] Decision: `ws.ping()` on an open session submits `channel.ping(new byte[0])` to the session's sender slot. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-8]

`ws.close(4000, "bye")` makes the client receive a close frame with code `4000` and reason `"bye"`; after the client answers with its close frame (echoing any code), `ws.isOpen()` returns `false`, `onClose` receives `(4000, "bye")`, the server's own code and reason as FR-WS-006 AC-9 states, and the TCP connection is closed. [D-310] Decision: `isOpen()` becomes false as soon as `ws.close(code, reason)` is called, later sends are dropped, and `onClose` receives the sent `(code, reason)` whatever code the client echoed. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-4 SDS-AC-9]

records.requirement: The system shall enforce RFC 6455 on accepted WebSocket connections through TinyHttpd's websocket module, closing with `1002` for an unmasked client frame or an oversized or fragmented control frame, `1007` for invalid UTF-8 text and `1009` for a message above the configured limit whether sent as one frame or fragmented, delivering fragmented messages reassembled, answering Ping with Pong, sending Ping on `ws.ping()`, and completing the close handshake on `ws.close(code, reason)` after which `isOpen()` returns `false`.
records.rationale: Covers D-302, D-304, D-305, D-306, D-307, D-308, D-309, D-310, D-419 (limit mapping part), wave decision Ping (r2 W2-001) and carried loop-D fixes V1-004 and V2-003 (both: the configured message limit goes to both `maxFramePayloadBytes` and `maxMessageBytes`, tested at a non-default limit as one frame and fragmented); tests T20 and T21. Measured: TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` offers `sendText`, `sendBinary`, `ping(byte[] <= 125)`, `close(code, reason)` and `isOpen`; NaruServe adds no frame codec (D-302), so these ACs are end-to-end tests over the TinyHttpd adapter with a raw-socket client that writes frames by hand. Pitfall: passing the limit only to `maxMessageBytes` lets one unfragmented frame above the limit through until reassembly, and only to `maxFramePayloadBytes` lets a fragmented message grow without bound (V1-004). Decision: `ws.ping()` sends an empty-payload Ping through the session's sender slot (FR-WS-007), calling `WebSocketChannel.ping(new byte[0])`, so it never interleaves with a data frame being written. Rejected alternative: a NaruServe-side UTF-8 or size check before TinyHttpd; duplicate logic, reopen only if TinyHttpd lacks a check.

records.title: WebSocketSession semantics: unique ids, per-connection attributes, onClose once, JSON through JsonCodec, onJson failure and listener exceptions

acceptanceCriteria.text: Three sessions opened on one app get ids `0000000000000001`, `0000000000000002` and `0000000000000003`, each matching `[0-9a-f]{16}`, and 1000 sessions opened concurrently from 8 threads get 1000 distinct ids. Decision: the id is 16 lowercase hex digits of an app-wide counter starting at 1. [D-312]

`ws.attribute("user", "kim")` set in the handler is read back as `"kim"` by `ws.attribute("user", String.class)` in a later `onText` listener, `req.attribute("user", String.class)` stays `null`, attributes written under distinct keys from 8 threads concurrently are all readable afterwards without an exception, and after the session closed the session's attribute map is empty, which a test asserts through the internal session (T21). [D-313] Decision: setting an attribute to a null value removes the key, the typed read boxes a primitive class as `Request.attribute` does, and the map is cleared after the `onClose` listeners ran. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-2] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-3]

`onClose` listeners run exactly once per connection with the close code and reason of AC-9: a client close `(1000, "done")` delivers `(1000, "done")` once, and a session closed by the server and then by an abort of the socket still runs each listener once, which a counter asserts. [D-314] Decision: the listeners run only on the first `onClose` call, guarded by one `AtomicBoolean`, on the calling thread in registration order; a `CloseListener` exception is logged at ERROR and the next listener still runs. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-4]

`ws.sendJson(Collections.singletonMap("a", 1))` sends a text message equal to the app `JsonCodec` encoding of the value, and `ws.onJson(Msg.class, l)` passes `l` the value the app `JsonCodec` decodes from a text message, which a test with a recording stub codec asserts by observing both codec calls. [D-315] Decision: `sendJson` encodes on the calling thread with `codec.encode` into a `StringWriter` and queues the result as a text message; an `IOException` from the codec is rethrown as `HttpException(500, "JSON encoding failed")` with nothing queued, because `UncheckedIOException` needs API 24. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-5] Decision: `onText` and `onJson` entries share one registration-ordered list, and each `onJson` entry decodes with `codec.decode(new StringReader(text), type)` on its own. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-6]

A text message `{bad` delivered to an `onJson(Msg.class, l)` listener does not call `l`, passes the codec's decode exception to every `onError` listener, and leaves `ws.isOpen()` `true`; with no `onError` listener the failure is logged at WARN with the request id. Decision: an `onJson` parse failure is reported through `onError`, not by closing the connection. [D-317] Decision: a listener whose decode throws `IOException` or `RuntimeException` is skipped, the later entries still run, and with no `onError` listener the core logs WARN `websocket <rid> json decode failed`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-7]

An exception thrown by an `onText` listener is passed to the `onError` listeners, logged at ERROR with the request id, and the client receives close `1011`; `onClose` receives `1011` as AC-9 states; no exception propagates to the adapter's endpoint callback, which the in-memory adapter asserts by observing its `onText` call return normally. Decision: user listener exceptions after `101` close the session with `1011`. [wave decision: User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005)] Decision: a throwing text, binary or JSON listener calls `fail(e, "listener")`, skips the remaining listeners of that message and returns normally to the adapter, with the ERROR line `websocket <rid> listener failed`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-8] Decision: an `onError` listener that itself throws is logged at ERROR and ignored, and the next `onError` listener and the `1011` close still run, with no recursion into `fail`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-9]

`sendText`, `sendBinary`, `sendJson` and `ping` called on a closed session return without an exception and send nothing, and `isOpen()` returns `false`. Decision: sends on a closed session are dropped silently. [D-311; D-310] Decision: the call returns before encoding or counting bytes when `isOpen()` is false. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-10]

`close(1005, "")`, `close(1016, "")`, `close(2000, "")`, `close(999, "")` and `close(5000, "")` throw `IllegalArgumentException`, `close(1000, r)` with a reason of 124 UTF-8 bytes throws `IllegalArgumentException`, and `close(1012, "")`, `close(3000, "")` and `close(4999, "x")` are accepted. Decision: the close code must be 1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999 (RFC 6455 section 7.4 and the sendable set that TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` also checks on receive), and the reason must fit 123 UTF-8 bytes. [D-310] Decision: `checkClose` runs first, also on a closed session, with the messages `close code must be 1000-1003, 1007-1014 or 3000-4999: <code>` and `close reason over 123 UTF-8 bytes: <n>`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-11]

When the core starts the close with code c and reason r (`ws.close(c, r)`, queue overflow `1008`, idle timeout `1001`, shutdown `1001`, listener exception `1011`), the `onClose` listeners and the FR-APP-019 close line report (c, r) whatever the peer answers, also when the peer never answers and the socket is aborted; a close TinyHttpd starts itself (ping timeout `1001`, protocol failures such as `1002`, `1007`, `1009`) reports the code TinyHttpd delivers; a close started by the client reports the client's code and reason; an end without any close frame from either side reports `1006` with an empty reason. A test asserts each case over the in-memory adapter, the overflow case over TinyHttpd with a client that does not answer the server's close frame, and the client-close case over TinyHttpd. Decision: the server's own close code wins over the `1006` TinyHttpd delivers to `WebSocketListener.onClose` when the peer does not answer. [D-314; D-310; D-321; D-325] Decision: when several closes are started by the core, the first recorded pair is reported to `onClose`, and with no recorded pair the code the adapter delivers. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-12]

An exception, checked or unchecked, thrown by the `ws` handler itself, which runs from the endpoint's `onOpen` after `101` (FR-WS-001 AC-3), is caught by the core endpoint, passed to every `onError` listener the handler registered before the throw, logged at ERROR with the request id, and closes the session with `1011`; `onClose` receives `1011` as AC-9 states; no HTTP error answer is written because the connection is already upgraded, and no exception reaches TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener.onOpen`; an in-memory test and a TinyHttpd test assert that the client receives close `1011` after the `101` and no other HTTP status line, and that an `onError` listener registered before the throw received the exception. Decision: an exception from the `ws` handler is handled like a listener exception after `101`. [wave decision: User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005)] [D-295] Decision: the core calls `fail(e, "handler")` with only the `onError` listeners registered before the throw, logs `websocket <rid> handler failed` and writes no HTTP answer. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-5 SDS-AC-13]

core endpoint behind the SPI callbacks

records.requirement: The system shall give each WebSocket session an id unique within its app, a per-connection concurrent attribute map separate from request attributes and released at close, `onClose` listeners run exactly once with the close code and reason, `sendJson` and `onJson` through the app's `JsonCodec`, `onJson` decode failures reported to `onError` with the session left open, and user listener exceptions caught, logged and answered by close `1011`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-312, D-313, D-314, D-315, D-317 (decision part), wave decision User exceptions after 101 (r2 W2-005, core endpoint part) and the C-07 send/close choices; test T21. Decisions (C-07): session id = 16 lowercase hex digits of an app-wide counter starting at 1; sends on a closed session are dropped without exception, like the `ws` library's send on a closed socket, with `isOpen()` reporting the state; `close(code, reason)` accepts only the codes an endpoint may send per RFC 6455 section 7.4 (1000-1003, 1007-1014 and 3000-4999; 1004-1006, 1015 and the unassigned 1016-2999 are rejected, matching TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` receive check so a NaruServe close is never failed as a protocol error by a strict peer) and rejects a reason over 123 UTF-8 bytes instead of truncating. Decision (close codes on TinyHttpd, AC-9): measured `WebSocket.java:261-405` at 46b973e reports to `WebSocketListener.onClose` the code of the peer's close frame, its own code for a close it starts itself (ping timeout `1001`, protocol failure), and `1006` when the socket ends without a close frame, so a close the core started and the peer never answered would surface as `1006`; the core therefore records the code and reason of every close it starts and reports those to `onClose` and to the FR-APP-019 close line. This decision applies to FR-WS-005 AC-8, FR-WS-007 AC-6, FR-WS-008 AC-4, FR-WS-010 AC-2/AC-7 and FR-APP-019 AC-9. Decision for D-317: an `onJson` parse failure goes to the `onError` listeners and the session stays open; with no `onError` listener it is logged at WARN with the request id. Rejected alternative: closing 1007 on a JSON parse failure; a malformed application message is not a protocol error, reopen if users ask for strict mode. Decision for r2 W2-005: an exception from any user listener is caught, passed to the `onError` listeners, logged at ERROR with the request id, and the session is closed with `1011`; nothing reaches TinyHttpd's callbacks. Pitfall: an `onError` listener that itself throws must not recurse; it is logged and ignored. Rejected alternative: random UUID ids; the counter is cheaper on API 21 and unique per app as D-312 requires.
- [2026-10-20] Handler exceptions (AC-10, r2 W2-005): the `ws` handler runs from the core endpoint's `onOpen` after `101`, and TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener.onOpen` declares no checked exception and answers a RuntimeException with close 1011 plus a rethrow out of `handle`, so the core catches every handler exception itself, reports it to the onError listeners registered so far, logs it at ERROR and closes 1011; no HTTP answer is possible after the upgrade.

records.title: Bounded per-session send queue drained by one app-wide sender executor, whole ordered messages and the 1008 overflow policy

acceptanceCriteria.text: With `sendQueueSize(1000)`, a session whose client does not read accepts queued sends up to 1000 bytes of payload without closing, and the in-memory test observes the queued byte count never exceed 1000; a test with non-ASCII text (`"é"` counts 2 bytes) asserts the count. Decision: queued bytes count the UTF-8 encoded length of a text message's payload and the array length of a binary message's payload; ping and close frames are not counted. [D-318] Decision: `sendJson` counts its encoded text, and the bytes are released when that write returns, so the in-flight message stays counted. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-1]

All sessions of an app share one sender executor whose maximum thread count equals `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128), which a test reads from the internal executor; its threads are named `naruserve-<port>-ws-sender-<n>`, with `<port>` the app's bound port read when the thread is created, so two apps in one JVM own distinct thread names, which a test with two bound apps asserts; an idle thread ends after the executor's keep-alive time, which a test that sets the internal keep-alive to 200 ms asserts by observing the thread count fall to 0 within 1 s after the last send. Decision: the keep-alive time is 60 s, overridable only through an internal test hook. Decision: sender threads are named `naruserve-<port>-ws-sender-<n>` like the adapter's `naruserve-<port>-worker-<n>`, so thread-count tests attribute them per app. [D-417] Decision: the sender is a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max, max, keep-alive, LinkedBlockingQueue)` with `allowCoreThreadTimeOut(true)` and daemon threads with a 256 KiB requested stack, with `port.getAsInt()` read in `newThread`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-3]

At most one write task of a session runs at a time: a test whose in-memory channel blocks the first `sendText` observes that a second `sendText` on the same session is not started until the first returns, while a `sendText` on another session completes meanwhile. [D-417; D-319]

Eight threads that each send 500 text messages tagged with their thread number and sequence to one session make the client receive all 4000 messages whole, with each thread's messages in its send order and no frame of one message interleaved with another's (T23). [D-319]

Over TinyHttpd, with 20 sessions whose clients stopped reading while the server sent to them until their writes blocked and one healthy session, a `sendText` to the healthy session reaches its client within 1 s (T23); with `writeTimeout(1, SECONDS)`, each stalled session's sender thread is released within 2 s after its write blocked, because TinyHttpd's write timeout aborts the socket. [D-320; D-417]

When a send would make a session's queued bytes exceed `sendQueueSize`, that message is dropped, the queue is emptied, the client receives close `1008` with reason `send queue overflow`, `onClose` receives `(1008, "send queue overflow")` even when the client never answers the close frame (FR-WS-006 AC-9), and the send call returns normally without an exception (T23); a single message larger than `sendQueueSize` overflows on an empty queue and closes the session the same way, which `docs/api/websocket.md` states. Decision: the overflow policy closes the session with `1008` instead of throwing. [D-321]

After a session closed, by client close, overflow or abort, its queue is released, no sender task for it remains, and its attribute map is empty, which a test asserts through the internal session registry after 200 sessions opened and closed (T23). [D-322]

After `HttpExchange.webSocket` returns, the core waits for that session's in-flight sender task to end before the exchange finishes, which a test asserts by blocking a sender task and observing that the exchange's finish is reached only after the task ended; the wait does not run in the TinyHttpd class or in `onClose`. [wave decision: Sender slot release (W2-007)] [wave decision: Sender-slot wait (r2 W2-004)] Decision: the wait is `awaitIdle(session)` without a time bound, run in `WebSocketUpgrade.run` when `ex.webSocket` returns or throws after open, and before `res.upgraded()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-7]

records.requirement: The system shall queue every WebSocket send in a per-session outbound queue bounded by `sendQueueSize` and drain the queues with one app-wide sender executor whose thread limit equals `maxUpgradedConnections`, running at most one write task per session at a time so that messages go out whole in queue-entry order and a stalled session never delays another session, closing a session whose queue would overflow with `1008`, and leaving no queue, thread or attribute of a closed session behind.
records.rationale: Covers D-318, D-417, D-319, D-320, D-321 (decision), D-322, wave decisions Sender slot release (W2-007) and Sender-slot wait (r2 W2-004, which moves the W2-007 wait into the core after `HttpExchange.webSocket` returns and before the exchange finishes, behaviour unchanged); test T23. Reason: TinyHttpd's `WebSocket` send is synchronous, so a direct send from a broadcaster would block on a slow peer. Measured: `ServerOptions.java:41-54` already defines `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128, FR-ENGINE-004); TinyHttpd's write timeout defaults to 30 s. Decision for D-321 (C-07): when queuing a message would make the session's queued bytes exceed `sendQueueSize`, the message is dropped, the queue is discarded, close `1008` with reason `send queue overflow` is handed to the sender slot as the last task, `onClose` receives `1008`, and the overflowing send returns normally. Rejected alternative: throwing from `send` on overflow; it forces every broadcaster to catch per peer, reopen if users need synchronous backpressure. Pitfall: a fixed pool of 16 threads would let 16 stalled peers block every other session (D-320 asks for at least 20 stalled sessions in the test). Pitfall: reusing a sender thread for another session's task while one write is in flight would interleave frames (D-319). Thread total and stack figures belong to PERF-APP-001 in the APP scope.

records.title: Ping interval, pong timeout, idle timeout scheduler and the handshake bound on TinyHttpd

acceptanceCriteria.text: The TinyHttpd `WebSocketHandler` receives `pingInterval` equal to the configured ping interval in milliseconds (default 30000), which a test with `pingInterval(2, SECONDS)` asserts as 2000, and NaruServe starts no thread or timer for pings. [D-423; D-323]

Over TinyHttpd with `pingInterval(1, SECONDS)`, a client that completes the handshake and then sends nothing and answers no Ping receives at least one Ping and then a close `1001` within 3 s (two ping intervals plus 1 s) of its last frame, and `onClose` receives `1001`, the code TinyHttpd delivers for its own ping-timeout close (FR-WS-006 AC-9) (T21). [D-424; D-423]

Reflection finds no pong-timeout setting, and `docs/api/websocket.md` and `docs/api/defaults.md` state that the pong timeout equals the ping interval; `docs/api/websocket.md` also states that a separate pong timeout is not available because TinyHttpd's `WebSocketListener` has no Pong callback and that this is a deferred TinyHttpd limitation, which a docs test finds by a fixed phrase. Decision: the pong timeout is fixed to the ping interval in v1. [D-424] Decision: reflection finds no method of `WebSocketOptions` or `ServerOptions` whose name contains `pong` or `handshake`, ignoring case. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-9]

With `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)` and `pingInterval(30, SECONDS)`, a session whose client sends a Ping frame every 300 ms but no text or binary message is handed close `1001` by the scheduler within 2 s of its last text or binary message, the client receives a Pong for each Ping until then, then stops pinging and answers the server's close frame, and `onClose` receives `1001` as FR-WS-006 AC-9 states (T21). [D-425; D-323] Decision: the idle check compares `nanoTime - lastActivityNanos >= idleTimeout`, then calls `closeBy(1001, "idle timeout")` and schedules one abort check 1000 ms later. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-11]

All idle checks of one app run on one thread named `naruserve-<port>-ws-idle`, with `<port>` the app's bound port read when the thread is created, which never calls a `WebSocketChannel` write method itself: a test with a session whose in-memory channel blocks `close` observes the scheduler run the idle check of another idle session within 100 ms and call `abort()` on the blocked session 1 s (plus 200 ms of scheduling slack) after it handed over the close task. Decision: the idle scheduler thread is named `naruserve-<port>-ws-idle`, so thread-count tests attribute it per app. [D-425]

A text message received or sent resets the session's idle clock: with `idleTimeout(1, SECONDS)`, a session that receives one text message every 500 ms for 3 s stays open. [D-425] Decision: `touch()` runs when `onText` or `onBinary` runs and when a text or binary write returns; pings, pongs and close frames do not touch. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-6 SDS-AC-10]

On TinyHttpd, a client that sends `GET /ws HTTP/1.1` and then stalls before the end of the request headers is disconnected within `headerTimeout` plus 1 s, which a test with `headerTimeout(1, SECONDS)` asserts, and reflection finds no handshake-timeout setter on `WebSocketOptions` or `ServerOptions`; `docs/api/websocket.md` and `docs/api/defaults.md` state that the handshake is bounded only by `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout` and that a dedicated upgrade deadline is a deferred TinyHttpd limitation, which a docs test finds by a fixed phrase. Deviation (recorded): D-323's handshake timeout is met on TinyHttpd only by `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`. [D-323; residual: WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002)]
