records.requirement: The system shall pass the WebSocket ping interval to TinyHttpd's `WebSocketHandler.pingInterval` so that a silent peer is closed with `1001` after two intervals, fix the pong timeout to the ping interval, enforce the idle timeout with one NaruServe scheduler thread that hands close `1001` to an idle session's sender slot and aborts the session's socket 1 s later when that close task has not returned, and bound the handshake on TinyHttpd by the server-wide `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-323, D-423, D-424, D-425 and residual WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002); test T21. Measured: TinyHttpd's read loop sends a Ping after one interval without an inbound frame and closes with 1001 after a second such interval, treats any inbound frame as the answer, and its `WebSocketListener` has no Pong callback, so NaruServe runs no ping scheduler (D-423) and cannot measure a separate pong timeout (D-424). TinyHttpd counts Ping and Pong as activity, so a peer that answers pings never idles out there; the idle timeout counts only text and binary messages received or sent (D-425). TinyHttpd at 46b973e has no upgrade-specific deadline; `ServerOptions.headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout` (`ServerOptions.java:29,32`, mapped in the adapter core under D-210) bound the handshake. Deviation (recorded): D-323 asks for a configurable handshake timeout; on TinyHttpd it is satisfied only through these existing server-wide timeouts, and no separate setting is added because it would have no effect. Deferred D-020 TinyHttpd-gap issues (opened by the orchestrator in the run's issue ledger at triage, not patched in TinyHttpd by wave 7): (1) the missing Pong callback of `WebSocketListener`, which blocks a separate pong timeout (D-424); (2) a dedicated upgrade (handshake) deadline (r5 W2-002). AC-3 and AC-7 check the user-facing statement of both gaps in `docs/api/`. Pitfall: a scheduler thread that writes the close frame itself would block on a stalled peer and delay every other session's idle check; it only enqueues and aborts. Rejected alternative: one timer per session; it multiplies threads on API 21. Defaults (30 s ping, 5 min idle) are settled in IR-WS-001.
- [2026-10-20] AC-4 has the client answer the server's close frame. A peer that never answers the close and keeps sending frames keeps the session open: TinyHttpd's closing read timeout restarts on every inbound frame, so such a peer is ended only by its own close, the shutdown abort or `writeTimeout`. This is a TinyHttpd gap under D-020, deferred and not patched by wave 7.

records.title: WebSocket connection limit and session registration: 503 beyond maxUpgradedConnections, reservation before the upgrade, refusal after the closed flag and after STOPPING

acceptanceCriteria.text: Over TinyHttpd with `maxUpgradedConnections(2)`, two open WebSocket sessions are accepted and a third upgrade receives `503` with a `Retry-After` header and the standard error body, without `101` and without running the `ws` handler. [D-324; D-444]

The core reserves a session in the WebSocket session registry, under the registry lock, before it calls `HttpExchange.webSocket`, which an in-memory adapter test asserts by reading the registry size inside its `webSocket` call before `onOpen`. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

When the registry's closed flag is already set, an upgrade request that reaches the upgrade extension point receives `503` with `Connection: close` before any `101`, `HttpExchange.webSocket` is not called and no session is registered. [D-445; wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

A handshake refused before `101` (for example `426` from the adapter) removes its reservation, and an upgrade refused with `403` by the Origin check of FR-WS-003 or by any other core check before `HttpExchange.webSocket` leaves no reservation, so the registry size returns to its previous value, which a test asserts after 10 refused handshakes of each kind. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the closed flag was set gets its channel, hands close `1001` to its sender slot as its only task and does not run the `ws` handler, which an in-memory test asserts by setting the flag between the reservation and `onOpen`. [wave decision: Session registration (r2 W2-003)] [D-445] Decision: the close task is `closeBy(1001, "server shutdown")`, and the idle watch is skipped as well as the handler. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-5]

An upgrade request that reaches the dispatcher after `STOPPING` began receives `503` with `Connection: close` from the stopping gate of FR-APP-013 and is not upgraded: `HttpExchange.webSocket` is never called. [D-301]

records.requirement: The system shall count WebSocket upgrades against `maxUpgradedConnections` and answer an upgrade beyond it with `503`, reserve each session in the WebSocket session registry under its lock before calling `HttpExchange.webSocket`, refuse the reservation with `503` and `Connection: close` once the registry's closed flag is set, remove the reservation when the handshake is refused, send close `1001` without running the handler for a reserved session whose `onOpen` comes after the flag, and reject upgrade requests arriving after `STOPPING` began without upgrading.
records.rationale: Covers D-301, D-324, D-445 (WebSocket part: closed flag before snapshot, upgrade answered `503` + `Connection: close` before any `101`) and wave decision Session registration (r2 W2-003). Measured: `ServerOptions.java:41-54` defines `maxUpgradedConnections` (default 128, range up to 65536) and `TinyHttpdAdapter.java:105-116` maps it onto TinyHttpd's `maxUpgradedConnections` (wave 5, FR-ENGINE-004), so TinyHttpd answers `503` + `Retry-After` beyond the limit and FR-WS-002 maps that rejection. D-301 is satisfied by FR-APP-013's stopping gate (requests reaching the dispatcher during `STOPPING` get `503` + `Connection: close`). The closing participant that sets the flag and takes the snapshot is FR-WS-010; the shared coordination across WebSocket and SSE belongs to FR-APP-020 in the APP scope. Pitfall: registering only in `onOpen` would let a session open between the closing participant's snapshot and the flag and escape the 1001 close; the reservation before `webSocket` closes that window. Rejected alternative: a NaruServe-side counter in addition to TinyHttpd's; two counters drift, reopen if a non-TinyHttpd adapter lacks a limit.

records.title: Shutdown of WebSocket sessions: before-wait participant closes with 1001, bounded close wait and abort through UpgradedConnection

acceptanceCriteria.text: The WebSocket closing participant is registered in the before-wait phase of the shutdown participants of FR-APP-011 and, when run, first sets the registry's closed flag under the registry lock and then takes its snapshot, so a session reserved before the flag is in the snapshot and an upgrade after it is refused as FR-WS-009 states. [D-435; D-445] Decision: the closing participant is registered in `BEFORE_WAIT` and the terminate step in `FORCE_CLOSE`, once per app. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-13]

During shutdown, an open healthy session's client receives close `1001` and its `onClose` listeners run once with `1001`, the server's own code as FR-WS-006 AC-9 states, also when the client does not answer the close frame (T21, T44). [D-340; D-435]

When the participant runs, no message queued before it is sent: a session with 50 queued messages behind a blocked write receives none of them after the participant started, and a `sendText` called after the participant started sends nothing and returns normally. [D-435] Decision: the close is `closeBy(1001, "server shutdown")` on every opened session, whose `last()` discards the queue and refuses later sends. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-7]

With two sessions whose clients stopped reading while the server sent to them until their writes blocked, the participant returns within 1 s plus 200 ms of scheduling slack, and both sessions' client sockets reach end of stream or reset by then, because the participant aborted them through `UpgradedConnection.close()` (T44). [D-435; D-343] Decision: when the close wait ends, the registry state is set to ENDED under the lock first, then `abort()` is called on each snapshot session with a channel whose slot is not idle. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-9]

When the participant receives a deadline that leaves 300 ms, its close wait ends after at most 300 ms plus 200 ms of scheduling slack before it aborts the unreturned sessions, which a test with a shutdown timeout of 300 ms and one stalled session asserts. [residual: Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003)] [D-435] Decision: the close wait ends at `min(now + 1000 ms, deadlineNanos)`, and earlier only when every snapshot session is removed or opened with `awaitIdleUntil` true. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-8]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the closed flag but before the close wait ended hands close `1001` to its sender slot as its only task, and the participant waits for that task within the same close wait and aborts the connection only if it has not returned by then. [wave decision: Reserved session at shutdown (r3 W2-003)]

A reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the close wait ended is aborted within 100 ms of its `onOpen` through its `UpgradedConnection` with no close frame sent, its `ws` handler never runs, and its FR-APP-019 close line reports `1006` (no close frame from either side, FR-WS-006 AC-9). Deviation (recorded): D-340 requires close `1001` for every open session at shutdown; this late-opening session is aborted without a close frame so TinyHttpd's stop callback never waits on a blocked close write. [D-340; wave decision: Session opening after the close wait (r4 W2-002)]

After `shutdown` returns, the sender executor and the idle scheduler thread of that app have terminated and the session registry is empty, which a test asserts by listing live threads whose names start with `naruserve-<port>-ws-` for that app's bound port (the names of FR-WS-007 AC-2 and FR-WS-008 AC-5), so another app's threads in the same JVM are not counted (T44). [D-343; D-435] Decision: terminate calls `shutdownNow(500)` on the sender and the idle scheduler and then clears the registry. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-7 SDS-AC-12]

records.requirement: The system shall register a before-wait shutdown participant that sets the WebSocket registry's closed flag, snapshots every reserved and open session, stops the sender executor from taking new messages, discards every session's queued messages, hands close `1001` to each session's sender slot as its last task, waits until every close task returned or until the earlier of 1 s and the time left to the shutdown deadline, and then aborts through `UpgradedConnection.close()` the socket of every session whose close task has not returned.
records.rationale:
Covers D-340, D-343 (WebSocket part), D-435, wave decisions Reserved session at shutdown (r3 W2-003, which replaces the round-2 "abort as soon as its channel is set"), Session opening after the close wait (r4 W2-002) and residual Deadline for shutdown participants (r5 W2-003, WebSocket use of the deadline; the add-only `ShutdownParticipants` overload itself is FR-APP-020 in the APP scope); tests T21 and T44. Measured: `internal/ShutdownParticipants.java:10-50` has a `Phase` enum and `add(Phase, Runnable)` without a deadline; `internal/DefaultRestApp.java:114-127,539-636` holds the shutdown deadline and `runShutdownSequence` (FR-APP-011). The bound rests on the abort alone with no write tracking: closing the socket makes a blocked write throw, including TinyHttpd's read-loop Ping/Pong writes and a close frame blocked on a full receive window, which share one write lock, so TinyHttpd's later stop callback `close(1001)` finds `closeSent` set or the socket closed and returns at once. Deviation (recorded): D-340 says shutdown closes every open session with 1001; a reserved session whose `onOpen` runs after the close wait ended is aborted at once with no close frame (r4 W2-002), which `docs/api/websocket.md` records, so TinyHttpd's stop callback never waits on a blocked close write and D-344's bound holds. Pitfall: waiting the full TinyHttpd write timeout (30 s) on a stalled peer would break the D-344 bound. Rejected alternative: tracking per-write ages to decide what to abort; the abort-all-unreturned rule is simpler and bounded. The closed-flag ordering shared with SSE, the D-344 margin and T44 as a whole are FR-APP-020.
- [2026-10-20] Verification coupling (wave-7 feasibility): AC-5 uses the `ShutdownParticipants` deadline overload owned by FR-APP-020 AC-1. No depends_on FR-APP-020 is declared because FR-APP-020 already depends_on this requirement for its T44 ACs and the reverse edge would form a cycle; implement FR-APP-020 AC-1 first and verify FR-WS-010 and FR-APP-020 in one group.

records.title: Explicit entry point RestApp.builder() and the JsonCodec SPI

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(a).jsonCodec(c).build()` returns a `RestApp` whose `state()` is `NEW` and whose class is the internal `DefaultRestApp`; two `build()` calls on one builder return two distinct apps. [D-111; wave-4 carried: public entry point constructs DefaultRestApp] Decision: the entry point is `RestApp.builder()` returning `RestApp.Builder`, a public final nested class whose setters return the builder. Decision: two `build()` calls on one builder share the configured adapter, codec and logger. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-1]

`build()` without `httpAdapter(...)` and `build()` without `jsonCodec(...)` each throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the missing setter, and `httpAdapter(null)`, `jsonCodec(null)` and `logger(null)` each throw `NullPointerException`. [D-111; D-137] Decision: the adapter is checked first, so a builder missing both names `httpAdapter(...)`, and a `null` setter argument throws at the setter, not at `build()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-2]

An app built without `logger(...)` has `app.logger()` returning an instance of the public console logger `com.snoworca.naruserve.ConsoleLogger` of IR-APP-006, and an app built with `logger(l)` has `app.logger()` returning `l`. [D-169; wave decision: RestApp.create()] Decision: each `build()` without `logger(...)` creates its own new `ConsoleLogger`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-3]

Reflection on `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.JsonCodec` finds exactly the two abstract methods `<T> T decode(java.io.Reader, java.lang.reflect.Type) throws java.io.IOException` and `void encode(java.lang.Object, java.io.Writer) throws java.io.IOException`, and no parameter, return or exception type of the interface lies in a `com.google.gson` package. [D-182; D-112]

`JsonCodec` and `RestApp.Builder` carry nullability annotations on every public parameter and return value, and a Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `RestApp.builder().httpAdapter(adapter).jsonCodec(codec).build()` with a Kotlin object implementing `JsonCodec`. [D-111; D-182; C-03] Decision: package `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` is `@NullMarked` and the `value` parameter of `JsonCodec#encode` is `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Middleware and Next interfaces and the middleware registration methods

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `Middleware` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request, Response, Next) throws Exception`, and `Next` with exactly the abstract methods `void run()` and `void error(Throwable)`; a Java lambda `(req, res, next) -> next.run()` compiles as a `Middleware`. [D-115; D-116]

`RestApp` declares `use(Middleware)`, `use(String, Middleware)`, the seven overloads `get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options(String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(Method, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)` and `route(MethodSet, String, Middleware, RouteHandler)`, each returning `RestApp`, and every wave 3 `RestApp` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-005 AC-5 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed to the wave 4 method set: the wave 3 methods plus those of IR-APP-002, IR-APP-003, IR-APP-005, IR-APP-006 and IR-APP-007, with `create()` and `builder()` as the only static methods. [D-119; I-014; D-137] Decision: the route-middleware overloads return `RestApp` like the plain registration methods.

`RouteBuilder` declares `use(Middleware)` returning `RouteBuilder`; middleware added through it applies as route middleware to every method the same builder registers after the `use` call, in `use` call order, so `app.route("/a").use(m1).use(m2).get(h)` runs `m1`, `m2`, then `h` for `GET /a`. [D-137; D-120] Decision: `RouteBuilder.use(middleware)` is adopted and is the way to attach several route middleware; no varargs or multi-middleware overload is added to `RestApp`.

`use(null)`, `use("/api", null)`, `use(null, mw)` and every route-middleware overload with a `null` middleware or handler throw `NullPointerException`, and `use(prefix, mw)` with a prefix that does not start with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-118; D-119] Decision: each refused call throws before anything is recorded. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-7]

No public type of `NaruServe-api` declares a method that resumes a middleware chain from another thread or returns a future, and `Next` has no method other than `run()` and `error(Throwable)`. [D-128]

A Kotlin test in `NaruServe-api` compiles and runs `app.use { req, res, next -> next.run() }`, `app.use("/api") { req, res, next -> next.run() }` and `app.get("/x", mw) { req, res -> res.send("x") }` without a DSL. [D-115; C-03]

records.title: onError, ErrorHandler and the framework HTTP error types

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ErrorHandler` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Throwable, Request, Response) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onError(ErrorHandler)` returning `RestApp`; `app.onError((error, req, res) -> res.status(500).send("x"))` compiles in Java and `app.onError { error, req, res -> }` in a Kotlin test. [D-129; D-137] Decision: the callback interface is `ErrorHandler` and it may throw `Exception`.

`HttpException` extends `RuntimeException`, has public constructors `(int status)`, `(int status, String message)` and `(int status, String message, Throwable cause)`, and `status()` returns the given status; a status outside `400..599` throws `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-130; D-134] Decision: framework errors expose their status through `HttpException#status()`. Decision: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names the refused status. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-1 SDS-AC-9]
`HttpException#code()` returns the `code` value of FR-APP-006 for its status (for example `BAD_REQUEST` for `400`, `UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY` for `422`). [D-130; D-137]
`new UnsupportedMediaTypeException()` and `new UnsupportedMediaTypeException("m")` are `HttpException`s with `status()` `415` and `code()` `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`. [D-134; wave decision: 415]
`onError(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, and `onError` is a registration method under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002. [D-114; D-129]

records.title: ServiceRegistry, ApplicationContext and the request service accessors

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `ServiceRegistry` exactly `register(Class, Object)`, `registerExternal(Class, Object)`, `get(Class)`, `getOrNull(Class)` and `contains(Class)` with the generic signatures of the requirement, and on `ApplicationContext` (a subinterface of `ServiceRegistry`) `attribute(String, Object)`, `attribute(String, Class)`, `own(AutoCloseable)` and `logger()`. [D-138; D-151] Decision: an externally owned object is registered with `registerExternal(Class<T>, T)`, which the framework never closes.

`get(type)` for a type that is not registered throws `ServiceNotFoundException` (a `RuntimeException`) whose message names the type, and `getOrNull(type)` returns `null` and `contains(type)` returns `false` for it. [D-138] Decision: the `ServiceNotFoundException` message contains the binary name of the type. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-1]

`Request` declares `ApplicationContext application()` and `<T> T service(Class<T> type)`, and every wave 3 `Request` method keeps its signature. The wave 3 surface test of IR-HTTP-001 AC-3 (a statement about the wave 3 merge) is re-pointed so that `service` and `application` are expected on `Request` from wave 4. [D-142; I-014]

`register`, `registerExternal` and `own` with a `null` argument, `get`, `getOrNull` and `contains` with a `null` type, and `attribute` with a `null` key throw `NullPointerException`; the value parameter of `attribute(String, Object)` is `@Nullable` and storing a typed `null` variable (`Object v = null; ctx.attribute(key, v)`) removes the key, because a literal `null` resolves to the read overload; `attribute(key, type)` throws `ClassCastException` when the stored value is not an instance of `type`, as the request attribute store of FR-HTTP-012 does. [D-138; D-144]

The new types carry nullability annotations on public signatures (`getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` `@Nullable`, `get` and `service` `@NonNull`), and a Kotlin test compiles `ctx.register(UserService::class.java, s)` and `req.service(UserService::class.java)` with a non-null result type. [D-138; C-03] Decision: of these signatures only the returns of `getOrNull` and `attribute(String, Class)` are `@Nullable`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-4]

records.title: Lifecycle API: AppState, onStart/onStop, listen, ServerHandle and shutdown

acceptanceCriteria.text: `AppState.values()` is exactly `NEW, STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING, FAILED, TERMINATED` in that order, and `app.state()` of a newly built app is `NEW`. [D-152]

Reflection finds `LifecycleCallback` annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(ApplicationContext) throws Exception`, and `RestApp.onStart(LifecycleCallback)` and `RestApp.onStop(LifecycleCallback)` returning `RestApp`; `onStart(null)` and `onStop(null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-137] Decision: `onStart` and `onStop` share the callback interface `LifecycleCallback`, which may throw `Exception`.

`ServerHandle` declares exactly `int port()`, `String address()` and `AppState state()`; after `listen(0)` succeeded `port()` returns the adapter's `boundPort()`, `address()` returns `127.0.0.1` and `state()` returns the app's current state, so it reads `TERMINATED` after shutdown. [D-155] Decision: the accessors are `port()`, `address()` and `state()`, and `listen` binds to `127.0.0.1`.

`listen(port)` with a port outside `0..65535` throws `IllegalArgumentException` and leaves the state `NEW`; `shutdown(timeout, unit)` with a negative timeout throws `IllegalArgumentException` and with a `null` unit `NullPointerException`. [D-153; D-161] Decision: the argument checks of `listen` and `shutdown` run before any state change. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-6]

`AppStartException` extends `RuntimeException`; it is the type `listen()` throws for a checked start-failure cause (as its cause) and for a start ended by a pending stop. [D-159; D-426] Decision: the unchecked wrapper type is `AppStartException`. Decision: `AppStartException` has a public `(String message, Throwable cause)` constructor. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-7]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.onStart { ctx -> ctx.attribute("k", 1) }`, `val h = app.listen(0)`, `h.port()`, `app.state()` and `app.shutdown(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`. [D-152; D-155; C-03]

records.title: Logger SPI, LogLevel, the console logger and app.logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds on `Logger` exactly the six abstract methods `trace(String)`, `debug(String)`, `info(String)`, `warn(String)`, `error(String)` and `error(String, Throwable)`, and `LogLevel.values()` is `TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR`. [D-168; wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`new ConsoleLogger()` writes `info`, `warn` and `error` records and drops `trace` and `debug`; `new ConsoleLogger(LogLevel.TRACE)` writes all five levels. Each record is one line `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>` where the timestamp is formatted with `SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSSZ")` (offset like `+0900`; no `java.time`, no `X` pattern, both absent from Android API 21), checked by a test under two time zones, `TRACE`/`DEBUG`/`INFO` go to `System.out` and `WARN`/`ERROR` to `System.err`, and `error(m, t)` writes the stack trace of `t` after the line. [D-169; D-181] Decision: the console logger defaults to threshold `INFO` and uses this line format. Decision: the console logger reads `System.out` and `System.err` at write time, so a stream replaced through `System.setOut` or `System.setErr` receives later records. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-2 SDS-AC-9]
`ConsoleLogger#close()` and `flush()` flush both streams and leave `System.out` and `System.err` open, so a later `System.out.println` still prints. [wave decision: Logger shutdown]

`app.logger(l)` makes `app.logger()` return `l`, `app.logger()` before any call returns the builder's logger (the console logger by default), and `app.logger(null)` throws `NullPointerException`; `logger(l)` is under the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 while `logger()` is readable in every state. [D-170; D-114]
`ConsoleLogger` is in `NaruServe-api` and references no SLF4J or `android.*` type. [D-169; D-178]

records.title: Cookie value class and SameSite enum

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie` public and final with exactly one public constructor `(String, String)`, a `getName()` method and no `setName` method; `new Cookie("sid", "abc").getName()` returns `sid` and `getValue()` returns `abc`; `new Cookie(null, "v")` and `new Cookie("n", null)` throw `NullPointerException`. [D-200]

`Cookie` declares `String getValue()`/`void setValue(String)`, `@Nullable String getPath()`/`void setPath(@Nullable String)`, `@Nullable String getDomain()`/`void setDomain(@Nullable String)`, `int getMaxAge()`/`void setMaxAge(int)`, `boolean getSecure()`/`void setSecure(boolean)`, `boolean isHttpOnly()`/`void setHttpOnly(boolean)` and `@Nullable SameSite getSameSite()`/`void setSameSite(@Nullable SameSite)`; a new cookie has path, domain and SameSite `null`, `getSecure()` and `isHttpOnly()` `false` and `getMaxAge()` `-1`. [D-201; D-208] Decision: setters return `void` like the Servlet `Cookie`, and an unset path, domain or SameSite is `null`.
`SameSite.values()` is exactly `STRICT, LAX, NONE` in that order. [D-202]

`setMaxAge(int)` accepts every `int`: a negative value (the default `-1`) means the attribute is not set, so the cookie is a session cookie, `0` means delete and a positive value is a lifetime in seconds. [D-208] Decision: the default `maxAge` is `-1`, and every negative value means "no `Max-Age`" as in the Servlet `Cookie`.

The constructor rejects with `IllegalArgumentException` a name that is empty or not an RFC 7230 token (for example containing a space, `=`, `;`, `,`, CR or LF), and the constructor and `setValue` reject a value with any character outside RFC 6265 `cookie-octet` (CR, LF, `;`, `,`, space, `\\`, a control character or non-ASCII), except that one pair of surrounding double quotes is accepted; `setPath` and `setDomain` reject CR, LF, `;` and every control character; the exception message names the rejected attribute. [D-205; I-017] Decision: an empty value is allowed, so `new Cookie("sid", "")` is valid.

`Cookie` has a package-private static factory method that builds a cookie from a name and a value without validation; the request-cookie parser in `com.snoworca.naruserve.internal` reaches it through the internal class `CookieFactoryHook`, whose `private static final java.lang.reflect.Method` field is resolved once with `Class.forName("com.snoworca.naruserve.Cookie")` (which also initialises `Cookie`) and `setAccessible(true)`, so no mutable static field exists and the no-mutable-static check of FR-APP-002 AC-2 still passes; the `NaruServe-api` consumer rules of IR-JSON-001 AC-3 also keep that factory method by name; reflection finds no public or protected member of `Cookie` other than those of AC-1 and AC-2 and the `Object` methods. [residual: Building request cookies; wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; FR-APP-002] Decision: the bridge is a reflective, immutable `Method` handle in `internal.CookieFactoryHook`, with no `java.util.function` type (absent from API 21).

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `val c = Cookie("sid", "v"); c.maxAge = 60; c.secure = true; c.isHttpOnly = true; c.sameSite = SameSite.LAX; c.path = "/"; val p: String? = c.path; val n: String = c.name`. [D-201; C-03; I-010]

records.title: Server settings API: app.server(Configurer<ServerOptions>) and app.trustProxy

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp server(Configurer<ServerOptions>)` and `RestApp trustProxy(boolean)`; `server(null)` throws `NullPointerException`, both methods throw `IllegalStateException` outside `NEW` through the guard of FR-APP-002, and several `server(...)` calls apply in call order to one options object. [D-225; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the settings entry point is `app.server(options -> ...)` and proxy trust is `app.trustProxy(boolean)` (Express `app.set('trust proxy', true)`).

`ServerOptions` declares exactly these setters, each returning `ServerOptions`, with these defaults and inclusive ranges: `bindAddress(String)` `127.0.0.1`; `allowedHosts(String...)` none; `maxHeaderSize(int bytes)` 16384, 1..1048576; `maxHeaderCount(int)` 100, 1..10000; `maxRequestLineLength(int bytes)` 8190, 1..65534; `headerTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 10 s, `bodyReadTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s and `writeTimeout(long, TimeUnit)` 30 s, each 1 ms..1 h; `minBodyRate(int bytesPerSecond)` 240, 1..104857600; `maxWorkers(int)` 64, 1..1024; `maxSseStreams(int)` 128, 1..1024; `maxConnections(int)` 512, 1..65536; `maxUpgradedConnections(int)` 128, 1..65536; `maxConnectionsPerAddress(int)` 256, 1..65536. [D-225; D-215; D-216; D-404; D-413; D-414; residual: Upper bounds on size settings] Decision: these names and maxima; `maxWorkers` is the HTTP worker budget of D-404, and `writeTimeout` maps TinyHttpd's socket write timeout (default 30000 ms) so the socket write timeout that `docs/api/defaults.md` names is configurable.

A value below the minimum or above the maximum of AC-2 makes its setter throw `IllegalArgumentException` naming the setting and the allowed range, and `bindAddress(null)`, `bindAddress("")`, `allowedHosts((String[]) null)`, a `null` or empty host name and a `null` `TimeUnit` throw `NullPointerException` or `IllegalArgumentException`; no setter accepts `0`, a negative value or another value meaning unlimited. [residual: Upper bounds on size settings; I-012]

`maxHeaderSize` changes only the total header size of D-215 and leaves the per-line header limit of D-437 unchanged, and `maxRequestLineLength(n)` is the request-line limit that D-414 turns into TinyHttpd's `inputBufferBytes = max(8192, n + 2)`. [D-437; D-414]
`listen(port)` keeps the loopback default: an app that never calls `server(...)` binds `127.0.0.1`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-211]
A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.server { o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0").allowedHosts("myphone.local").maxHeaderSize(32768) }` and `app.trustProxy(true)`. [D-225; C-03; I-010]

The `RestApp` surface test of IR-APP-002 AC-2 (`HttpApiSurfaceTest`, the wave 4 method set) is re-pointed to the wave 5 set: the wave 4 methods plus `server`, `trustProxy`, `jsonCodec` and `jsonLimit`, every wave 4 signature unchanged, `create()` and `builder()` still the only static methods and no `@Nullable` position on `RestApp`. [I-014; D-225; D-185]

records.title: HttpAdapter settings bind: ServerSettings value, ErrorRenderer and safe logger

acceptanceCriteria.text: `HttpAdapter` keeps `void bind(String, int, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` unchanged and gains the `default` method `void bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler) throws IOException` whose body calls `bind(settings.bindAddress(), settings.port(), handler)`; the test-fixtures `InMemoryHttpAdapter` and a minimal adapter that implements only the four wave 3 methods compile and bind unchanged. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; I-014; D-107]

`DefaultRestApp.listen(port)` calls `bind(ServerSettings, ExchangeHandler)` exactly once with a settings value whose `port()` is the `listen` argument and whose other values equal the frozen `ServerOptions` (defaults when `server(...)` was never called), so a recording adapter sees `127.0.0.1` by default and `0.0.0.0` after `server(o -> o.bindAddress("0.0.0.0"))`. [wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter; D-225]

`ServerSettings` is a public final class with a getter for every setting of IR-ENGINE-001 AC-2, the port, `Logger logger()` and `ErrorRenderer errorRenderer()`; it has no setter, `allowedHosts()` returns an unmodifiable list, and no parameter, return or field type of `ServerSettings` or `ErrorRenderer` lies outside `java.*` and `com.snoworca.naruserve` packages. [D-104; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter]

The `logger()` of the settings value is the core's exception-safe wrapper of the app logger, so a test app logger that throws on every call, used by an adapter through `settings.logger().warn(...)`, never lets an exception reach the adapter. [wave decision: The adapter gets the safe logger; D-220]

`ErrorRenderer` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with `String render(int status)`; the renderer in the settings returns the standard error body of FR-APP-006 for that status with the `code` of its status and a fresh 16-hex-digit request id on every call, identical in format to the body the dispatcher writes. [D-405; D-132; wave decision: Server settings reach the adapter] Decision: the renderer returns the JSON text, which the adapter sends as `application/json; charset=UTF-8`.

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Request` is a public interface in `com.snoworca.naruserve` declaring `method()`, `path()`, `rawPath()`, `param(name)`, `query(name)`, `queries(name)`, `header(name)`, `headers(name)`, `remoteAddress()`, `isSecure()`, `lastEventId()`, `attribute(key, value)` and `attribute(key, type)`, with `method()` returning `Method`. [D-071] Decision: the write overload `attribute(String, @Nullable Object)` returns `void` and the read overload is generic `<T> @Nullable T attribute(String, Class<T>)`, so a literal `null` second argument resolves to the read overload. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-1]

`Response` is a public interface in `com.snoworca.naruserve` declaring `status(code)`, `header(name, value)`, `send(String)`, `send(byte[])`, `html(String)`, `stream(InputStream, contentType)`, `end()`, `isCommitted()` and `abort(error)`. [D-071] Decision: `status` and `header` return the receiver; `send`, `html`, `stream`, `end` and `abort` return `void`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-1 SDS-AC-2]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI exchange data contract

acceptanceCriteria.text: The SPI exposes, per request, the request line as the method token, the raw request-target path, the raw query string (or its absence) and the HTTP version, plus the header names and values in received order, a body `InputStream`, the remote address and the secure flag. [D-105] Decision: the headers are exposed as a `List<Map.Entry<String, String>>` in received order with duplicates kept, not as a `Map`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-1]

The SPI accepts from the core a status code, response headers and a body `OutputStream`, and the core writes status and headers before the first body byte. [D-105] Decision: status, headers and the content length (`-1` when unknown) pass in one `commit` call that returns the body `OutputStream`, and a second start of the response throws `IllegalStateException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-2] The exchange outlives `ExchangeHandler#handle` until the core calls `finish` or `abort`, and the adapter may force-close it only at its stop deadline; `abort()` is idempotent and thread-safe (it may run on any thread, also while another thread is in `commit`, a body write or `finish`, which then fail with an `IOException`). The headers passed to `commit` are sent as given: they already carry `Content-Length` when the core knows it (a `HEAD` response carries the length the `GET` body would have had) and the adapter never adds, removes or changes `Content-Length`; `contentLength` is the number of body bytes the core will write, `0` for a bodyless response (`204`, `304`, `HEAD`) or `-1` when unknown, which the adapter frames itself (chunked, or close on HTTP/1.0) and is the only case where it may add a framing header. Header names and values are ISO-8859-1: the core guarantees every char is at most U+00FF and never CR or LF, so the adapter writes each char as one byte. [wave 3 implementation decision]

The raw request-target path and the raw query string travel through the SPI as separate undecoded fields: an exchange with target `/a%20b?x=%41` reaches the core with raw path `/a%20b` and raw query `x=%41`, and the core alone yields `req.path()` = `/a b` and `req.query("x")` = `A`. [D-399; wave decision: Adapter halves] Decision: the raw query is `null` when the target has no `?`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-3]

records.title: HttpAdapter SPI extension points and bind/stop lifecycle

acceptanceCriteria.text: Through the file-transfer extension point the core hands the adapter a `java.io.File` with an offset and a length, and the adapter writes exactly those bytes of the file as the response body; an in-memory test hands over a file with a non-zero offset and a length shorter than the rest of the file and reads back exactly that byte range from the client body. [D-106]

Through the protocol-upgrade extension point the core hands the adapter an upgrade callback with a `101` response, and the adapter invokes that callback with the exchange's raw input and output streams after writing the `101` response; an in-memory test observes that the callback ran with the exchange's streams (or that the in-memory adapter recorded the hand-over). [D-106]

The event-stream point hands the adapter a core-owned drain loop that keeps writing after the handler returned until the core reports the stream ended, and the adapter chooses the thread that runs it; in wave 3 (before `res.sse` exists) an in-memory test supplies a drain loop through the SPI type, runs it on an adapter-chosen thread after the handler returned and sees it end only when the end is reported. [D-106] Decision: `eventStream` returns to the caller at once, and the in-memory adapter runs the drain on its own worker thread, completing the client response when the drain returns. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-4]

The three extension points are SPI types in `NaruServe-api`, usable by an adapter without any NaruServe class outside `NaruServe-api`, so waves 6, 7 and 8 add adapter classes against them without changing the SPI. [D-106]

The SPI declares a bind to an address and port that returns only after binding completed, and a separate call through which the core reads the actual bound port; with the in-memory adapter, a bind with port `0` reports a positive bound port that the core reads back through the SPI and that stays the same on every read until stop, and a bind with a positive port reports that port. [D-107] Decision: for a bind with port `0` the in-memory adapter assigns a positive port from a counter starting at `49152`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-5]

The SPI declares a blocking stop that stops accepting, waits for in-flight exchanges until a deadline passed by the core and then force-closes the remaining connections, and a separate final release that waits at most a fixed margin for the adapter's threads to end; the in-memory adapter implements both and a test shows an in-flight exchange still running at the deadline is force-closed. [D-107] Decision: an exchange in flight at the deadline is aborted so its client response reports `abnormallyClosed`, and the in-memory adapter's release shuts its worker pool waiting at most 1 second. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-3-2 SDS-AC-6]

records.title: HttpException response headers: withHeader, headers() and the error path that applies them

acceptanceCriteria.text: `HttpException` declares `public HttpException withHeader(String name, String value)` returning the same instance and `public List<Map.Entry<String, String>> headers()`, which returns an empty list for a new exception; the existing constructors, `status()` and `code()` keep their signatures, which a reflection test asserts. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]

`new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1").withHeader("Connection", "close")` returns entries in that order from `headers()`, adding the same name twice keeps both entries in order, and calling `add` or `remove` on the returned list throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] Decision: entries are kept in an `ArrayList` of `SimpleImmutableEntry` so the exception stays `Serializable`, and `headers()` returns `Collections.unmodifiableList` of it. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-8]

`withHeader` with a name or value containing CR or LF throws `IllegalArgumentException`, with a `null` name or value throws `NullPointerException`, and in both cases `headers()` is unchanged afterwards. Decision: the check is the `res.header` check of FR-HTTP-015. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] Decision: a name that is not a token, a control character in the value and a character above U+00FF in the value are refused with `IllegalArgumentException` as well as CR and LF. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-7]

A handler that sets `X-App: 1` and then throws `new HttpException(426).withHeader("Sec-WebSocket-Version", "13")` gives the client `426`, the header `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13`, the standard error body with the request id, and no `X-App` header, because the error path drops app-set headers as FR-APP-005 states and then applies the exception's headers. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] [D-444] Decision: the exception's headers are appended after the app-set headers were cleared and `Content-Type` was set; when an `onError` handler itself throws, that exception is the error, so the original exception's headers are not added. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-9]

When an `onError` handler leaves the response `NEW`, the standard error response still carries the exception's headers; when an `onError` handler answers with `res.status(418).send("x")`, the client receives only the headers that handler set and none of the exception's. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]

Over TinyHttpd, a handler throwing `new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1").withHeader("Connection", "close")` gives the client `503` with `Retry-After: 1` and `Connection: close`, and the server closes the connection after the response. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)] [D-445]

A `withHeader("Content-Length", "5")` entry is not written to the error response, whose `Content-Length` matches the standard error body, which a test asserts byte for byte. Decision: the body writer owns `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`. [wave decision: Rejection headers (W2-002)]
A Kotlin test compiles `throw HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1")` inside a SAM handler, and `withHeader` and `headers()` return non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [C-03; T11]

traceLinks.notes: error path applies the exception headers after dropping app-set headers

records.requirement: The system shall let an `HttpException` carry response headers through `withHeader(String name, String value)`, which validates the header like `res.header` and returns the same exception, and `headers()`, an unmodifiable list in insertion order, and shall set those headers on the standard error response that the dispatcher's error path renders for that exception.
records.rationale: Covers wave decision Rejection headers (W2-002; D-444, D-445): it carries `Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13` (FR-WS-002), `Retry-After` (FR-WS-009) and `Connection: close` (FR-WS-009, FR-APP-020) from a pre-`101` rejection to the error response, the way Express `finalhandler` applies `err.headers`. Measured: `HttpException.java:8-37` has the constructors `(int)`, `(int, String)`, `(int, String, Throwable)` and `status()`/`code()` and no header field; `internal/ErrorPath.java` and `internal/StandardErrors.java:60-92` render the standard error body after dropping app-set headers (FR-APP-005 AC-4, which still holds: the exception's own headers are new, not app-set ones). IR-APP-003 lists no method set, so the add-only methods need no supersede. Decision: `withHeader` returns `this` so `throw new HttpException(503).withHeader("Retry-After", "1")` compiles; duplicates are kept in order; validation reuses the `res.header` CR/LF check (FR-HTTP-015). Decision: an `onError` handler that leaves the response `NEW` still gets the exception's headers on the standard error response; an `onError` handler that answers itself decides its own headers. Pitfall: a `Content-Length` or `Transfer-Encoding` set through `withHeader` would corrupt the error body framing; the error path lets the body writer own those two names and skips them. Rejected alternative: a separate `HeaderedHttpException` subclass; every catch site would need two types, reopen never in v1.

records.title: TypeRef captures generic types and ships consumer R8/ProGuard rules

acceptanceCriteria.text: `new TypeRef<List<User>>() {}.getType()` returns a `ParameterizedType` whose raw type is `java.util.List` and whose only argument is `User`, and `new TypeRef<String>() {}.getType()` returns `String.class`. [D-183; T08] Decision: `TypeRef` is a public abstract class with a protected no-argument constructor and the public method `Type getType()`.

Constructing a raw subclass (`new TypeRef() {}`) or a subclass whose type argument is a type variable (inside `<X> TypeRef<X> make() { return new TypeRef<X>() {}; }`) throws `IllegalStateException` whose message says that a concrete type argument is required. [D-184] Decision: the exception type is `IllegalStateException`. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-1]: the message is `TypeRef needs a concrete type argument`.

records.title: JSON API surface: app.jsonCodec, app.jsonLimit, req.body, res.json and the nullable JsonCodec.decode

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `RestApp jsonCodec(JsonCodec)`; `jsonCodec(null)` throws `NullPointerException` and a call outside `NEW` throws `IllegalStateException` through the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002; after `app.jsonCodec(c2)` on an app built with codec `c1`, `req.body` and `res.json` call only `c2`, and the app's internal codec accessor, which the wave 7 `ws.sendJson` and `ws.onJson` read, returns `c2`. [D-185] Decision: the app holds one codec in `DefaultRestApp`, read through an internal accessor by every JSON feature. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-3]: the codec that `req.body` and `res.json` use is read once from the internal accessor `DefaultRestApp.jsonCodec()` at the configuration freeze.

`RestApp` declares `RestApp jsonLimit(long bytes)` under the same guard; the limit defaults to 1048576 bytes, and values below 1 or above 1073741824 throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [D-188; D-192; residual: Upper bounds on size settings] Decision: the size API is `app.jsonLimit(bytes)` with a 1 GiB maximum. Decision [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-5-1 SDS-AC-4]: the `IllegalArgumentException` message names `jsonLimit` and the range `1..1073741824`.

`Request` declares `<T> @Nullable T body(Class<T>)` and `<T> @Nullable T body(TypeRef<T>)`, and `Response` declares `void json(@Nullable Object)`; a reflection test checks the `@Nullable` type-use annotation on both `body` returns and on the `json` parameter. [D-431; D-193] Decision: `json` returns `void` like `send`.

The return type of `JsonCodec.decode` carries the JSpecify `@Nullable` type-use annotation while the erased signature `<T> T decode(Reader, Type) throws IOException` and the `@Nullable` parameter of `encode` stay unchanged, and the copy of the interface shown in `docs/api/json.md` shows the same annotations. [wave decision: A JSON `null` decodes to `null`; D-182; I-008]
Reflection finds no method named `jsonTree` or `jsonMap` on `Request`. [D-192] Decision: v1 has no `jsonTree()`/`jsonMap()`; untyped access uses `req.body(Map.class)`.
A second `req.body(...)` call, or `req.body(...)` after another body reader consumed the body, throws `BodyAlreadyConsumedException` as FR-HTTP-019 defines. [D-431; FR-HTTP-019]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.jsonCodec(codec)`, `val u: User? = req.body(User::class.java)`, `val l: List<User>? = req.body(object : TypeRef<List<User>>() {})` and `res.json(null)` without platform types. [D-431; D-440; C-03; I-010]

The wave 3 surface tests (statements about the wave 3 merge) are re-pointed as wave 4 did in IR-APP-004 AC-3: in `HttpApiSurfaceTest` the exact `Request` and `Response` method sets of IR-HTTP-001 AC-1 and AC-2 gain both `body` overloads and `json`, `body` and `json` leave the later-wave name list of IR-HTTP-001 AC-3, and the `@Nullable` position set of IR-HTTP-001 AC-4 gains the returns of both `body` overloads and the `json` parameter (beside the cookie position of FR-COOKIE-002 AC-8, no other position); in `BodyStateTest` the FR-HTTP-019 AC-5 check now allows exactly `body(Class)` and `body(TypeRef)` as the public body readers of `Request` and still finds no stream, `byte[]`, raw or text reader; every wave 3 position and signature stays as verified. [I-014; D-072; D-392; D-431] Decision: the wave 3 "exactly these positions" decision of IR-HTTP-001 AC-4 covers the wave 3 methods; new methods add positions without a supersede, following the wave 4 precedent.

records.title: Value objects follow getX, setX and isX naming so Kotlin property syntax compiles

acceptanceCriteria.text: A reflection test on `Cookie` finds, for every public `setX` method, a public `getX` or `isX` method with the same property name and the identical type, `isX` only for `boolean`, and fails naming the property otherwise. [D-353]

A Kotlin test constructs `Cookie("session", "t")` and assigns `maxAge = 60`, `isHttpOnly = true`, `secure = true`, `path = "/"`, `domain = null` and `sameSite = SameSite.LAX`, reads them back through the property names, and adds the cookie through `res.addCookie`, asserting the `Set-Cookie` header. [D-353; D-349]

A Kotlin test reads `res.isCommitted` before and after `res.send("x")` and `req.isSecure`, `req.method()` and `req.path()` in a handler, asserting `false`, `true`, a `Boolean` and the Express-style calls with parentheses. [D-353; T11]

A reflection test lists the JavaBeans property names of `Cookie` as exactly `name` (read-only), `value`, `path`, `domain`, `maxAge`, `secure`, `httpOnly` and `sameSite`, which Kotlin reads as `name`, `value`, `path`, `domain`, `maxAge`, `secure`, `isHttpOnly` and `sameSite`, so a later wave that adds an accessor must keep the `getX`/`setX`/`isX` rule and update the list together with `docs/api/cookie.md`. [D-353]

records.requirement: The system shall name the accessors of value objects such as `Cookie` with the Servlet-style `getX()`, `setX(value)` and `isX()` rules so that Kotlin property syntax compiles — `cookie.maxAge = 60`, `cookie.isHttpOnly = true`, `cookie.secure = true`, `res.isCommitted` and `req.isSecure` — while the Express-style short methods (`req.param`, `req.path`, `res.status`) stay ordinary methods.
records.rationale: Covers D-353 and wave decisions of waves 3 and 5 on `Cookie`; supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `Cookie.java:90-151` declares `getName`, `getValue`/`setValue`, `getPath`/`setPath`, `getDomain`/`setDomain`, `getMaxAge`/`setMaxAge`, `getSecure`/`setSecure`, `isHttpOnly`/`setHttpOnly` and `getSameSite`/`setSameSite`; `docs/api/kotlin.md` already shows `isHttpOnly = true`, `secure = true`, `maxAge = 3600` and `res.isCommitted`. Pitfall: Kotlin synthesises a property from a `boolean getX()` as `x` and from `boolean isX()` as `isX`; the pair `getSecure`/`setSecure` therefore reads `secure`, not `isSecure`, and a rename to `isSecure()` would break `kotlin.md`. Pitfall: a getter without a matching setter gives a read-only `val`; a setter whose parameter type differs from the getter's return type gives no property. Rejected alternative: fluent setters (`cookie.maxAge(60)`) as in Express; they would not form Kotlin properties and C-03 requires property syntax.

records.title: NaruServe-kotlin provides the reified Request.body extension

acceptanceCriteria.text: `NaruServe-kotlin/src/main/kotlin/com/snoworca/naruserve/kotlin/RequestExtensions.kt` declares exactly the function above, and a Kotlin test in `NaruServe-kotlin` compiles `val user = req.body<User>()` with `user` of type `User` (non-null) inside an `app.post` lambda; the module's `testImplementation` gains `testFixtures(project(':NaruServe-api'))` for the in-memory harness, in the root `build.gradle` (CON-BUILD-006 AC lists main dependencies only). [D-354]

Through the in-memory harness with a test `JsonCodec`, a `POST` with `{"name":"a"}` returns the decoded instance, and a `POST` whose body is the JSON `null` answers `400` with the standard error body whose message is `JSON body is null`. [D-354; T11]

A test asserts that `req.body<List<User>>()` passes the raw class `java.util.List` to the codec (no element type), matching the sentence of `docs/api/kotlin.md` that the extension does not preserve the element type. [D-354]

`NaruServe-api` and `NaruServe-servlet` stay free of `kotlin.*` and `kotlin-stdlib` stays on the `runtimeClasspath` of `NaruServe-kotlin` only, which the wave 1 build checks assert, and the test-local copy of `body()` in `JsonDocsKotlinTest` is not edited. [D-354; CON-BUILD-007; I-002]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-kotlin`, in package `com.snoworca.naruserve.kotlin`, the top-level function `inline fun <reified T : Any> Request.body(): T = body(T::class.java) ?: throw HttpException(400, "JSON body is null")`, so that `req.body<User>()` returns a non-null `T` and a JSON `null` body is a client error.
records.rationale: Covers D-354 and the module line of wave decision Kotlin reified extension of wave 5 (OPS-JSON-001 AC-3, which fixed the shape in `docs/api/kotlin.md`); supports T11. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-kotlin/src/main` holds only the placeholder `KotlinModule.NAME`; `NaruServe-api/src/test/kotlin/com/snoworca/naruserve/JsonDocsKotlinTest.kt:40` carries a test-local copy of the same function with the comment that the module extension arrives in wave 8; `NaruServe-kotlin` has `kotlin-stdlib` as `api` and depends on `NaruServe-api` (CON-BUILD-006). Decision: the file is `RequestExtensions.kt` and the consumer imports `com.snoworca.naruserve.kotlin.body`; the extension adds no overload on `Request` because the member `body(Class<T>)` takes an argument, so `req.body<User>()` resolves to the extension. Pitfall: `T::class.java` loses element types, so `req.body<List<User>>()` decodes a raw `List`; `docs/api/kotlin.md` says so and points to `TypeRef`. Rejected alternative: an extension that returns `T?`; it would only rename the member, and the point of D-354 is a non-null result for a caller that asked for one.

records.title: Multipart and form configuration API: app.multipart(Configurer<MultipartOptions>) and app.formLimit

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `multipart(Configurer<MultipartOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.MultipartOptions` declares the fluent setters `maxFileSize(long bytes)`, `maxRequestSize(long bytes)`, `maxParts(int count)`, `memoryThreshold(int bytes)` and `tempDirectory(File dir)`, each returning `MultipartOptions`; a configurer that sets all five values is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings. Decision: the configurer is the `Configurer` functional interface of IR-APP-007. [D-231] Decision: the configurer runs on a copy of the settings that is swapped in only after it returned, so a configurer that throws propagates its exception and leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-1]

An app that never calls `multipart` uses `maxFileSize` 33554432, `maxRequestSize` 67108864, `maxParts` 20, `memoryThreshold` 65536 and `tempDirectory` equal to `new File(System.getProperty("java.io.tmpdir"))`. Decision: the default temp directory is `java.io.tmpdir`, which on Android is the app's cache directory. [D-232; D-239] Decision: `java.io.tmpdir` is read once when the app is constructed, not at each parse. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-4]

`maxFileSize` and `maxRequestSize` accept 1 to 4294967296, `maxParts` accepts 1 to 10000 and `memoryThreshold` accepts 1 to 16777216, all inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the upper bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the setting, and `tempDirectory(null)` throws `NullPointerException`. Decision: unlimited multipart limits are not allowed, so no value means unlimited. [D-239] Decision: the message has the form `<setting> must be in <lo>..<hi>: <value>` and is thrown by that setter. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-2]

`RestApp` declares `formLimit(long bytes)` returning the same `RestApp`, with default 1048576 and inclusive range 1 to 1073741824; a value outside the range throws `IllegalArgumentException` naming the setting. Decision: the urlencoded limit API is `formLimit`, mirroring `jsonLimit` and Express `express.urlencoded({ limit })`. [D-238]

The part header limits are fixed at 8192 bytes per part header line and 16384 bytes of total header size per part, and reflection finds no setter for them on `MultipartOptions` or `RestApp`. Decision: the two part header limits are not configurable. [D-235; wave decision: Oversized part headers]

`multipart(...)` and `formLimit(...)` called after `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002, and leave the settings unchanged. [D-231; D-238] Decision: the `NEW`-state guard throws before the configurer is invoked. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-1 SDS-AC-3]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.multipart { o -> o.maxFileSize(1024).maxParts(3) }` and `app.formLimit(2048)` as SAM lambdas without a DSL, and the returned `MultipartOptions` and `RestApp` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-231; D-238; C-03; T11]

records.title: Request form, file, files and parts accessors and the UploadFile interface

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Request` declares `@Nullable String form(String name)`, `@Nullable UploadFile file(String name)`, `List<UploadFile> files(String name)` and `List<UploadFile> parts()`, and reflection finds each with exactly that signature. [D-240; D-241]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.UploadFile` extends `AutoCloseable` and declares `String name()`, `@Nullable String filename()`, `@Nullable String contentType()`, `long size()`, `InputStream inputStream()`, `void save(File destination)`, `void transferTo(OutputStream target)`, `byte[] bytes()` and `void close()`, the content methods declaring `throws IOException` and `close()` declaring no checked exception. Decision: `filename()` and `contentType()` return `null` when the part header has no `filename` parameter or no `Content-Type`. [D-248]

Decision: `parts()` returns every part of a multipart body in body order, text fields included (their `filename()` is `null`), as an unmodifiable `List<UploadFile>`, and returns an empty list for a urlencoded or non-form body. [D-239] Decision: repeated `parts()` calls return the same unmodifiable list instance, while `files(name)` returns a new unmodifiable list on each call. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-3 SDS-AC-4]

Decision: the in-memory limit of `UploadFile.bytes()` is fixed at 8388608 bytes (8 MiB); a part above it makes `bytes()` throw `IllegalStateException` whose message names the part size and the limit. [D-239; D-251]

No public or protected signature of `UploadFile`, `MultipartOptions` or the new `Request` methods names a `java.nio.file` type, which a reflection test checks, and the API 21 animal-sniffer check of CON-BUILD-012 passes on `NaruServe-api`. [D-253]

`HttpApiSurfaceTest`, re-pointed to this requirement, checks the wave 6 `Request` set: the wave 5 methods plus `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts`, with every earlier signature unchanged; `LATER_WAVE_NAMES` no longer lists `form`, `file`, `files` or `parts`; and the listed `@Nullable` positions gain exactly the returns of `form(String)` and `file(String)` and of `UploadFile#filename()` and `UploadFile#contentType()`. `BodyStateTest#sdsAc11_FR_HTTP_019_AC5_requestHasNoPublicBodyReadingMethod`, re-pointed to this requirement, accepts exactly `form`, `file`, `files` and `parts` as additional readers, which read through the `FORM` body kind, and still finds no `InputStream`, `byte[]`, raw or text reader on `Request`. [D-240; D-241; D-242; I-014]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs a handler that reads `val name: String = req.form("name") ?: ""`, `val f: UploadFile? = req.file("avatar")`, `f?.filename()` and `for (p in req.parts())`, and closes an upload with `f?.use { it.save(dest) }`, with no platform type left on these positions. [D-240; D-241; D-248; C-03; T11]

records.title: Method enum constants and static MethodSet factories

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Method.values()` returns exactly `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, `CONNECT` in this order. [D-030]

`Method.get()` returns a `MethodSet` containing only `GET`, `Method.of(Method.PUT, Method.PATCH)` returns a `MethodSet` containing exactly `PUT` and `PATCH`, and `Method.any()` returns a `MethodSet`; all three are static methods of `Method`. [D-031] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-1 SDS-AC-2] `Method.of` throws `NullPointerException` for a null array or a null element.

Reflection over `Method` finds no non-static method, and no static method other than `get()`, whose name is `get`, `head`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`, `options`, `trace` or `connect` (case-insensitive), so `Method.GET.delete()` does not compile. [D-032]

records.title: Immutable MethodSet combinators

acceptanceCriteria.text: For `MethodSet s = Method.get()`, calling `s.post()` returns a set containing `GET` and `POST`, and `s` still contains only `GET` afterwards; the same holds for every combinator and for `except`. [D-033] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-1 SDS-AC-4] Every combinator, `with` and `except` returns a different `MethodSet` instance unless the members are unchanged, and leaves the receiver's members unchanged.

`Method.get().delete().post()` contains exactly `GET`, `DELETE` and `POST`, and each of `get()`, `head()`, `post()`, `put()`, `patch()`, `delete()` and `options()` adds exactly its own constant to the receiver's members. [D-034]
`Method.get().post().except(Method.POST)` contains exactly `GET`, and `except` of a method that is not a member returns a set equal to the receiver. [D-035]
`MethodSet` has no public constructor or mutator, its fields are final, and any iterator or collection it exposes is unmodifiable (`remove` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`). [D-033]

records.title: MethodSet membership, ordered iteration and value equality

acceptanceCriteria.text: The membership accessor returns true for every member and false for every other `Method` constant; the iteration accessor of `Method.of(Method.DELETE, Method.GET, Method.POST)` yields `GET`, `POST`, `DELETE` in that order. [D-038]

`Method.get().post()` equals `Method.of(Method.POST, Method.GET)` and both have the same `hashCode()`; sets with different members are not equal. [D-039] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-1 SDS-AC-7] `toString()` lists the members in declaration order joined by ", " (the `Allow` header form).

records.title: Lookup result contract and precedence

acceptanceCriteria.text: The result type exposes exactly six kinds and each lookup returns exactly one; the matched kind carries the handler, the path parameters, the actual method (the request method for a direct match, `GET` under automatic `HEAD` and for a WebSocket match; it does not decide the wave 3 `req.method()` value, D-398), the route kind and the automatic-`HEAD` flag, and the method-mismatch and automatic-OPTIONS kinds carry an `Allow` `MethodSet`. [D-390] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-1] A field a kind does not carry reads as null (handler, method, route kind, allow) and params reads as an empty map.

An unrecognised method token yields unsupported method even when no pattern matches the path, and a recognised method on a path no pattern matches yields no match. [wave decision: lookup result order]
On a matched path a route of the request method wins over automatic OPTIONS and automatic `HEAD`, which win over WebSocket-only, which wins over method mismatch. [wave decision: lookup result order]

The lookup takes the raw, undecoded path as received in the request target, so a lookup of `GET /files/%252e` against `GET /files/:name` yields `name` = `%2e`; the path is checked with the path validator before any result is chosen, so a rejected path such as `/a%zz` fails with `IllegalArgumentException` for every method token, and "whatever the path" elsewhere in this scope means whatever accepted path. [D-051; loop W residual: validator does not decode] [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-2-3 SDS-AC-2] The `IllegalArgumentException` names the path and is thrown before the method token is read.

The upgrade flag is ignored unless the method token is `GET`; registering a route after the freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, a lookup before a successful freeze fails with `IllegalStateException`, and the routing configuration error is an exception type of its own (name decided under C-07), distinct from `IllegalStateException` and `IllegalArgumentException`. [wave decision: route kind; D-058]

records.title: Public SSE API: res.sse(), SseClient, SseEvent and app.sse(Configurer<SseOptions>)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `Response` declares `default SseClient sse()`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` naming the class on a `Response` implementation that does not override it, and the internal `DefaultResponse` overrides it; a reflection test asserts the default method and the override. Decision: `sse()` is a `default` method like `json` and `addCookie`, so the `Response` change is add-only. [D-326] Decision: the message is `<class> has no SSE writer`, the form that `json` and `addCookie` use. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-1]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.SseClient` declares `boolean send(String event, String data)`, `boolean send(String data)`, `boolean send(SseEvent event)`, `void close()`, `boolean isOpen()` and `void onClose(SseClient.CloseListener listener)`, and the nested `SseClient.CloseListener` is annotated `@FunctionalInterface` with the single method `void onClose() throws Exception`, which a reflection test lists. Decision: the data-only send is `send(String data)`, the explicit close is `close()`, and `send` returns `false` exactly when the client has ended or this send ends it (closed by `close()`, disconnected, overflowed, shut down, or a `HEAD` request), so the send that overflows the queue returns `false` as FR-SSE-002 states, and `true` otherwise, when the event was written or queued. [D-339]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.SseEvent` has no public constructor and declares the public static factory `SseEvent event(String name)` and the instance methods `id(String id)`, `data(@Nullable String data)` and `retry(long millis)`, each returning `SseEvent`; a Java test compiles `SseEvent.event("progress").id("100").data("x").retry(3000)` and reflection finds no other public method declared by `SseEvent`. [D-330]

`RestApp` declares `sse(Configurer<SseOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.SseOptions` declares `heartbeatInterval(long time, TimeUnit unit)` and `sendQueueSize(int bytes)`, each returning `SseOptions`; a configurer setting both is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings, `sse(...)` called after `listen()` throws `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 without running the configurer, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `sse(Configurer)->RestApp`. Decision: the configurer runs on a copy swapped in only after it returned, so a throwing configurer leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [D-339; D-419] Decision: `requireConfigurable("sse")` runs before the null check, and the configurer runs on `copy()`, which is swapped in only after it returned. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-3]

An app that never calls `sse` uses `heartbeatInterval` 15 s and `sendQueueSize` 262144 bytes, which a test reads through the internal settings. Decision: the heartbeat interval default is 15 s. [D-339; D-332; D-419]

`heartbeatInterval` accepts 1 s to 1 h and `sendQueueSize` accepts 1 to 16777216, both inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message has the form `sendQueueSize must be in 1..16777216: <value>` for the size and `heartbeatInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: <time> <unit>` for the duration, a `null` unit throws `NullPointerException`, and no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited: every setting has a bounded range and a finite default (I-012). [D-419; D-339] Decision: the duration is converted with `unit.toMillis` (saturating) and accepted at 1000..3600000 ms, so `999 MILLISECONDS` is refused with the caller's own time and unit in the message. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-9 SDS-AC-4]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.get("/events") { req, res -> val c = res.sse(); c.send("ready"); c.onClose { } }` and `app.sse { o -> o.heartbeatInterval(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS) }` as SAM lambdas without a DSL against the in-memory adapter, and `res.sse()`, `SseEvent.event("x")` and the returned `SseOptions` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-326; C-03; T11]

records.rationale:
Covers D-326 (API part), D-330 (API part), D-339 (heartbeat, data-only send and explicit close APIs), D-419 (SSE setting name) and the C-07 choices of the authoring plan; T11/C-03 for Kotlin. Measured: `Response.java:9` says "No sse method yet; a later wave adds it", and `json` (`:55`) and `addCookie` (`:66`) are `default` methods throwing `UnsupportedOperationException`, so `sse()` follows the same add-only pattern (I-014: no changed public signature). `Request.java:47` already declares `lastEventId()` (FR-HTTP-011 AC-3), reused by FR-SSE-001. The configurer follows IR-APP-007 and IR-MULTIPART-001 (copy swapped in after it returned; message `sendQueueSize must be in 1..16777216: <value>` for the size and `heartbeatInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: <time> <unit>` for the duration, as AC-6 states), and the ranges keep I-012 (no unlimited value). Decision on defaults: heartbeat 15 s, below the 30 s to 60 s idle cutoffs of common proxies and load balancers; send queue 256 KiB from D-406. Pitfall: a `send` that throws on an ended client would force every broadcaster to catch; `send` returns `false` instead, like the `ws` library's send on a closed socket. Rejected alternative: a fluent `SseEvent` with a public constructor; the factory keeps `event` mandatory and matches `docs/api/sse.md`, reopen if data-only `SseEvent` objects are requested. Rejected alternative: Express-style `res.write` of raw event text; it leaves line splitting to the app and breaks D-329. Express mapping: `res.writeHead(200, {'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream'})` plus `res.write('event: x
data: y

')` and `req.on('close')`. Test to re-point: `HttpApiSurfaceTest` (the `LATER_WAVE_NAMES` entry `sse` and the `Response` method set) moves to IR-SSE-001.

records.title: Static mount API: app.staticFiles, StaticOptions and the engine-free ResourceResolver

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `staticFiles(String prefix, File dir)` and `staticFiles(String prefix, File dir, Configurer<StaticOptions> options)`, both returning the same `RestApp`; a prefix not starting with `/` throws `IllegalArgumentException`, a `null` argument throws `NullPointerException`, and several calls with different prefixes register several mounts. Decision: a trailing `/` on the prefix is ignored, so `/assets` and `/assets/` name the same mount. [D-256; D-258] Decision: a trailing `/` is stripped except from the prefix `/` itself, and the same prefix registered twice keeps both mounts in registration order, like two Express `static` middlewares. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-1] Decision: a `dir` that does not exist is accepted at registration; the canonical root is taken at `listen`, and a missing root serves nothing (`404`). [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-2]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.StaticOptions` declares `index(String name)` (default `index.html`), `directoryListing(boolean)` (default `false`), `spaFallback(boolean)` (default `false`), `spaExclude(String... prefixes)`, `cache(String pattern, CachePolicy policy)`, `mime(String ext, String type)` and `allowSymlinks(boolean)` (default `false`), each returning `StaticOptions`. Decision: `allowSymlinks(true)` serves symbolic links below the root while the canonical-root containment still applies, `spaExclude` adds prefixes to the always-excluded `/api/` and `/ws/`, and `mime(ext, type)` accepts `ext` with or without the leading dot (a leading dot is stripped), like `MimeTypes.register`. [D-261; D-272; D-267; D-275] Decision: `index` with an empty name or a name holding `/`, and `spaExclude` with a prefix not starting with `/`, throw `IllegalArgumentException`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-3]

The public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.ResourceResolver` in `NaruServe-api` declares `open`, `length`, `etag` and `modified` and names only `java.io` and `java.lang` types; the built-in `java.io.File` resolver is an internal class and the only implementation in v1, and reflection finds no public or protected method of `RestApp`, `StaticOptions` or `Response` that accepts a `ResourceResolver`. Decision: `InputStream open(String path)`, `long length(String path)`, `String etag(String path)` and `long modified(String path)` take the mount-relative path; for `res.file` and `res.download`, which have no mount, the built-in resolver is rooted at the canonical absolute parent of the named file (FR-STATIC-006 AC-5) and the path is the file's name; the SAF resolver is a post-v1 P5 item under D-380. [D-409; wave decision: The root of res.file and res.download] Decision: a resolver method that cannot read the path throws `IOException`, and `FileNotFoundException` for a missing or refused path. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-4]

No public or protected signature of `StaticOptions`, `ResourceResolver`, `CachePolicy` or `MimeTypes` names a `java.nio.file` type (reflection test), and the API 21 animal-sniffer check of CON-BUILD-012 passes on `NaruServe-api`. [D-409; D-270]

`AppLifecycleGuardTest#sdsAc4_FR_APP_002_AC4_reflectionFindsEveryRestAppAndRouteBuilderRegistrationRefusedInRunning`, re-pointed to this requirement, covers the new `RestApp` setters `multipart`, `formLimit`, both `staticFiles` overloads and `defaultCache`, each throwing `IllegalStateException` under the `NEW`-state guard when called after `listen()`, and `mimeTypes().register(...)` after `listen()` also throws `IllegalStateException`. [D-231; D-238; D-256; D-410; D-277]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.staticFiles("/", dir) { o -> o.index("main.html").spaFallback(true) }` and `app.staticFiles("/assets", File("public"))` without a DSL, then requests `/` and receives `main.html`, with `StaticOptions` a non-platform type. [D-256; D-261; C-03; T11]

records.title: CachePolicy, MimeTypes, res.cache, res.file, res.download and app.defaultCache API

acceptanceCriteria.text: The public final class `com.snoworca.naruserve.CachePolicy` has no public constructor and no setter, provides the static factories `noStore()`, `noCache()`, `privateFor(long amount, TimeUnit unit)` and `publicFor(long amount, TimeUnit unit)`, and `immutable()` returns a new `CachePolicy` while the receiver keeps its value. Decision: the header value is read through `String getHeaderValue()`, so Kotlin reads `policy.headerValue`. [D-278] Decision: `privateFor` and `publicFor` with a negative amount throw `IllegalArgumentException`, and `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString` follow `getHeaderValue()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-5]

`RestApp mimeTypes()` returns a `MimeTypes` whose `MimeTypes register(String ext, String type)` returns the same registry for chaining; two apps get two independent registries. Decision: `ext` is accepted with or without the leading dot, and a leading dot is stripped, the same rule as `StaticOptions.mime`. [D-277]

Decision: `res.file` sends no `Content-Disposition`, like Express `res.sendFile`. [D-280; D-292; D-293] Decision: `cache` on a committed response throws `IllegalStateException`, like `header`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-6-5 SDS-AC-6]
`RestApp` declares `defaultCache(@Nullable CachePolicy policy)` returning the same `RestApp`. Decision: the default is `null`, which adds no `Cache-Control` header. [D-410]
