records.title: NaruServe-servlet public surface: ServletAdapter, ServletConfigurer, NaruServeInitializer and the init-parameters

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reflection finds `ServletAdapter` public, final, implementing `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.HttpAdapter` with a public no-argument constructor; `ServletConfigurer` a public interface annotated `@FunctionalInterface` whose only abstract method is `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder)` declared `throws Exception`; `NaruServeInitializer` a public class implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`; and package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet` annotated `@NullMarked`. [D-358; D-363]

The built module jar holds `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer` whose only line is `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet.NaruServeInitializer`, read from the jar as `DefaultAppFactoryTest` reads the bootstrap services file, through a new system property that `build.gradle` sets for `:NaruServe-servlet` tests (as it does `naruserve.bootstrapJar` for `:NaruServe`). [D-363]

On an embedded Jetty 9.4 `WebAppContext` started with its annotation configuration (the `jetty-webapp` and `jetty-annotations` test dependencies of CON-SVL-001), the initializer is discovered from the services file without any test code naming it; a web application with the init-parameter `naruserve.configurer` registers exactly one servlet named `naruserve` mapped to `/*`, with `isAsyncSupported() == true` and no multipart configuration, and a web application without the init-parameter registers nothing and every request is answered by the container (`404`). Residual gap: other Servlet 3.1 containers are not exercised and `docs/api/servlet.md` says so. [D-363; r4 W2-005]

The init-parameter `naruserve.urlPattern` accepts `/*`, `/` and `/api/*` (mapping the servlet accordingly) and any other value (`api/*`, `*.json`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-363]

The init-parameter `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds` is an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 and is the timeout of the `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` call that the container's destroy callback makes; any other value (`0`, `301`, `ten`, an empty string) makes context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the parameter and the value. [D-359; D-363; I-012]

The initializer instantiates the class named by `naruserve.configurer` through its public no-argument constructor and hands it a `RestApp.Builder` that already holds a `ServletAdapter`; a missing class, a class that does not implement `ServletConfigurer`, a class without a public no-argument constructor, a `configure` that throws and a `configure` that returns `null` each make context startup fail with a `ServletException` whose message names the class. [D-359; r4 W2-003]

The build adds the class-reference prefix `jakarta/servlet/` for `:NaruServe-servlet` to the `classRefPrefixes` closure of `build.gradle` as a separate `if (path == ':NaruServe-servlet')` branch, leaving the pinned `:NaruServe-api` prefix line of `BuildLayoutTest` unchanged, so the existing `checkClassReferences` task fails the build, naming `Class -> jakarta/servlet/...`, when a main class of `NaruServe-servlet` references it; a negative fixture proves the check fails, and `settings.gradle` includes no module for `jakarta.servlet`. [D-358; I-002]

records.requirement: The system shall provide in `NaruServe-servlet`, package `com.snoworca.naruserve.servlet`, the public final class `ServletAdapter` implementing `HttpAdapter`, the public `@FunctionalInterface ServletConfigurer` with `RestApp configure(RestApp.Builder builder) throws Exception`, and the public `NaruServeInitializer` implementing `javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, registered in `META-INF/services/javax.servlet.ServletContainerInitializer`, which reads the context init-parameters `naruserve.configurer`, `naruserve.urlPattern` and `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`; the module has no `jakarta.servlet` counterpart in v1.
records.rationale: Covers D-358, D-363 (container registration and class names), wave decisions Servlet adapter decisions (r1 W2-007), Who builds the app on the Servlet adapter (r4 W2-003) and Servlet SSE registration (r4 W2-005); answers Q-4. Measured (2026-10-20): `NaruServe-servlet/src/main` holds only `package-info.java`; `build.gradle` declares `javax.servlet:javax.servlet-api:3.1.0` and `javax.websocket:javax.websocket-api:1.1` `compileOnly` for the module; a built `RestApp` has no adapter setter and `RestApp.Builder` takes `httpAdapter`, `jsonCodec` and `logger` (`RestApp.java:226-267`). Decision (C-07): the names are `ServletAdapter`, `ServletConfigurer`, `NaruServeInitializer` and the package-private `NaruServeServlet`; the initializer is discovered through the Servlet 3.0 service file, so an application only sets the init-parameter; `naruserve.urlPattern` defaults to `/*` and accepts `/*`, `/` or `/prefix/*`; the servlet is named `naruserve` and registered with `asyncSupported=true` and no `MultipartConfig`. Decision (C-07): the container's destroy callback calls `app.shutdown(timeout, SECONDS)` because `RestApp` has only `shutdown(long, TimeUnit)`; the timeout is `naruserve.shutdownTimeoutSeconds`, an integer from 1 to 300 with default 10 (the value `docs/api/app.md` uses; a bound exists because no limit may default to unlimited, I-012). When `naruserve.configurer` is absent the initializer does nothing, because the jar may sit in `WEB-INF/lib` of an application that does not use NaruServe. Pitfall: `@HandlesTypes` is not used, so no classpath scan runs at container start. Pitfall: `jetty-servlet` alone does not run `ServletContainerInitializer`s; the tests use a Jetty `WebAppContext` with the annotation configuration so that the services file is discovered, and containers other than Jetty 9.4 are not exercised (recorded in `docs/api/servlet.md`). Rejected alternative: a `ServletContextListener` declared in `web.xml` or by `@WebListener`; it needs the application to list it and `@WebListener` needs annotation scanning, which a jar in `WEB-INF/lib` loses when `metadata-complete=true`.

records.title: Public WebSocket API: app.ws, WebSocketHandler, WebSocketSession, listeners and app.webSocket(Configurer<WebSocketOptions>)

acceptanceCriteria.text: `RestApp` declares `ws(String path, WebSocketHandler handler)` returning the same `RestApp`, and `com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketHandler` is a `@FunctionalInterface` with the single abstract method `void handle(Request req, WebSocketSession ws) throws Exception`; a Java test registers `app.ws("/ws/rooms/:room", (req, ws) -> ...)` and reflection confirms both signatures, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `ws(String,WebSocketHandler)->RestApp`. Decision: `ws` returns `RestApp` like `get`, and the callback interface is named `WebSocketHandler`. [D-294]

A path passed to `ws` follows the HTTP route pattern syntax and its registration-time validation: `app.ws("/a/:id", h)` registers and resolves `req.param("id")` in the handler, an invalid pattern throws the same exception type as `app.get` with that pattern, and `ws(null, h)` or `ws("/a", null)` throws `NullPointerException`. Decision: registration goes through the internal `Router.addWebSocket` path, which the internal `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute` hook already uses. [D-294]

`ws(...)` and `webSocket(...)` called after `listen()` throw `IllegalStateException` from the `NEW`-state guard of FR-APP-002 before the handler is recorded or the configurer runs, leaving routes and settings unchanged. [D-294; D-323] Decision: `requireConfigurable("ws")` or `requireConfigurable("webSocket")` runs first and the null checks after it, so the `IllegalStateException` wins over a null argument after `listen()`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-2]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketSession` declares `String id()`, `void sendText(String)`, `void sendBinary(byte[])`, `void sendJson(@Nullable Object)`, `void ping()`, `void close()`, `void close(int code, String reason)`, `boolean isOpen()`, `void onText(TextListener)`, `void onBinary(BinaryListener)`, `<T> void onJson(Class<T> type, JsonListener<T>)`, `void onClose(CloseListener)`, `void onError(ErrorListener)`, `void attribute(String key, @Nullable Object value)` and `<T> @Nullable T attribute(String key, Class<T> type)`, which a reflection test lists. Decision: `close()` equals `close(1000, "")`, and the attribute overloads follow the `Request.attribute` overload rule. [D-311]

The nested types `WebSocketSession.TextListener.onText(String)`, `BinaryListener.onBinary(byte[])`, `JsonListener<T>.onJson(@Nullable T value)`, `CloseListener.onClose(int code, String reason)` and `ErrorListener.onError(Throwable error)` are each annotated `@FunctionalInterface` and declare `throws Exception`, which a reflection test asserts; two listeners of one kind registered on one session both run, in registration order. [D-311]

`RestApp` declares `webSocket(Configurer<WebSocketOptions> configurer)` returning the same `RestApp`, and the public interface `com.snoworca.naruserve.WebSocketOptions` declares the fluent setters `allowedOrigins(String... origins)`, `maxMessageSize(int bytes)`, `sendQueueSize(int bytes)`, `pingInterval(long time, TimeUnit unit)` and `idleTimeout(long time, TimeUnit unit)`, each returning `WebSocketOptions`; a configurer setting all five is applied, which a test reads back through the internal settings, and the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `webSocket(Configurer)->RestApp`. Decision: the configurer runs on a copy that is swapped in only after it returned, so a throwing configurer leaves every earlier setting unchanged. [D-419; D-323; D-303]

An app that never calls `webSocket` uses no configured origin allowlist, `maxMessageSize` 1048576, `sendQueueSize` 1048576, `pingInterval` 30 s and `idleTimeout` 300 s; `allowedOrigins()` with no argument resets the allowlist to that default, and a second `allowedOrigins("https://b.example")` after `allowedOrigins("https://a.example")` leaves only `https://b.example` allowed, which a test asserts. Decision: ping interval default 30 s and idle timeout default 5 min; each `allowedOrigins` call replaces the allowlist (like the `origin` option of Express `cors`). [D-303; D-323; D-419] Decision: `allowedOrigins` with a null array or a null entry throws `NullPointerException` and keeps the previous list; otherwise it stores a defensive copy in the given order. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-5]

`maxMessageSize` accepts 1 to 16777216, `sendQueueSize` accepts 1 to 67108864, `pingInterval` accepts 1 s to 1 h and `idleTimeout` accepts 1 s to 24 h, all inclusive; `0`, a negative value or a value above the bound throws `IllegalArgumentException` whose message has the form `<setting> must be in 1..<max>: <value>` for a size (for example `maxMessageSize must be in 1..16777216: 0`) and `<setting> must be in 1 s..<max>: <time> <unit>` for a duration (for example `pingInterval must be in 1 s..1 h: 0 SECONDS`), a `null` unit or origin entry throws `NullPointerException`, and no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited: every setting has a bounded range and a finite default (I-012). [D-419; D-323] Decision: a duration is converted with `unit.toMillis` (saturating) and compared against 1000..3600000 ms or 1000..86400000 ms, so `999 MILLISECONDS` and `Long.MAX_VALUE DAYS` are refused with the caller's own time and unit in the message. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-2 SDS-AC-4]

Reflection finds no handshake-timeout setter and no pong-timeout setter on `WebSocketOptions` or `RestApp`. Decision: the handshake is bounded by the server-wide `headerTimeout` and `bodyReadTimeout`, and the pong timeout equals the ping interval. [residual: WebSocket handshake timeout (r5 W2-002)] [D-424]

A Kotlin test compiles and runs `app.ws("/ws") { req, ws -> ws.onText { m -> ws.sendText(m) }; ws.onClose { code, reason -> } }` and `app.webSocket { o -> o.maxMessageSize(1024).pingInterval(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS) }` as SAM lambdas without a DSL, and the returned `RestApp`, `WebSocketOptions` and `ws.id()` are non-platform types (`@NonNull`). [D-294; D-311; C-03; T11]

records.requirement: The system shall provide `RestApp ws(String path, WebSocketHandler handler)`, the `@FunctionalInterface` `WebSocketHandler` taking `(Request req, WebSocketSession ws)`, the `WebSocketSession` interface with its nested `@FunctionalInterface` listeners, and `RestApp webSocket(Configurer<WebSocketOptions> configurer)` with the settings `allowedOrigins`, `maxMessageSize`, `sendQueueSize`, `pingInterval` and `idleTimeout`, each bounded and defaulted as the acceptance criteria state.
records.rationale: Covers D-294, D-311, D-303 (API and default part), D-419 (WebSocket setting names), D-323 (configuration API part), D-317 (API part), wave decision Handler timing (W2-004, API part) and the C-07 choices of the authoring plan; T11/C-03 for Kotlin. Registration goes through the existing internal `Router.addWebSocket` path: `ws` registers through the internal `DefaultRestApp.webSocketRoute(String, RouteHandler)` hook, which keeps its signature so the verified FR-HTTP-008 AC-5 and AC-7 tests and the `TestApp.webSocketRoute` fixture stay unchanged (FR-WS-001 AC-7), so the pattern syntax and the freeze and conflict rules are the HTTP route rules of FR-ROUTE-003 and FR-ROUTE-015 (measured: `DefaultRestApp.java:828` records a `webSocketRoute` with `MethodSet.of(GET)` and `:859` calls `router.addWebSocket`). The configurer follows IR-APP-007 and IR-MULTIPART-001 (copy swapped in after it returned); range messages follow the existing forms `<name> must be in 1..<max>: <value>` (`DefaultServerOptions.java:23`) and `<name> must be in 1 ms..1 h: <time> <unit>` (`DefaultServerOptions.java:35`), with the 1 s lower bound for WebSocket durations. Pitfall: an unlimited value would contradict I-012, so no setting accepts a value meaning unlimited and every setting has a bounded range and a finite default. Decision: each `allowedOrigins` call replaces the allowlist (Express `cors` `origin` style), although TinyHttpd's own `allowedOrigins` appends; the core does the Origin check (FR-WS-003). No handshake-timeout setting exists (residual r5 W2-002: TinyHttpd at 46b973e has no upgrade deadline, so a setting would have no effect) and no pong-timeout setting exists (D-424: pong timeout equals the ping interval). Test to re-point: the RestApp signature set of `HttpApiSurfaceTest` gains `ws` and `webSocket` (AC-1, AC-6). Rejected alternative: `ws` returning a route builder like `route()`; reopen if per-route WebSocket middleware is requested. Rejected alternative: a listener interface with all callbacks (express-ws style `ws.on(...)`); Java SAM per event keeps Kotlin lambdas without a DSL. Express mapping: express-ws `app.ws(path, (ws, req) => ...)` with argument order reversed.

records.title: Add-only WebSocket SPI: WebSocketEndpoint, WebSocketChannel, WebSocketSettings and HttpExchange.webSocket

acceptanceCriteria.text: `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketEndpoint` declares `void onOpen(WebSocketChannel channel)`, `void onText(String text)`, `void onBinary(byte[] data)` and `void onClose(int code, String reason)`, which a reflection test lists; the core implements it and no adapter class implements it. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: none of the four callbacks declares a checked exception, and no class under `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` or the test fixtures implements the interface. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-4]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketChannel` declares `void sendText(String)`, `void sendBinary(byte[])`, `void ping(byte[] payload)`, `void close(int code, String reason)`, `void abort()` and `boolean isOpen()`, which a reflection test lists. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [wave decision: Ping (r2 W2-001)] Decision: `sendText`, `sendBinary` and `ping` declare `IOException`; `close`, `abort` and `isOpen` declare no checked exception. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-3]

`com.snoworca.naruserve.spi.WebSocketSettings` exposes the configured message limit in bytes and the ping interval, and the core builds it from the `WebSocketOptions` of IR-WS-001; a test reads back a non-default `maxMessageSize` 4096 and `pingInterval` 2 s from the settings passed to `webSocket`. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [D-419; D-423] Decision: `WebSocketSettings` is a final class with the public constructor `(int maxMessageBytes, long pingIntervalMillis)` and, besides it, only the getters `maxMessageBytes(): int` and `pingIntervalMillis(): long`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-6]

`HttpExchange` declares `default void webSocket(WebSocketSettings settings, WebSocketEndpoint endpoint) throws IOException`, and calling it on an exchange class that does not override it throws `UnsupportedOperationException`; the method returns only after the connection has closed. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: the message is `webSocket is not supported by this adapter` and the exchange is not touched. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-5]

A signature comparison test finds every method of every type of `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` present at the wave 6 close (`9ce5cc4`; the SPI is unchanged since `40b9665`), namely `AppFactory`, `ErrorRenderer`, `ExchangeHandler`, `HttpAdapter`, `HttpExchange`, `JsonCodec`, `ServerSettings`, `StreamDrain` and `UpgradeHandler`, unchanged, with `webSocket` the only added `HttpExchange` method and `attach(OutputStream)` the only added `StreamDrain` method (the SSE hand-over of IR-HTTP-007 AC-4). Deviation (recorded): D-106 reads "without changing the SPI"; wave 7 adds types and `default` methods only, read as "without breaking the SPI"; W2-001's "one default method" becomes two with `StreamDrain.attach`, still add-only. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] [committee decision: StreamDrain.attach (wave-7 feasibility B-1)]

When `webSocket` refuses a handshake before `101` it throws a NaruServe `HttpException` carrying the status and headers of the rejection and leaves the exchange unstarted, so the dispatcher's error path then calls `commit(...)` on that exchange without an `IllegalStateException` and the client receives the rejection status; the exchange is marked started only once `101` has been written. [wave decision: Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002)]

No class under `com.snoworca.naruserve` in `NaruServe-api` or `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` parses or writes WebSocket frames: a source scan finds no frame-opcode or masking-key handling, and the TinyHttpd upgrade class delegates framing to `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd.websocket`. [D-302] Decision: the scan reads every `.java` file under `NaruServe-api/src/main` and `NaruServe-tinyhttpd/src/main` and fails on the words `opcode` or `masking` in any case. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-10]

The test-fixture `InMemoryHttpAdapter` exchange overrides `webSocket`, records the settings and endpoint, calls `onOpen` with an in-memory `WebSocketChannel` that records sent text, binary, ping and close calls, and lets a test inject text, binary and close events; a core test uses it to open a session and receive a recorded `sendText`. [wave decision: WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001)] Decision: the in-memory exchange marks itself started with status `101`, calls `onOpen` on its worker thread, delivers queued peer events from that thread in order and returns only after `onClose` ran. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-7] Decision: `close(code, reason)` is recorded and echoed by the peer so `onClose` gets `(code, reason)`; `abort()` sets aborted and delivers `onClose(1006, "")`. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-7-1 SDS-AC-8]

records.requirement: The system shall extend the `com.snoworca.naruserve.spi` package for WebSocket only by adding the types `WebSocketEndpoint`, `WebSocketChannel` and `WebSocketSettings` and the `default` method `HttpExchange.webSocket(WebSocketSettings, WebSocketEndpoint)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` unless an adapter overrides it, beside which wave 7 adds only the SSE `default` method `StreamDrain.attach(OutputStream)` of IR-HTTP-007, so that an adapter supplies RFC 6455 framing and the core owns every WebSocket callback without any existing SPI signature changing.
records.rationale:
Covers wave decision WebSocket upgrade SPI (W2-001; D-106, D-302, D-429, D-435, D-444, D-419, D-423), Ping (r2 W2-001; D-309, D-311), Start state on a refused handshake (r2 W2-002, SPI part) and D-302 (no NaruServe frame codec). Deviation note: D-106 says the upgrade extension point works "without changing the SPI"; the wave reads it as "without breaking it" (add-only types and one default method), which `docs/api` records; IR-HTTP-007 (the successor of IR-HTTP-004 in the HTTP scope) restates the SPI-surface AC accordingly. Measured: `spi/HttpExchange.java:85` declares `upgrade(List<Map.Entry<String,String>>, UpgradeHandler)` and `:89` `eventStream(...)`; the existing raw `upgrade` stays for raw upgrades and keeps its signature. Pitfall: putting TinyHttpd's `WebSocket`/`WebSocketListener` types on the SPI would leak an engine type into the core (CON constraints of wave 1); rejected. Rejected alternative: driving WebSocket through the raw `UpgradeHandler` and a NaruServe frame codec; contradicts D-302, reopen never in v1. The in-memory test adapter implements `webSocket` so core-level tests of FR-WS-001, FR-WS-003, FR-WS-006, FR-WS-007 and FR-WS-009 run without sockets.
- [2026-10-20] Correction (feasibility F-03/F-05): the SPI now gains two default methods, HttpExchange.webSocket and StreamDrain.attach (committee decision B-1), replacing the earlier "one default method" wording. AC-5's signature test names StreamDrain.attach, which IR-HTTP-007 AC-4 owns; IR-HTTP-007 depends_on this requirement, so the two are built and verified together as one group (no reverse edge, to keep the graph acyclic).

records.title: Wave 5 cookie decisions recorded in docs/api and their markers removed

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/cookie.md` states that `getMaxAge()` defaults to `-1`, that every negative value omits `Max-Age` (a session cookie), that `0` deletes and that a positive value is seconds, with its reason (the Servlet `Cookie` model), and the `getMaxAge()` row has no (미확정) marker. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that v1 writes no `Expires` attribute (lifetimes use `Max-Age`) and has no signed cookies (an app signs values itself, for example with an HMAC in middleware), each with its reason, and the `Expires` marker line is gone. [D-208; I-013]

`docs/api/cookie.md` states that NaruServe neither encodes nor decodes cookie values, unlike Express's `res.cookie`, that an app encodes other characters itself (for example with `URLEncoder`), that request cookies with an invalid name or without `=` are skipped instead of failing the request, and that `res.addCookie` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for an invalid name or value. [wave decision: Request cookies are parsed leniently; D-205]
The `cookie-parser` row of `docs/api/express-migration.md` states that signed cookies and automatic value encoding are not provided in v1 instead of carrying a (미확정) marker. [D-208]

The Java blocks of `docs/api/cookie.md` are compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry whose reason is `Cookie`, `req.cookie`, `req.getCookies` or `res.addCookie`, and a docs test fails when `docs/api/cookie.md` contains a (미확정) marker. [I-008; I-009]

records.title: Wave 5 engine and server-setting decisions recorded in docs/api with defaults checked against the code

acceptanceCriteria.text: `docs/api/app.md` documents `app.server(options -> ...)` with every setter of IR-ENGINE-001 AC-2, a LAN example `options.bindAddress("0.0.0.0").allowedHosts("myphone.local")` in Java and Kotlin, `app.trustProxy(true)`, that `ServerHandle.address()` reports the address actually bound (`127.0.0.1` by default), and that one non-daemon keeper thread keeps the JVM alive after `main` returns while TinyHttpd's threads stay daemon; the LAN binding marker line is gone and no sentence says the server threads are non-daemon. [D-225; D-212; D-167; wave decision: Thread wording; wave decision: The default bind address is IPv4 `127.0.0.1`]

`docs/api/defaults.md` lists header size 16 KiB (`431`, `maxHeaderSize`), request-line length 8190 bytes (`414`, `maxRequestLineLength`, renamed from URL length), the per-line header limit of `inputBufferBytes - 2` (8190 by default, `431`, unchanged by `maxHeaderSize`), header count 100, header timeout 10 s, body-read timeout 30 s, write timeout 30 s, minimum body rate 240 B/s (`408`), the connection limits (workers 64, SSE streams 128, connections 512, derived wait queue 320, upgraded connections 128, per address 256) and the maximum of every setting; it states that no setting accepts an unlimited value, drops the sentence that `431`/`414` are not final, and the markers on these rows and on the unlimited-value question are gone. [D-225; D-437; residual: Upper bounds on size settings; I-012]

`docs/api/defaults.md` states that the bind default is `127.0.0.1`, that `bindAddress("0.0.0.0")` always logs a security warning and the app must add authentication itself, names `app.trustProxy(true)` for `X-Forwarded-*`, lists the D-400 transport-level rejections (`400`, `408`, `414`, `417`, `431`, `501`, `505` and the socket-level `503`) as plain-text answers that bypass `onError`, the error JSON and the access log, records the `421` Host rejection with the standard error body, and states that the TinyHttpd adapter has no TLS listener in v1; the binding and proxy markers are gone. [D-213; D-400; D-418; D-433; wave decision: The LAN warning is unconditional]

`docs/api/request.md` names `app.trustProxy(true)` in its proxy paragraph without a marker, and `docs/api/express-migration.md` maps `app.set('trust proxy', ...)` to `app.trustProxy(true)` and names `bindAddress("0.0.0.0")` in its LAN sentence, both without markers. [D-225; D-080]

`docs/api/README.md`, `docs/api/app.md` and `docs/api/json.md` name the bootstrap module `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe` and the Gson module `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe-gson` exactly as CON-BUILD-002 and CON-BUILD-005 fixed them, which a docs test checks. [D-230]

A test parses the defaults of AC-2, the JSON size and depth rows of `docs/api/defaults.md` and compares them with the defaults of `ServerOptions`, `app.jsonLimit` and `GsonJsonCodec`, failing on any difference; the Java blocks that call `server`, `trustProxy` or `ServerOptions` are compiled by the root docs compile test of OPS-HTTP-004 with no skip entry naming them. [I-011; I-009]

The other (미확정) markers that these decisions settle are removed in the same change: the sentence of `docs/api/defaults.md` on socket read/write timeouts, header count, wait queue and SSE/WebSocket connection limits names `headerTimeout`, `bodyReadTimeout`, `writeTimeout`, `maxHeaderCount`, the derived queue, `maxSseStreams` and `maxUpgradedConnections`; `docs/api/sse.md` names `maxSseStreams` for the concurrent SSE connection limit; the `docs/api/websocket.md` limits row names `maxUpgradedConnections` for the connection count while idle timeout, ping interval and handshake timeout keep their wave 7 marker; and the trust-proxy and LAN-binding bullet leaves the undecided list of `docs/api/express-migration.md`. [D-225; D-404; I-008; I-013]

records.rationale: Covers D-381, I-018, I-019, I-020, D-347 (listed as a post-v1 row), T10, T12, T47, T26, T49 and T50, and wave decisions Status of the removed Android tests (r1 W1-001), Status literal (r2 W2-005) and Release scan and result rows (r3 W2-005). Frozen: D-381 names three statuses; Deviation (recorded): the fourth literal `out-of-v1-scope` is added and I-018 is narrowed for the five Android lines by the user's decision, which also supersedes the header wording "device parts of T26 and T49 recorded as manual checks" and the Q-3 manual device run; I-020 does not apply to them because they are not manual-pending, and no requirement may call them verified. Decision: `automated` means an automated test of `./gradlew build` covers it (evidence `path#method`), `manual-pending` a recorded manual check not yet run (evidence a checklist item), `verified` a manual check run with recorded evidence; the document and its test use the literal only, never the prose "out of v1 scope (user decision)". Measured: `object.md:1015-1082` holds the T-table and the platform matrix; T10, T12 and T47 read "Gson 2.14.0 API21 실기기", "R8 최적화 on" and "Android Service 메인스레드 IO 금지". Pitfall: a result document that lists a test as `automated` without a method link rots silently; the docs test resolves each link to an existing file and method. Rejected alternative: marking the Android tests `manual-pending` with a checklist; the user removed device verification from v1.

records.requirement: The release documentation `docs/release/release-notes.md` shall contain the platform matrix of `object.md` §17.1 with a status per row: the JVM Java 8 row `pending` when no Java 8 runtime ran the suite, citing `--release 8` and the animal-sniffer `android-api-level-21` check as compile-time evidence; the Android 5.0, latest Android and Kotlin Android rows `out-of-v1-scope`; and the Servlet row reporting HTTP, multipart, async and SSE tested on an embedded Servlet 3.1 container and WebSocket not supported.
records.rationale: Covers D-382 and the Platform matrix of object.md §17.1, and wave decisions Release documentation statement (r1 W1-005). Measured (2026-10-20): the build machine has one JDK, OpenJDK 17.0.20 (`java -version`; `/usr/libexec/java_home -V` finds no other), so no Java 8 runtime ran the suite; the bytecode target is Java 8 by `options.release = 8` (CON-BUILD-004). Decision: the Java 8 row status is `pending` until a Java 8 run is recorded, then `verified` with that record as evidence; meanwhile the row cites the two compile-time checks and the command that produced them. The matrix uses the four literals of OPS-REL-003 (`automated`, `manual-pending`, `verified`, `out-of-v1-scope`) plus `pending` for a row whose run has not happened. Pitfall: `--release 8` proves the API surface and bytecode level, not runtime behaviour on a Java 8 JVM (for example Java 8 canonical path caching, FR-STATIC-006); the row must say so. Rejected alternative: marking the row `verified` because the bytecode is Java 8; D-382 forbids it.

records.title: How consumers obtain TinyHttpd: includeBuild of the checkout, since this repository does not publish it

acceptanceCriteria.text: `README.md` and `docs/release/release-notes.md` each contain the statement that TinyHttpd is not published by this repository, the `includeBuild` snippet for a consumer `settings.gradle`, the two TinyHttpd coordinates with `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`, and the verified commit `46b973e`, which a docs test asserts. [D-383; r4 W2-002]

A recorded consumer run shows that a Gradle build in a temporary directory that declares `mavenLocal()`, depends on `com.snoworca.naruserve:NaruServe-tinyhttpd:0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and includes the TinyHttpd checkout through `includeBuild` resolves the runtime classpath of the dependency with the TinyHttpd projects, and that the same build without the `includeBuild` fails with an unresolved `tinyhttpd-core`; the run's command, date and results are in the release notes. [D-383]
The documents do not say that TinyHttpd can be taken from `mavenLocal` or a remote repository, and a docs test fails on the phrase "publish it to mavenLocal". [D-383; r4 W2-002]

records.requirement: The README and the release documentation shall state that this repository does not publish TinyHttpd, that Gradle `includeBuild` of the TinyHttpd checkout is the one verified way to obtain it, and that the `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` POM dependency on `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd:tinyhttpd-core` and `tinyhttpd-websocket` resolves only when an artifact with those coordinates is available from the consumer's own build of TinyHttpd.
records.rationale: Covers D-383 and wave decisions TinyHttpd for consumers (r4 W2-002, which supersedes "publish it to mavenLocal themselves" of the Publishing decision). Measured (2026-10-20): TinyHttpd's `build.gradle` sets group `com.snoworca.tinyhttpd` and version `0.1.0-SNAPSHOT` and has no publishing configuration; the checkout is read-only here (I-006, CON-BUILD-010); `settings.gradle` does `includeBuild(tinyHttpdDir)` and warns when the checkout HEAD differs from the verified commit `46b973e` (the checkout was at `38051b6` on this date). Decision: the documented snippet is `includeBuild('/path/to/TinyHttpd')` in the consumer's `settings.gradle`, which substitutes the TinyHttpd coordinates of the POM; the doc states the verified commit. Pitfall: a consumer who depends on `NaruServe-tinyhttpd` from `mavenLocal()` without the included build fails to resolve TinyHttpd; the doc says so, naming the coordinates. Rejected alternative: publishing TinyHttpd to `mavenLocal` from here; the checkout is read-only and has no publishing configuration.

records.title: Long-connection load bounds: 100+ WebSocket and SSE connections within the thread total and a heap bound, documented thread and stack figures, and the low-end Android follow-up

acceptanceCriteria.text: A JVM test (T26) opens 60 WebSocket sessions and 60 SSE streams from `127.0.0.1` under the default limits, each receives one message or event within 5 s, and while all 120 are open the count of live threads belonging to the app is at most 452 and the used heap after `System.gc()` grew by less than 64 MiB from the value before the connections opened. Decision: the heap bound is 64 MiB. Decision: the app's threads are counted by name, as the threads whose names start with `naruserve-` plus `tinyhttpd-acceptor-<port>` and `tinyhttpd-watchdog`, and the test runs in an isolated test JVM fork that starts no other app, because TinyHttpd's `tinyhttpd-watchdog` name carries no port. [D-346; T26]

A test computes the thread total from the defaults as `maxWorkers + maxSseStreams` (192) + `maxUpgradedConnections` read threads (128) + `maxUpgradedConnections` sender threads (128) + 1 idle scheduler + TinyHttpd acceptor + watchdog + `naruserve-keeper` and asserts 452, and asserts that the T26 thread bound constant equals it. Frozen: D-416 bounds the threads of one app to 451. Deviation (recorded): the total is 452 because the non-daemon `naruserve-keeper` thread runs from bind to stop. [D-416; wave decision: Thread total (W2-006); wave decision: Thread total (r2 W1-001)]

The WebSocket sender threads and the idle scheduler thread are created with a requested stack size of 262144 bytes, which a test reads through an internal hook of each thread factory that reports the stack size the factory passed to the `Thread` constructor, because a live thread does not expose its requested stack size, and `docs/api/defaults.md` states for API 21 devices the thread total 452 and that 449 request-path threads request 112.25 MiB of stack, which a docs test reads. [D-416]

`docs/api/defaults.md` has a section headed `저사양 Android 튜닝(수동 후속 작업)` stating that device-specific tuning of `maxSseStreams`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and the WebSocket and SSE `sendQueueSize` on a low-end Android 5.0 device is a manual follow-up of the release test, not an automated result, and a docs test finds that heading and the names `maxSseStreams`, `maxUpgradedConnections` and `sendQueueSize` in that section. Manual follow-up recorded. [D-347]

records.requirement: The system shall hold at least 100 concurrent WebSocket and SSE connections from the loopback address under the default limits with the app's thread count at most 452 and its heap growth below the bound written in the test, document the thread total and the stack figure of the default limits for API 21 devices, and record device-specific tuning of long-connection limits for low-end Android as a manual follow-up of the release test in a section of `docs/api/defaults.md`.
records.rationale:
Covers D-346 (T26), D-416, D-347, wave decision Thread total (W2-006) and its round-2 reading (r2 W1-001). Frozen D-416 bounds the threads of one app to 451: 192 TinyHttpd request workers (64 HTTP plus 128 SSE), 128 WebSocket read threads kept by upgraded connections, 128 WebSocket sender threads, one NaruServe idle-timeout scheduler thread, and TinyHttpd's acceptor and watchdog threads. Deviation (recorded): the bounded total is 452, because the wave 5 non-daemon `naruserve-keeper` thread (FR-ENGINE-006; `tinyhttpd/KeeperThread.java:11-35`) runs from bind to stop; the T26 bound and `docs/api/defaults.md` use 452 (W2-006, r2 W1-001). The stack figure is unchanged: 449 request-path threads (192 + 128 + 128 + 1) request 256 KiB each = 112.25 MiB, while the acceptor, watchdog and keeper use the platform default stack and sit outside that budget. Measured: `ServerOptions.java:41-54` defaults `maxWorkers` 64, `maxSseStreams` 128, `maxUpgradedConnections` 128 (defaults.md rows), and `TinyHttpdAdapter.java:105-116` sizes the worker pool `maxWorkers + maxSseStreams`. Decision: the T26 heap bound is 64 MiB of used-heap growth after `System.gc()` with 120 open connections, which is far below 120 full 1 MiB send queues because queues allocate only what is queued and T26 queues one message per connection. Pitfall: counting every JVM thread would include the test's own client threads; the test counts the app's threads by name prefix and by the TinyHttpd thread group. D-347 cannot be automated on a JVM; its AC is a recorded manual follow-up. Rejected alternative: a fixed WebSocket sender pool of 16 threads; D-320 forbids it (20 stalled sessions).
- [2026-10-20] Correction: the 64 MiB heap bound is far below 120 full 1 MiB send queues because queues allocate only what is queued, and T26 queues one message per connection. D-347 is recorded in the `저사양 Android 튜닝(수동 후속 작업)` section of `docs/api/defaults.md` (AC-4), a path the wave 7 docs create, so a docs test can find it.
- [2026-10-20] Correction (wave-7 feasibility): the "TinyHttpd thread group" counting above is replaced by name-based counting (AC-1): threads named `naruserve-*` (workers `naruserve-<port>-worker-<n>`, keeper, `naruserve-<port>-ws-sender-<n>`, `naruserve-<port>-ws-idle`) plus `tinyhttpd-acceptor-<port>` and `tinyhttpd-watchdog`, in an isolated test JVM fork, since the watchdog name has no port. AC-3 reads the requested stack size through an internal thread-factory hook.

records.title: Access log never records secrets and escapes control characters

acceptanceCriteria.text: A request `POST /login?token=qzv&password=pwz` with `Authorization: Bearer s3cr3t`, `Cookie: sid=c00k1e` and body `password=pwq2` whose handler answers `token-xyz` produces a line that contains none of `qzv`, `pwz`, `s3cr3t`, `c00k1e`, `pwq2`, `token-xyz` or `?`. [D-175; T39] Decision: the line is built only from the method token, the raw path without the query, the status, the duration and byte counts and the request id. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-11]

A raw path containing `%0d%0a` is logged with the raw percent-encoded form, and an unrecognised method token or path containing a CR, LF, TAB, `0x01`, `0x7F` or `0x85` character is logged with `\r`, `\n`, `\t` and `\u0001`, `\u007f`, `\u0085`, and `\` as `\\`, so every access log record is one line. [D-176; T39] Decision: control characters U+0000–U+001F, U+007F and U+0080–U+009F are escaped this way. Decision: other escaped characters are written as `\u` plus four lowercase hex digits, and percent-encoded text stays raw. [SDS 2026-10-19.naruserve.naruserve-v1-wave-4-8 SDS-AC-12]
The access log line holds no header value at all. [D-175]
